docs.title: FLEET Mira documentation
docs.text:
For software developers and authorised integration partners, see the private German/English developer handbook. Repository access is required; internal and external chapters both remain private.

FLEET Mira brings device operations, compliant tachograph archiving, driver-card and vehicle-unit analysis, fleet records, driving-licence checks, deadlines, finance documents and verified cloud backup into one Windows application.

docs.title: Download – version 1.1.0-beta9
docs.text:
Current build: FLEET Mira 1.1.0-beta9, dated 4 November 2026, for Windows x64. New setup candidates are built locally; public publication is a separate step. The releases page lists downloads actually published.

Download Basic/Pro setup

Download Enterprise application setup

Download Enterprise PostgreSQL Server setup

Basic/Pro is restricted to local Windows 10/11 console sessions and local SQLite storage. Enterprise uses PostgreSQL and supports Windows Server and terminal-server environments. Follow the Enterprise installation guide before using either Enterprise setup.

Basic/Pro checksums · Enterprise checksums · Release notes and all files

Unsigned beta release

The setups are not yet code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may display a warning. Enterprise background work runs in the standalone FleetMiraWorker Windows service; clients do not start an integrated worker. Microsoft Entra ID SSO is Beta and has not yet been validated end to end with a real customer tenant. A local emergency administrator must remain available.

Figure: FLEET Mira start dashboard with anonymised demonstration data.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
FLEET Mira combines compliant tachograph-data processes, fleet management, cost control and traceable compliance workflows in one central application. Its key capabilities include:

  • Tachograph-data archiving and analysis
    • automated recursive import of C/M files from USB removable drives (Pro 💎)
    • day and week charts for personnel and vehicles
    • interactive maps for position data
    • technical infringement evaluation under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006
    • cryptographic signature verification for driver cards and vehicle units
    • audit trail for EU and German FPersV procedures
    • support for current Smart Tachograph 2 data:
      • border crossings
      • loading and unloading operations
      • load type
      • authenticated GNSS positions
      • Generation 2 Version 2 files
      • 56-day data structures of new driver cards
  • Fleet Management
    • RFID-assisted driving-licence checks
    • personnel due-date management, including driver cards, professional-driver qualification and ADR
    • vehicle due-date management, including tachograph calibration, statutory inspections and service
    • cost controlling, KPIs and TCO (Total Cost of Ownership)
      • fixed operating costs such as insurance and tax
      • variable operating costs such as maintenance and repairs
    • XRechnung and e-invoice import with audit-ready original-document storage
    • reporting:
      • cost per vehicle
      • cost per kilometre
      • fixed and variable costs
      • time and period comparisons
    • audit trail for GoBD-compliant procedures
  • Users and roles with granular permissions and optional two-factor authentication (2FA)
  • Multilingual and regional formatting
    • Languages: Deutsch, English, Français, Italiano, Español, Português, Polski, Română, Nederlands, Dansk, Čeština, Magyar, Slovenščina, Hrvatski, Suomi, Norsk bokmål, Svenska, Latviešu, Lietuvių, Eesti, Slovenčina, Български, Ελληνικά, Gaeilge and Malti
    • Regions: Germany (de-DE), Austria (de-AT), Switzerland (de-CH), United Kingdom (en-GB), United States (en-US), France (fr-FR), Italy (it-IT), Spain (es-ES), Portugal (pt-PT), Poland (pl-PL), Romania (ro-RO), Netherlands (nl-NL), Denmark (da-DK), Czechia (cs-CZ), Hungary (hu-HU), Slovenia (sl-SI), Croatia (hr-HR), Finland (fi-FI), Norway (nb-NO), Sweden (sv-SE), Latvia (lv-LV), Lithuania (lt-LT), Estonia (et-EE), Slovakia (sk-SK), Bulgaria (bg-BG) Greece (el-GR), Ireland (ga-IE) and Malta (mt-MT)
  • Manual complete backup for Basic and Pro as a ZIP64 file or directory on local/UNC destinations, plus optional automatic Pro backup to filesystem, WebDAV or Google Drive targets
  • Guided data-root relocation with complete read-back and hash verification in every edition
  • Application-wide auditing with one central, filterable audit log
  • GPS-server.net telematics for Pro and Enterprise with object assignment, position history, maps, events and qualified daily odometer readings; see the integration guide
  • Traffic-offence management for Pro and Enterprise with document-specific deadlines, historical driver evidence and review-only response channels; see the user guide
  • Complete compliance history for imports, checks, assignments, changes and exports
  • GDPR-compliant data processing through role-based access, protected credentials and traceable procedures

docs.title: Key principles
docs.text:
• Original C and M files remain byte-for-byte traceable through hashes and the immutable local archive.
  • Signature results are stored per signed section; invalid or unverifiable files are quarantined without being deleted.
  • Business changes and automatic imports are recorded in the global audit log.
  • Tachograph source data remains stored unchanged in UTC. Display and calculations use UTC by default; when Use local time for activities and calculations is enabled, display, day/week boundaries and compliance evaluations use the time zone selected under System → Settings. Region settings independently affect formatting only.
  • Optional backup is one-way from the local primary archives to one configured target.
  • Locally verified financial originals can be verified and booked independently of backup status.
  • UI layout, language and region are stored per user.

docs.title: Product and legacy names
docs.text: FLEET Mira is the visible product name. Technical identifiers such as DLTNGDownloadTool.spec, database tables, API paths, existing configuration keys and the backup prefix DLTNG/<installation-id>/... remain unchanged for compatibility. They must not be renamed in an existing installation.

docs.title: Documentation status
docs.text:
The documentation follows the current application menus and implemented services. Screenshots use a reproducible, isolated demonstration profile; they contain no production DDD files, credentials, URLs or personal records.

The separate Connector Framework section contains the extension architecture explicitly marked as a target concept: developer handbook, customer concept, product flyer and reviewed overview illustration. These concept pages do not describe a released framework feature.

docs.title: Administrator and integrator guide
docs.text:
All public machine APIs require user-bound credentials and current permissions. The webhook requires an API bearer in addition to its connection token. The driver portal explicitly retains its case-specific invitation link without a user account. Mobile upload responses include vehicle/deadline details only with separate read permissions. Use interactive DLTNGDownloadTool.exe --api-admin administration to issue credentials once or revoke them. The private developer handbook contains the complete endpoint and scope list under “Unified API access”.

The optional device REST API now uses its own verified credentials and customer grants; the factory enables no network service.

docs.title: 1. Deployment model
docs.text:
FLEET Mira Basic/Pro is a locally installed Windows 10/11 desktop application with background schedulers. Setup and runtime block Windows Server, RDP, Citrix and other terminal sessions. The application directory contains Python modules or the PyInstaller build, static assets and translations. Mutable data is referenced by config.json and normally includes:

Item Default/role SQLite database state/archive.db; fixed local drive only, never UNC, mapped network or removable storage Tachograph archive compressed .ddd.gz objects below the configured archive root Logs logs/app.log, REST logs and native_crash.log Configuration config.json; paths, sources, tasks and service defaults UI profile SQLite per-user JSON plus machine-local QSettings geometry

Under Administration → Settings, FLEET Mira displays the active data root and the fully resolved log, SQLite, DDD archive, document archive and financial archive paths. These paths are read-only in Basic, Pro and Enterprise until a controlled relocation wizard can move data, database references and permissions as one operation. Raw configuration cannot bypass this restriction. Enterprise marks the SQLite path as unused because that edition uses PostgreSQL.

The Basic and Pro SQLite location is canonicalised and checked at startup. Mapped drives and reparse paths targeting network storage are rejected even when they appear to use a local drive letter. A blocked environment exposes only the rescue dialog for a verified local SQLite copy. Do not edit or move the data root manually. Grant write access only to the relevant application identity.

docs.title: Initial deployment
docs.text:
1. Deploy the build and the supplied empty deployment database.
  2. Review archive, database and log paths before importing data.
  3. Start FLEET Mira and sign in with admin / admin.
  4. Change the password to at least 12 characters.
  5. Create named users and test role restrictions.
  6. Configure sources/tasks, SMTP and backup in that order.
  7. Execute and document backup/restore and terminal-retention tests.

docs.title: 2. Users, roles and permissions
docs.text:
Passwords use Argon2id. Five failed attempts lock an account for 15 minutes. The last active administrator cannot be deactivated.

Figure: User, role, language and account administration.

Role Typical scope ADMIN complete administration, finance booking, restore and retention SUPPORT device/source/task operations, archive troubleshooting, read-only fleet/finance OPERATOR operational imports, fleet maintenance, licence checks, finance workflows AUDITOR read/report/export without business changes

The UI disables unauthorised actions, while repositories/services call PermissionService.require(...) again. Do not treat hidden/disabled controls as the security boundary.

Local administrator recovery is available with --reset-admin-password. It requires Windows administrator rights, resets only the initial admin credential to admin, unlocks the account, enables its local sign-in method and forces a new password. The password itself is never audited. At least this local emergency account must remain available. SSO setup is described below.

Failed sign-ins display a translated inline message from the first attempt. Dynamic status survives showing the label and repeated runtime translation; the password field is cleared and retains focus. This behavior is shared by local and central Enterprise sign-in.

docs.title: Single sign-on with Microsoft Entra ID and Google
docs.text:
Microsoft Entra ID SSO: Beta – untested

The Microsoft Entra integration has not yet been validated end-to-end in production with a real customer tenant. Use it only in pilot and test environments until customer-specific acceptance is complete. A tested local emergency administrator must remain available; do not disable local sign-in for an Entra user until WAM, browser fallback, MFA and Conditional Access have all been tested successfully. This beta notice does not apply to Google SSO.

FLEET Mira supports tenant-bound Entra work or school accounts and individually approved Google accounts. Windows domain accounts that are hybrid-connected to Entra can use the Windows Account Manager (WAM) for single sign-on. Pure AD DS without Entra and personal Microsoft accounts are not supported. Roles and permissions are assigned only in FLEET Mira; identity-provider groups or roles are never imported.

Prerequisites:

  • FLEET Mira administrator with settings.manage for providers and users.manage for assignments;
  • customer-owned Entra app registration; the Google vendor client is already included in FLEET Mira;
  • Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2019 or later for WAM; otherwise the system-browser fallback is used;
  • outbound HTTPS access to Microsoft or Google sign-in endpoints;
  • loopback access to 127.0.0.1/localhost for the browser callback;
  • one tested local administrator account for emergency access.

docs.title: Register Microsoft Entra ID – Beta
docs.text:
1. Open App registrations > New registration in the Entra admin centre.
  2. Enter a unique name and select Accounts in this organizational directory only.
  3. Open Authentication > Add a platform and select Mobile and desktop applications.
  4. Register http://localhost and ms-appx-web://Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin/<CLIENT_ID> as redirect URIs, replacing <CLIENT_ID> with the Application (client) ID.
  5. Enable Allow public client flows. Do not create a client secret: FLEET Mira is a public desktop client.
  6. Retain only the OIDC baseline permissions and delegated User.Read required by MSAL. Do not add mail, file or directory permissions.
  7. Copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID.
  8. In FLEET Mira, open Administration > Single sign-on, enter both IDs, run Test Microsoft sign-in, and only then select Enabled and save.

WAM is attempted first and supports Windows Hello, MFA and Conditional Access. If the broker is unavailable, MSAL opens the system browser with Authorization Code and PKCE. The immutable link key is (tid, oid); UPN and email are used only as the initial assignment hint.

These Entra steps describe the intended setup path but are not yet a production-validated reference configuration. Record the tenant, client ID, redirects, consent and Conditional Access policies, and all pilot results in the customer-specific acceptance record.

docs.title: Enable the central Google sign-in
docs.text:
Google requires no customer-side Cloud Console configuration. FLEET Mira contains a vendor-operated desktop OAuth client for personal Google and Google Workspace accounts.

  1. Open Administration > Single sign-on.
  2. In the Google section, verify that the application is FLEET Mira and the diagnostic reads The integrated Google vendor client is ready.
  3. Select Test Google sign-in. The system browser opens the central FLEET Mira consent dialog; Google may request consent for the basic profile and email on first use.
  4. After a successful test, select Enabled and choose Save SSO settings.
  5. Under Administration > Users, pre-assign the Google email addresses of permitted users. No further Google credentials are required.

If the integrated configuration is missing or damaged, the enable control remains unavailable and the diagnostic identifies a faulty software build. Contact the FLEET Mira vendor in this case; do not import or configure a customer OAuth client.

The browser callback binds only to 127.0.0.1 on a random free port. FLEET Mira uses Authorization Code with PKCE and validates signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce and email_verified. The durable key is (iss, sub); the email address is only used for initial assignment and may change afterwards. Google SSO stores no refresh tokens and does not reuse credentials, tokens or scopes from Google Drive backup. Scopes remain limited to openid, email and profile.

Figure: Entra configuration in untested beta status and the activatable, regularly supported Google vendor client.

docs.title: Assign users and control local sign-in
docs.text:
1. Open Administration > Users and create or edit a user.
  2. Set the local role, language, region and account status.
  3. Enter the expected Microsoft UPN under Microsoft UPN or verified Google address under Google email.
  4. Clear Local sign-in for an SSO-only account. A new SSO-only user does not require a temporary password.
  5. On the first successful provider sign-in, FLEET Mira atomically binds the immutable provider ID to exactly that user. Status changes from PENDING to LINKED.
  6. After the pilot sign-in, verify the link, local role and audit events.

Unknown identities are never provisioned automatically. Select Unlink SSO identity to relink an account; the approval returns to PENDING and the next matching provider sign-in binds it again. To remove the assignment completely, then clear the expected UPN/email in the user dialog. A disabled user cannot sign in locally or through SSO. The final local administrator cannot be converted to SSO-only.

Figure: Local sign-in, pre-approved SSO accounts and link status.

docs.title: Operations, offboarding and incidents
docs.text:
• Signing out of the app ends only the local session; Windows, Microsoft and Google sessions remain active.
  • During provider or network outages, only users with local sign-in enabled have a fallback.
  • Microsoft Entra remains beta until WAM, browser fallback, MFA and Conditional Access have been tested and documented for the customer; no user should depend exclusively on Entra before then.
  • For offboarding, disable the local user first, then block the provider account/consent and unlink the identity with an audit trail.
  • Customer administrators rotate the Entra client as for initial setup. Only the vendor rotates the central Google client through a new FLEET Mira build; existing (iss, sub) links remain and must be verified with pilot accounts.
  • ID, access and refresh tokens and complete claims must never appear in the database, audit or logs.
  • Regularly review SSO_LOGIN_*, SSO_IDENTITY_* and SSO_PROVIDER_CONFIG_UPDATED together with provider sign-in logs.
Symptom Check and action Entra beta not yet accepted Keep local sign-in enabled and document the complete pilot flow with WAM, browser fallback, MFA and Conditional Access in a real customer tenant. Wrong Entra tenant Verify tenant ID and the account's tid; multi-tenant or personal accounts are not accepted. Redirect error Register http://localhost and the WAM redirect exactly on the desktop platform. Account not assigned Check expected UPN/email, provider and account status in user administration. WAM/broker unavailable Check Windows version and broker package; system-browser fallback must remain operational. Loopback/timeout Check local firewall, proxy, browser launch and binding to 127.0.0.1, then retry. Google vendor client missing/invalid Check the diagnostic under Single sign-on and obtain a corrected FLEET Mira build from the vendor. Do not import a customer client file. Google consent expired/blocked Restart sign-in; for a Workspace restriction, check the organisation policy. The vendor checks branding, publication and central client status. Browser cancelled Start sign-in again; no local session or identity link is created.

Pilot and production check: successful provider test, pilot identity LINKED, unknown identity rejected, audit inspected for token leakage, local recovery tested and offboarding rehearsed. Microsoft Entra may only be considered a production sign-in method after successful additional acceptance of WAM, browser fallback, MFA and Conditional Access in a real customer tenant; until then it remains beta and untested.

docs.title: 3. Languages, regions and time basis
docs.text:
New deployments default to English and en-GB. User profiles may select any registered language/region. Date pickers, numbers and currency follow the region. Database/API dates remain ISO. Tachograph source data remains stored unchanged in UTC. Administrators may optionally select a local activity time zone under System → Settings; day/week boundaries, displays and compliance evaluations then use the same DST-safe projection. Evaluation runs and audit data record the selected time basis independently of the UI locale.

The UI supports 25 languages: all 24 official EU languages and Norwegian Bokmål. Irish (ga, Gaeilge) defaults to Ireland (ga-IE); Maltese (mt, Malti) defaults to Malta (mt-MT). Both regions use euro currency and dd/MM/yyyy dates. The authenticated profile language controls text independently of region; selecting another region does not change the language.

Translation catalogues live under translations/<language>.json. English is the fallback catalogue. Missing production keys log I18N_MISSING and fail the catalogue parity test.

Figure: Administrative application settings.

docs.title: 4. SQLite and migrations
docs.text:
Migrations run once at startup before repositories serve UI jobs. Use SQLite WAL/default locking as configured by the application; never copy a live database file for backup.

Operational recommendations:

  • keep database and archive on reliable local storage;
  • monitor free space and failed backup jobs;
  • use the built-in SQLite backup API snapshot;
  • test PRAGMA integrity_check after restore and during maintenance;
  • stop application and services before manual file-level maintenance;
  • never edit audit, signature or finance tables directly.

The deployment database must contain schema/default rows but no operational persons, vehicles, DDD files, documents, credentials or audit history.

docs.title: 5. Scheduler, sources and tasks
docs.text:
Background scheduling starts independently of an authenticated UI session and runs as SYSTEM. Supported source types are FTP, DLT API, SFTP, local folders and UNC shares. Every network operation must have connect/read timeouts. USB monitoring is intentionally owned by the desktop process and stops when that process exits.

Task processing sequence:

flowchart TD
    A[Schedule or Run now] --> B[List matching remote objects]
    B --> C[Download to controlled local path]
    C --> D[Hash, classify and archive]
    D --> E[Parse/signature verify or RFID CSV import]
    E --> F[Create/update business links and deadlines]
    F --> G[Queue cloud backup]
    G --> H{Strict backup mode?}
    H -->|No| I[Mark processed / optional terminal deletion]
    H -->|Yes| J[Wait for verified cloud object]
    J --> I

A technical failure before durable archiving must not mark or delete the terminal object. Duplicate hashes resume pending backup/deadline work without creating duplicate archives.

docs.title: 6. Tachograph archive and signature trust
docs.text:
The content dispatcher classifies DRIVER_CARD, VEHICLE_UNIT or UNKNOWN. C files use G1 RSA/SHA-1 or G2 ECDSA chains; M files verify signed download sections for G1/G2/G2V2. cryptography is a required runtime dependency.

Signature result priority is INVALID → UNVERIFIABLE → VALID. Parser status maps to verified, verified-with-warnings or quarantine. Quarantine never deletes the original but blocks trusted linking, C/M comparison, compliance snapshots and “latest trusted” selection.

Trust-store updates are administrative, explicit and audited. Validate package source, manifest and pinned fingerprints. Do not silently fetch or trust certificates from an arbitrary server.

docs.title: 7. Audit and diagnostics
docs.text:
The global audit normalises device, tachograph, fleet, finance, user and backup events. Each entry should include UTC time, actor/user ID, role, origin, action, object type/ID, result, correlation ID and sanitised before/after data. Passwords, tokens, API keys and binary originals are prohibited.

app.log is the complete application log. It includes scheduler, downloads, imports, jobs, cache timings, backup and service errors. Technical messages are always English. native_crash.log is written by faulthandler for process-level failures after diagnostics initialisation; failures before Python startup cannot be captured there.

Figure: Audit evidence used together with technical diagnostics.

The UI heartbeat logs UI_STALL if the main event loop is blocked for more than one second. A recovery entry records the duration. Use job/request/correlation IDs to join UI, service and audit events.

In Pro, GPS-server background runs start only after authentication has completed. A historical run honours stored coverage even when its progress cursor is missing. During shutdown, the UI waits only briefly for an active provider call; a TLS request that cannot be interrupted immediately must not freeze the window for minutes. Diagnose incidents by correlating the main_stack of UI_STALL, the active UI_JOB, and TELEMATICS_HISTORY_RESULT with its provider_windows and cached_intervals.

docs.title: 8. UI job operation
docs.text:
Expensive reads/calculations use worker-local SQLite connections. Qt widgets are changed only in the GUI thread. Read jobs, serialised writes and low-priority prefetch use separate lanes. New filter/date requests cancel stale generations; tab closure cancels owned work.

Performance incidents should be investigated by separating queue, database, compute, render and total time from the job log. Do not reintroduce processEvents() loops or modal busy dialogs for long work.

The native position map combines route lines into a small number of graphics paths, limits visible individual markers, and reads local cache tiles in small turns. This keeps the Qt event loop responsive even for large routes already reduced by the database query.

docs.title: 9. Driving-licence checks and notifications
docs.text:
PC/SC reads UID with FF CA 00 00 00, normalises to uppercase hexadecimal and assigns at most one active UID per person. A UID cannot be active for multiple persons.

Terminal CSV fields are UID;DD.MM.YYYY;HH:mm:ss;hostname. File- and row-level fingerprints provide idempotency. Unknown/inactive/time-incompatible UIDs remain clarification records.

SMTP supports STARTTLS or TLS. Passwords are DPAPI-protected. Default rules produce driver reminders and a daily fleet-responsible report. A desktop/tray process must be running for scheduled sends; missed runs are caught up only on the same day. Outbox idempotency prevents duplicate automatic mail per rule/object/recipient/day.

Figure: SMTP recipients, rules and send-log administration.

docs.title: 10. Finance and document vault
docs.text:
Financial data is stored in cents and EUR. Foreign invoices require exact header/position totals and at least one locally verified original before verification. Backup status is irrelevant to that decision. Booking makes business records immutable; corrections use cancellations or credits.

Original documents are never SQLite BLOBs. The financial vault stages, hashes, uploads, reads back and verifies each object. Metadata stores target, remote path/ID, hash, size, version and retention. Target deletion is blocked while documents reference it.

Accounting delivery is available through REST and CSV/ZIP. Only booked records are exportable. REST uses a persistent idempotent outbox.

docs.title: 11. Backup and disaster recovery
docs.text:
Basic and Pro open a guided wizard through Administration → Backups → Quick Backup. Database only remains a diagnostic ZIP. Complete manual backup contains the consistent SQLite snapshot and all active DDD, financial and record-document archives with their manifests. Each run can produce either a portable ZIP64 file or a backup directory. Local and UNC destinations are allowed; WebDAV and Google Drive are not offered by this wizard. AES-256-GCM is optional and requires a separately exported recovery key. Restore accepts both formats, validates completeness, key and every SHA-256 value, and normalises archive paths to the currently configured locations.

Pro may additionally have one local/UNC, Google Drive or HTTPS WebDAV target for automatic backups. Its queue, retention and schedule remain separate from the manual wizard.

Figure: Cloud target, backup queue and restore administration.

Archives are backed up asynchronously when a target is configured; database snapshots default to 02:00 UTC. Retention keeps 30 daily and 12 monthly database states. DDD backup objects are never automatically removed. Details and runbooks are in Archiving, backup and restore.

The complete operator and verification procedure is in the Backup and restore how-to.

docs.title: Controlled data-root relocation
docs.text:
Administration → Settings → Relocate data root … requires settings.manage and is available in every edition. The target must be an empty, absolute directory on a fixed local drive. UNC paths, mapped network drives, removable media, overlapping directories and unsuitable reparse targets are rejected.

The wizard stops local writers, copies every file, reads it back by size and SHA-256, normalises internal paths and atomically activates the machine-wide bootstrap locator. Basic and Pro additionally check SQLite integrity and foreign keys. Enterprise relocates only the local application root; PostgreSQL and deliberately external archives remain in place; a locally installed FleetMiraWorker is stopped for the move and restarted after startup validation. If startup validation fails, the locator is automatically switched back to the old root. After a successful restart, the old root can be retained or explicitly removed permanently. Retain is the default.

SSO activation, Entra configuration and identity assignments are stored in SQLite and are therefore included in database snapshots. The central Google client is part of the software build; provider tokens are not backed up. Test local emergency access and both SSO methods after every restore. Microsoft Entra remains beta after a successful restore until WAM, browser fallback, MFA and Conditional Access have been documented and accepted in the restored customer context.

At least quarterly, restore a database snapshot and representative C/M objects to an isolated test directory, verify hashes/integrity and document the result.

docs.title: 12. REST and integrations
docs.text:
• DriverCard REST binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and exposes parsed card evaluations.
  • Accounting REST sends booked invoice metadata and originals to a configured HTTPS endpoint.
  • Mobile licence-check endpoints remain a separate fleet API surface when enabled.

Do not expose a local development endpoint directly to the Internet. Place authentication, TLS, rate limiting and network access controls in front of any externally reachable API.

docs.title: GPS-server.net: creating a vehicle from the reconciliation list
docs.text:
Under Administration → Telematics → GPS-server.net, an administrator with telematics.reconcile and fleet.manage can select an unassigned object and choose Create vehicle from GPS-server object. The Telematics tab groups the connected providers, with each connector placed on its own subtab. Registration and VIN are only prefilled and remain visible for review before saving. A valid VIN from io256 in the latest position message is a provider observation, not verified vehicle evidence. Duplicate VINs or registrations are blocked.

Manage the system-wide calculation rules under Administration → Cost analysis → Calculation parameters → Odometer determination: by default, extrapolation uses a 14-day basis, at least three daily values and a maximum seven-day gap. The provider tab continues to control retention of telematics daily readings; the default is six years and zero means unlimited. Odometer rules can store a vehicle-specific override for a linked vehicle or restore the system default. The reconciliation table shows the latest daily reading, quality and projection state.

The optional online manufacturer/model lookup sends the VIN to NHTSA vPIC only after explicit confirmation. Because European vehicle coverage is limited, every suggested value requires business review. The complete procedure, source labels and operating boundaries are in the GPS-server.net integration guide.

docs.title: 13. Legacy technical identifiers
docs.text:
The visible product is FLEET Mira. The following are intentionally retained for compatibility:

  • repository/project folder and PyInstaller file DLTNGDownloadTool.spec;
  • technical executable/internal names where changing them would break upgrades;
  • SQLite table/column names, configuration keys and event codes;
  • DriverCard/API paths and payload fields;
  • remote root DLTNG/<installation-id>/..., manifest magic values and existing User-Agent identifiers.

These are protocol/storage identifiers, not user-facing product branding. Renaming them requires a separately versioned migration.

docs.title: 14. Security checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] named users only; initial admin password changed;
  • [ ] role matrix tested with a non-admin account;
  • [ ] database/archive ACLs restricted;
  • [ ] source, SMTP, backup and REST secrets protected;
  • [ ] WebDAV HTTPS certificate, separate Google Drive client and integrated Google SSO diagnostic validated;
  • [ ] Entra beta tested with WAM, browser fallback, MFA and Conditional Access in a real customer tenant; local fallback remains enabled;
  • [ ] recovery key stored offline and access logged;
  • [ ] strict terminal deletion selected where policy requires it;
  • [ ] audit/log retention and log rotation monitored;
  • [ ] signature trust store current and controlled;
  • [ ] daily database backup and archive backlog monitored;
  • [ ] restore test completed and documented;
  • [ ] operator procedural documentation covers retention, scan and legal review.

docs.title: 15. Incident and recovery checklist
docs.text:
1. Stop automatic writes if integrity, ransomware or credential compromise is suspected.
  2. Preserve app.log, native_crash.log, configuration and relevant audit exports.
  3. Revoke/rotate affected source, SMTP, SSO app registrations, Google/WebDAV and API credentials; see SSO operations and offboarding.
  4. Verify local archive hashes and remote object manifests.
  5. Restore into an isolated path first; never overwrite the only remaining database copy.
  6. Run integrity/hash checks and reconcile backup states.
  7. Resume services only after root cause, credentials and recovery result are documented.

docs.title: 16. Build and release checks
docs.text: Before release, run application tests, translation parity, documentation verification, mkdocs build --strict --clean, PyInstaller smoke tests and a clean deployment-database start. Verify both German and English screenshots contain FLEET Mira branding and no operational data.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: FLEET Mira supports transport operators in collecting, archiving and evaluating digital tachograph data while connecting that data to operational fleet records. Basic and Pro run on a local Windows 10/11 console session with SQLite on a fixed local drive. Enterprise provides the Pro business scope with PostgreSQL, a separate FleetMiraWorker Windows service and support for Windows Server, RDP, Citrix and multi-user installations.

docs.title: Main navigation
docs.text: Area Purpose Dashboard Consolidated operational status and direct links to filtered workspaces Device Management FLEET Mira terminals, status, remote files and device diagnostics Tachodata Archive C/M import, verification, analysis, export, deletion and backup status Fleet Management people, vehicles, deadlines, licence checks, tachodata coverage and finance Administration sources, tasks, audit, notifications, backup, users, roles, logs and settings

docs.title: Licensing and edition comparison
docs.text:
FLEET Mira remains freely downloadable and provides the complete Pro feature set for 30 days after the first start. The local primary tachograph and financial evidence archives remain part of Basic; they are not backups. Every 💎 feature is marked consistently in menus, tabs, buttons, settings and context actions.

docs.title: Enterprise runtime model
docs.text:
Aspect Basic / Pro Enterprise Database local SQLite only PostgreSQL only Background processing integrated worker while the application is running independent FleetMiraWorker Windows service Workstations local Windows 10/11 console Windows 10/11 clients or Windows Server sessions Co-location application and SQLite on one workstation client, worker and PostgreSQL may share one server but remain independent components Central jobs processed in the application runtime queued in PostgreSQL and leased by one worker Backup SQLite diagnostic snapshot or manual complete ZIP64/directory set; Pro additionally provides configured archive backup PostgreSQL custom dump plus DDD, financial and record-document archives

Enterprise never falls back to SQLite. Client actions that need background processing create a central job; advisory locks, leases and idempotency keys prevent duplicate external effects when several workers are available.

docs.title: Highlights in 1.1.0-beta9
docs.text:
• time-based, mileage-based and combined fleet deadlines, including lead values, recurrence, odometer quality and personnel/fleet reports;
  • record documents for people and vehicles with drag-and-drop, versions, metadata, preview, independent retention, backup and audit;
  • target-independent Quick Backup for Basic/Pro database diagnostics or complete ZIP64/directory sets and Enterprise PostgreSQL diagnostics;
  • guided, verified relocation of the local data root in every edition;
  • complete record-level audit coverage for deadlines, documents, licence checks, tachograph links, odometer readings, costs, invoices, evidence and exports;
  • language-specific field guidance while region settings independently control date, time and number formatting;
  • conventional PC/SC RFID/NFC UID byte order for display, assignment and checks.

The Report dashboard guide describes twelve working-time, mileage, return and deadline reports. The Violation dashboard guide documents the risk screen, violation report and driver instruction using anonymised demo data.

docs.title: Data flows
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[FTP, DLT API or manual import] --> B[Hash and immutable local archive]
    B --> C{Content classification}
    C -->|C file| D[Driver-card parser and signature verification]
    C -->|M file| E[Vehicle-unit parser and signature verification]
    D --> F[Person, activities, deadlines and compliance]
    E --> G[Vehicle, activities, calibration and positions]
    B --> H[Verified cloud backup]
    I[(SQLite metadata and audit)] --> H

docs.title: Security and evidence
docs.text:
• Local passwords use Argon2id; accounts lock after repeated failed attempts.
  • Fixed roles are ADMIN, SUPPORT, OPERATOR and AUDITOR; services re-check permissions independently of the UI.
  • Secrets are DPAPI-protected on Windows and excluded from logs and audit.
  • Archived DDD files and cloud objects are hash-verified.
  • Logical deletion requires a reason. Audit entries cannot be edited through the application.
  • Database backups are produced through the SQLite backup API and pass integrity_check before upload.

docs.title: Supported languages and regions
docs.text: The application provides German, English and 23 additional European UI languages (all 24 official EU languages plus Norwegian Bokmål). Language and region are independent profile settings. English (en-GB) is the default for new deployments. Tachograph timestamps remain UTC regardless of region.

docs.title: Scope boundaries
docs.text: FLEET Mira provides technical controls and technical pre-checks. It does not replace legal assessment, employment-law decisions, national exception handling, a certified accounting system or the operator's procedural documentation.

docs.title: User manual
docs.text: The workshop guide covers orders, articles, inventory, purchasing and outgoing invoicing in Pro and Enterprise. Follow workshop accounting operations for archiving, external backup and recovery.

docs.title: Detailed business guides
docs.text:
• Consistent action ribbons and form actions

  • Personnel and fleet tachodata evaluations

  • Driver-card analysis – every tab
  • Vehicle-unit analysis – every tab
  • Deadlines and record documents
  • Driving-licence checks and RFID/NFC
  • Vehicle costs and credits
  • Foreign invoices – workflow and every tab
  • Lease contracts, factor calculation and reports
  • E-invoice and XRechnung import
  • Cost analysis and reporting
  • Position maps for C and M data

These guides use a temporary anonymised copy of the development database. Activities, timestamps, amounts and approved coordinates remain representative. Driver names, dates of birth, card identities, registrations and VINs are replaced deterministically with recognisable demonstration values.

docs.title: Edition and processing model
docs.text:
Basic and Pro use a local SQLite database and process background tasks in the application. Enterprise uses PostgreSQL exclusively. Its client places central work in the database queue; the independent FleetMiraWorker service performs imports, notifications, backup and other scheduled work. The same user workflow therefore produces the same business result, but Enterprise jobs may continue after the client window is closed.

Open licence management through Help → Licensing. This menu entry and the licence dialog titles follow the signed-in user's language; the region does not change their wording. Changing the language does not activate a licence or replace online activation.

docs.title: 1. Sign-in and workspace
docs.text:
Start FLEET Mira from the installed shortcut. The splash screen remains visible throughout startup initialization and the initial workspace load wave. Only after its UI callbacks have completed is the splash seamlessly replaced, within the same render cycle, by the immediately interactive sign-in dialog. A new installation uses admin / admin once and forces a secure replacement password. If an administrator has configured SSO and pre-assigned your account, select Sign in with Microsoft or Sign in with Google instead. Microsoft Entra ID SSO is currently beta and has not yet been validated end-to-end with a real customer tenant. Keep local sign-in available as a fallback until customer-specific acceptance is complete and contact your administrator if sign-in fails. Setup and troubleshooting are covered by the Administrator and integrator guide.

Figure: FLEET Mira splash screen before sign-in.

Figure: Local sign-in, Microsoft Entra SSO in untested beta status and regularly supported Google SSO.

After every sign-in, the Dashboard is the active page. The top navigation switches between the five main areas. Long operations show a non-modal loading status and may be cancelled; other tabs remain usable.

docs.title: User profile
docs.text:
Open User → My profile to change display name, email, language and region. Language or region changes take effect after the next sign-in. Table layouts, filters, splitter positions and column order are stored per user.

Editable fields, selection lists, date and number fields, and toggles provide concise input guidance. In forms, point to the field caption; for standalone filters or toggles, the guidance appears on the control itself. The description states the expected input, any applicable format or range, and the effect of the selection. It always follows the authenticated user's language, while date, time, and number formats continue to follow the selected region.

Figure: User-specific language, region and profile settings.

docs.title: Tables and context menus
docs.text:
• Click a header to sort; click again to reverse the direction.
  • Drag headers to change the column order and drag header boundaries to change widths.
  • Right-click a header to show or hide columns where offered.
  • Right-click a data row for object-specific actions. The row under the pointer is selected first.
  • Selected rows use a dark-blue background and white text, overriding status colours for readability.

Column width, order, visibility and sorting belong to your personal table layout. When users change, the most recent actual edits are retained; another unchanged view of the same table cannot overwrite them. Restore default layout removes the saved layout until you change a column again. Closing the context menu without a selection changes nothing. Menu captions follow your user language.

docs.title: 2. Dashboard
docs.text:
The six photo-backed cards provide direct navigation:

Figure: Dashboard with anonymised demonstration data and direct navigation figures.

  • DLTNG devices: total, online and offline devices.
  • People/Vehicles: active master records.
  • Tachograph files: total C/M files, backup backlog/errors and latest imports.
  • Personnel deadlines / Vehicle deadlines: upcoming, due today and overdue items.
  • Driving-licence checks: pending clarification, checks due soon, overdue checks and the latest successful check.

Click an individual figure, not only the card, to open the corresponding pre-filtered list. Select Refresh dashboard after major imports when an immediate refresh is needed.

Basic always shows these six widgets in the fixed default layout. In Pro and Enterprise, Configure dashboard 💎 opens a personal editing mode on a 6×4 grid. Use the catalogue to show or hide widgets and drag them by their handle. A free area accepts the widget; dropping it on one equally sized widget swaps their positions. Save stores the layout for the signed-in user across workstations, Cancel discards the draft, and Restore default restores all six 2×2 widgets before saving.

Figure: Editing mode with the 6×4 grid, widget catalogue and drag handles.

docs.title: 3. Device Management
docs.text:
Figure: Device list and device-management workspace.

The device list can be filtered by name, tenant, site, group and status. Depending on permission, the toolbar and context menu allow you to:

  1. create, edit or duplicate a device;
  2. check status for one device or the current result set;
  3. open the embedded or standard browser interface;
  4. retrieve system information, remote files and the website log;
  5. deactivate or archive a device with confirmation.

The lower detail pages show master data, files, status history and audit. Remote file downloads use the configured destination and never alter the archive until the normal import path processes them.

docs.title: 4. Sources and download tasks
docs.text:
Open Administration → Sources to configure FTP, DLT API and SFTP endpoints, local folders, or UNC server shares. Test the connection before assigning a source to a task. Credentials and SFTP key passphrases are protected and do not appear in logs.

Figure: Administration of automatic import sources.

Open Administration → Tasks to define source selection, file patterns, recursion, schedule, archive behaviour and optional strict cloud-backup mode. Run now opens a detailed progress view with one row per source and live log messages. View latest log in the context menu opens the most recently stored execution with its trigger, run status, counters, source details and file details; unfinished runs remain visible. RFID terminal CSV files require RFID_*.CSV in the pattern.

The Administration → Settings → Automatically import USB removable drives option recursively scans newly inserted drives for DDD and RFID*.CSV files. It operates only while FLEET Mira is open or running in the system tray; source files remain on the drive.

docs.title: Data root and storage paths
docs.text: Under Administration → Settings, administrators can see the active data root and the fully resolved log, SQLite, DDD archive, document archive and financial archive paths. These fields remain read-only so files, database references and access permissions cannot be separated. Relocate data root … opens a guided wizard that copies and verifies the complete local root, normalises internal paths and restarts FLEET Mira through the new machine-wide locator. The target must be empty and on a fixed local drive. Enterprise moves only its local application root; PostgreSQL and deliberately external archives remain in place.

docs.title: Quick Backup and central backup jobs
docs.text:
Under Administration → Backups → Quick Backup, Basic and Pro choose between Database only and Complete manual backup. The database option remains a consistent, read-back-verified diagnostic ZIP. The complete backup also contains active DDD, financial and record-document archives with their manifests and can be written as either a portable ZIP64 file or a backup directory on a local or UNC destination. Optionally encrypted sets require a separately exported recovery key. The restore wizard supports both formats.

In Enterprise, Quick Backup requests the dedicated backup credentials and creates a PostgreSQL custom dump through the worker. Complete Enterprise backup jobs additionally process the configured DDD, financial and record-document archives. Closing the Enterprise client does not cancel a job already accepted by FleetMiraWorker.

Figure: Backup configuration, verification state and manual actions.

Figure: Scheduled and manually executable download tasks.

In strict mode, a terminal file is not marked as processed or deleted until its cloud copy is verified.

docs.title: 5. Tachodata Archive
docs.text:
Figure: Filterable C/M tachodata archive with status columns.

The archive contains driver-card C files and vehicle-unit M files. Filter by date, name, driver/vehicle, file type, generation, parser status, signature status, deletion state or backup state.

docs.title: Import and status
docs.text:
• Import DDD files accepts one or more local files.
  • Content determines C/M type; the filename is only a hint.
  • Successful parsing stores structured details without changing the original archive object.
  • VALID means all available signatures and the chain could be verified.
  • INVALID or UNVERIFIABLE places the file in quarantine; it remains viewable and exportable but cannot drive trusted links or combined evaluations.

docs.title: Open, export and delete
docs.text:
• Double-click or choose Open analysis to open the C or M analysis.
  • One selected row exports the original DDD; several rows or the current view export a ZIP.
  • Logical deletion requires a reason and is recorded in audit. It does not automatically delete a verified cloud backup.
  • Details / Signature / Audit explains hashes, parser warnings, signature sections and history.

docs.title: Backup status
docs.text: Verified is shown only after complete upload and remote hash verification. Use the context menu to retry, verify or restore a file. Backup errors are also linked from the dashboard.

docs.title: 6. Driver-card analysis
docs.text:
The header identifies the driver, card number and selected archive file. The analysis always uses the selected C file as its base.

Figure: Driver-card analysis for one selected C archive.

Tab Purpose Overview identity, validity, issuing authorities, generation and data range Activities sortable activity intervals in the configured time basis with C/M availability Day / Week graphical timelines, totals and details for the selected period DDD week view Web browser-style interactive week view using the selected file Events / Faults technical records from the card Vehicles used vehicle identifiers observed on the card Positions location list and interactive map Violations technical EU 561/2006 pre-check Signatures chain and per-EF verification results

The Data availability filter distinguishes all activities, C and M available, driver card only and vehicle unit only. The other source is comparison evidence; it never replaces the selected base file. Tachograph source data remains stored unchanged in UTC. Display and calculations use UTC by default. When Use local time for activities and calculations is enabled under System → Settings, display, day/week boundaries and compliance evaluations instead use the selected time zone. Daylight-saving transitions change neither source values nor elapsed durations.

docs.title: 7. Vehicle-unit analysis
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle-unit analysis for one selected M archive.

The M analysis shows vehicle identity and the selected M file. Driver sessions are grouped by normalised card number and generation. Team driving displays slot 1 and slot 2 separately.

Tabs include drivers, activities, day/week timelines, events/faults, speed, technical data, calibrations, positions/borders/loading, signatures and violations. Technical data uses a field tree; Calibrations lists calibration time, next calibration, workshop, VIN and registration. Position tabs can open the interactive map.

“No assigned driver card” means the M file contains slot activity for which no active card-insertion interval with a usable card number was found. It does not mean that a matching C archive is merely missing; the tooltip in day/week views explains this distinction.

docs.title: 8. Fleet Management
docs.text:
The compact left icon navigation opens non-duplicated work tabs and behaves the same in Fleet Management and Administration. A + or − to the left of a parent item expands or collapses its children. The context menu shows fixed pairs for Expand/Collapse item, Expand/Collapse group, and Expand/Collapse all; actions that do not apply are disabled. Group recursively affects the complete top-level subtree, including nested areas such as Traffic offences and External invoices. The state is stored for the signed-in user. Users without a stored preference start with the navigation fully collapsed. A new session starts with an empty workspace in both areas.

In Administration, Operations, Users and security, Communication and integrations, and Finance and system are the parent groups. Their pages are child entries and each opens one closable, movable work tab on the right. Selecting an already open child focuses its tab instead of creating a duplicate.

Figure: Fleet Management icon navigation and non-duplicated work tabs.

docs.title: Master data
docs.text:
• People: personal number, identity, contact data, licence data, FSK policy and status.
  • Vehicles: internal number, registration, VIN, type and status.
  • Due types: system and user-defined deadline categories for people or vehicles.
  • Suppliers / Cost categories: finance master data.

Figure: Personnel master-data list.

Figure: Vehicle master-data list.

Double-click a person or vehicle to open its record. Context menus jump directly to deadlines, tachodata, RFID or finance pages.

Use Fleet > Cost analysis to evaluate booked vehicle costs. Its initial period runs from the start of the current year through today; administrators can change the global default under Administration > Cost analysis > Calculation parameters.

docs.title: Person record
docs.text:
Figure: Person record with related business tabs.

The record contains master data, deadlines, documents, licence checks, RFID history, card links/files, day/week/activity views and audit. The Audit tab uses the same context menu as the global Audit Log: open the related record, show the XML tree view, or copy details, rows and cells. The Documents tab accepts drag-and-drop or file selection, versioning and metadata; PDF and image files can be previewed directly. Document and validity dates use date pickers formatted for the signed-in user's region. The immutable local original is created when the document is added, while the configured backup task handles external backup. Logical archiving remains available from the context menu. Local restore and permanent purge are visible only to appropriately authorised administrators. Use Assign RFID/NFC to read a UID from a local PC/SC reader. FSK via PC/SC records a successful check only when the read UID belongs to the selected person.

For a new record document, the document date defaults to today. Valid until is calculated from the document date plus the period configured under Administration → Receipts/Documents → Document retention period. The financial-document retention period remains independent.

The Audit tab covers the complete record. In addition to personnel or vehicle master-data changes, it includes logged events for related deadlines, documents, driving-licence checks and tachograph links. Vehicle records additionally include odometer readings, costs/credits, associated supplier invoices, financial documents and accounting exports. The Area column identifies the related sub-object.

docs.title: Vehicle record
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle record with tachograph, finance and position tabs.

The Master data tab opens the existing modal vehicle form through Edit vehicle. It also shows the latest reliable odometer reading with its source and quality, and the last known human-readable location. With an active telematics assignment, Open telematics opens a dedicated workspace for current location, route history, combined positions and events.

The Positions tab globally merges tachograph and telematics evidence, clearly labels its source and provides a source filter. Only telematics points form the route line in Route history; tachograph positions can be shown as reference markers.

Tabs include deadlines, documents, costs/credits, foreign invoices, lease, positions and audit. Tachograph links, mass-memory files, day/week views, infringements, drivers/activities, events/faults, speeds, technical data and calibrations are grouped below Tachodata. The Audit tab uses the same context menu as the global Audit Log: open the related record, show the XML tree view, or copy details, rows and cells. Record documents use the same audit-oriented archive and configured local, UNC or cloud backup destination. Aggregate functional tables hide the source-file column by default; the source archive remains available from the context menu. Identical technical records appear once with their source count and complete detail tree. Position rows can be opened together on the map.

docs.title: Odometer determination
docs.text:
FLEET Mira uses the same central odometer resolver for mileage reports and cost per kilometre. Manage the system-wide calculation rules under Administration → Cost analysis → Calculation parameters → Odometer determination. The provider tab Administration → Telematics → GPS-server.net additionally controls retention of telematics daily readings; use Mileage rules there to enable an override for an individual linked vehicle.

The settings shown in the standard dialog have the following meaning:

Setting Default Meaning Position detail retention (days) 28 Position points and sensor parameters are purged after 28 days. Qualified daily odometer readings are retained separately. Retain daily odometer readings (years) 6 Consolidated telematics daily readings are retained for six years. The permitted range is 1 to 20 years; Unlimited disables this purge. Missing period boundaries Extrapolate If a day or month has no sufficiently recent actual reading at its boundary, the following rules estimate it. This also applies to the current day once it has started. The alternatives are Interpolate and Incomplete. Estimation basis (days) 14 Depending on direction, extrapolation considers up to 14 plausible daily distances before or after the missing boundary. Minimum daily values 3 At least three usable daily distances are required for extrapolation. Maximum estimation gap (days) 7 The gap between the actual support reading and the missing boundary must not exceed seven days. For interpolation, this limit applies on both sides.

FLEET Mira first searches the 24 hours before the period boundary for a qualified actual reading. If several sources are available, the following priority is mandatory:

  1. M-file midnight reading (M_MIDNIGHT)
  2. Telematics sensor (GPS_SERVER_SENSOR)
  3. C-file vehicle use (C_VEHICLE_USE)
  4. C-file place (C_PLACE)
  5. C-file three-hour GNSS position (C_GNSS_3H)
  6. Telematics GPS (GPS_SERVER_GPS)

Only readings with quality Valid or Warning are eligible. Unverified, unknown, manual or conflicting readings are excluded. The newest reading wins within the same source. A higher-priority reading can therefore override a slightly newer lower-priority reading as long as it is not older than 24 hours.

Source-priority example: At the 1 July 00:00 boundary, an M-file midnight reading of 80,000 km was measured at 23:58 and a telematics sensor reading of 80,005 km at 23:59. Both are recent and qualified, so the M-file value of 80,000 km is used. If the M-file value is absent, the sensor value is used.

With Interpolate, the resolver draws a straight line between the latest qualified reading before the boundary and the first qualified reading after it. Both support readings must lie within the maximum estimation gap, must be compatible and must not produce an odometer rollback:

Estimated value = previous reading + elapsed share × (following reading − previous reading)

Interpolation example: A reading of 120,000 km is available for 10 July 00:00 and 120,800 km for 14 July 00:00. Two of the four days have elapsed at the 12 July boundary. The interpolated reading is 120,000 + 2/4 × 800 = 120,400 km.

With Extrapolate, FLEET Mira calculates the median of the plausible daily distances in the estimation basis. A missing closing boundary is projected forwards from the latest actual reading. If the opening boundary is missing and qualified readings only follow it, the same logic is applied symmetrically backwards from the first actual reading. Daily rates below 0 or above 1,800 km are rejected, and different GPS odometer kinds are not mixed:

Estimated value = latest actual reading + median daily distance × estimation gap

Opening reading = first following actual reading − median daily distance × estimation gap

Example using the default settings: The latest actual reading on 12 July is 120,000 km. The usable daily distances in the preceding 14 days are 180, 200 and 220 km, giving a median of 200 km. The gap to the 15 July boundary is three days. FLEET Mira calculates 120,000 + 200 × 3 = 120,600 km. With only two usable daily distances or an eight-day gap, the displayed settings would not permit an estimate and the boundary would remain incomplete.

Opening-boundary example: The first qualified reading after the start of the month is 80,200 km at 2 July 00:00. Three subsequent plausible daily distances have a median of 180 km. For the month boundary one day earlier, FLEET Mira derives an opening reading of 80,200 − 180 × 1 = 80,020 km.

Estimated values are not stored as actual odometer readings. The report exposes the result, method, support readings, measurement times, estimation distance and algorithm version. Opening and closing boundaries use the same configured strategy and quality limits. Both readings are rounded to whole kilometres first; the difference is then calculated exactly as closing − opening. For the current local day, FLEET Mira first uses the latest qualified actual reading from that day. If none exists and Extrapolate is configured, the reading is estimated up to the current calculation instant, not to the future midnight boundary. Daily, monthly and overall mileage and cost analysis share this central closing boundary. If no permitted estimate can be produced, an existing latest actual period reading remains usable as partial coverage. See Report dashboard for the detailed daily audit and Cost analysis and reporting for the identical use in cost per kilometre.

docs.title: 9. Deadlines and download due dates
docs.text:
Personnel and vehicle deadline evaluations are separate but use the same sortable/filterable component. Personnel deadlines remain time-based. Vehicle deadlines can be time-based, mileage-based or combined; a combined deadline becomes due when the first limit is reached. Time and mileage lead values and recurrence intervals can be configured per deadline or as due-type defaults.

The fleet evaluation displays the latest reliable odometer reading, measurement time and source, target and remaining mileage, trigger and data quality. Filters cover due type, status, basis, trigger, mileage quality and evaluability. If a combined deadline has no valid mileage reading, its time condition remains usable while the mileage condition is marked only partially evaluable. Colours mean:

  • green: outside the lead time;
  • blue/orange status: approaching or due today;
  • red: overdue;
  • completed: closed with completion date.

Automatic download deadlines are managed by the system:

Figure: Filterable personnel deadline evaluation.

  • current driver card: readout date + 28 days;
  • vehicle unit matched by VIN: readout date + 90 days.

The readout date is taken from a valid C_YYYYMMDD_HHmm... or M_YYYYMMDD_HHmm... filename, then falls back to source creation, download and archive UTC dates. Automatic deadlines cannot be manually moved or completed. Tachograph calibration remains a separate vehicle deadline.

docs.title: 10. Driving-licence checks and RFID
docs.text:
The complete workflow for check policy, UID assignment, PC/SC checks, automatic follow-up dates, terminal CSV and exceptions is documented in Driving-licence checks and RFID/NFC. A system-managed deadline is completed only by a successful check; an unknown chip or a chip assigned to another person creates no success record.

The Personnel navigation provides:

Figure: Driving-licence-check (FSK) due-date evaluation.

  • FSK evaluation with interval, last check, next due date, terminal and status;
  • licence-check history;
  • RFID pending list for unknown UIDs or invalid CSV rows.

The default check interval is 28 days. Successful PC/SC, terminal CSV and resolved mobile records use the same service and update one managed FSK deadline. Assigning an RFID UID alone is not a check.

Unknown terminal UIDs remain pending. Assigning them creates the effective check; discarding requires a reason and never creates a permanent RFID assignment.

docs.title: 11. Notifications
docs.text:
Under Administration → Notifications, configure SMTP, responsible recipients, rules/templates and the send log. Recipients may be assigned to fleet management, system management or both; their To/CC type applies to both assignments. Double-clicking a recipient or rule opens its edit dialog. The system is disabled until SMTP and recipients have been tested and sending is explicitly enabled.

Figure: Notification rules, templates and schedules.

Standard rules cover weekly information, daily reminders from ten days, urgent reminders from three days, overdue warnings and a daily responsible-person report. Additional rules can distribute violation dashboards to managers and deliver each new driver instruction exactly once with its PDF attachment. Rules may be previewed or sent manually when the user has permission.

The Daily task status report system rule is sent exclusively to system managers at 07:00 each day by default. Immediately before delivery it checks every active DLTNG device and summarises scheduled and manual download tasks from the complete previous day. For each source it shows availability, error details and downloaded, successful, failed and skipped file counts. One UTF-8 CSV lists every successful or failed file; a report with a header-only CSV is also sent on days without a run. Previewing deliberately performs no live device access. Fleet status, cost analysis and violation dashboard reports remain exclusive to fleet managers.

docs.title: Direct vehicle costs
docs.text:
Open a vehicle record → Costs / Credits. Select category and type and enter document date, validity period, net and VAT. Variable allocates the full amount to the document date; fixed entries are distributed by day over their complete validity period. Amounts are stored to the cent. Draft, verification, booking, cancellation and credit are covered in Vehicle costs and credits.

Figure: Supplier master data for financial documents.

docs.title: Foreign invoices
docs.text:
Open Fleet → Foreign invoices. Double-click an invoice to open it as a work tab.

Figure: Foreign-invoice list and work-tab entry point.

flowchart LR
    A[Create draft header] --> B[Add vehicle positions]
    B --> C[Upload original documents]
    C --> D[Cloud hash verified]
    D --> E[Verify totals]
    E --> F[Book]
    F --> G[REST or CSV/ZIP accounting export]

The status row compares gross invoice amount, split amount and difference. Zero difference is green; any cent difference is red and blocks verification. Invoice-bound positions inherit the invoice date for document/valid-from/valid-to and are always variable. Booked data is immutable; corrections use cancellation or linked credits.

docs.title: Lease contracts
docs.text:
Use Fleet → Lease contracts to manage contract data, factor-based pre-calculation, payment schedule, documents, recurring invoices and linked actual costs. Creation is manual or, in Pro/Enterprise, document-assisted through XInvoice, PDF text, OCR, local ML and the optional AI connector; every proposal requires explicit review and confirmation. Lease contracts explains the workflows, factor formulas, M-data mileage evidence and all three leasing reports.

Figure: Filterable lease-contract overview from the anonymised demo database.

docs.title: E-invoice/XRechnung
docs.text: Fleet → Import XRechnung guides users through KoSIT validation, invoice and supplier data, vehicle/category allocation, line splitting and totals reconciliation. Only confirmed creation atomically writes a foreign-invoice draft and locally verified original, XML and report objects. See E-invoice and XRechnung import.

docs.title: 13. Audit, reports and logs
docs.text:
The global audit under Administration → Audit combines device, tachograph and fleet events. Filter by date, user, action or text. Double-click an entry to open its current related object when the stable ID can be resolved. Structured JSON/XML details can be opened as a tree, exported as JSON and printed. Navigation itself is not audited.

Figure: Global audit log with object-based navigation.

Fleet → Violation dashboard 💎 provides period-based risk scoring, detailed findings, a dashboard report and tamper-evident driver instructions. Fleet → Report dashboard 💎 contains fifteen working-time, mileage, leasing, return and deadline reports with favourites, run history and PDF/Excel output. All screens, purpose descriptions and Stimulsoft PDF examples are shown in Violation dashboard and driver instructions and Report dashboard.

Deadline and evaluation grids support print preview, system printing and PDF. Only visible filtered rows and columns are included.

Administration → Logs shows app.log, REST logs and native crash diagnostics. Logs use English technical messages regardless of the selected UI language.

docs.title: 14. Tray and shutdown
docs.text: Closing the main window normally keeps background services running in the system tray. Use the tray action to restore the window. Use System → Exit application and services or the equivalent tray command for a clean shutdown; schedulers, REST API, notification service, backup coordinator and logs are closed in order.

docs.title: 15. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Action File is quarantined Open Details/Signatures; install missing crypto/trust material or verify the source. Do not re-label the file manually. Backup remains pending Test the active target, inspect quota/authentication and use Back up now. No PC/SC reader Install the reader driver, reconnect it and reopen the read dialog. No C/M comparison Verify matching card number, generation, UTC range and valid signature status. Invoice cannot be verified Resolve the split difference and ensure at least one original document is locally verified. Backup status does not block verification. UI job failed Use Retry, then inspect app.log with the displayed job/request ID.

For administrator-level recovery, continue with the Administrator and integrator guide.

Application-wide action-bar and function-icon standardization is documented in the UI rollout report, including every covered program point.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: The accounting adapter transmits a booked foreign invoice, supplier, vehicle positions and original documents to a configured HTTPS endpoint. FLEET Mira is the HTTP client; the accounting system implements the receiver.

docs.title: 2. Preconditions
docs.text:
• invoice status is BOOKED;
  • header totals match active positions to the cent;
  • at least one original document is locally verified; backup status is irrelevant;
  • user has finance.export;
  • endpoint uses HTTPS;
  • no successful export exists for the same idempotency key.

docs.title: 3. Request
docs.text:
POST /configured/accounting/path HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...
Idempotency-Key: <stable-sha256>

Multipart fields:

Field Content type Meaning metadata application/json; charset=utf-8 complete versioned accounting bundle document_1...n original MIME type byte-identical, hash-verified originals

docs.title: 4. Metadata model
docs.text:
Top level:

Field Meaning format technical constant DLTNG-ACCOUNTING retained for compatibility version contract version invoice invoice header supplier supplier master snapshot positions vehicle-linked cost/credit positions

Important invoice fields include stable ID, document type/number/date, delivery date/number, cost centre, due date, payment/discount terms, net/tax/gross cents, status and currency. Supplier includes stable ID, supplier/creditor numbers, address, tax ID, phone and email. Positions include stable ID, vehicle ID/number/registration/VIN, category, type, description, validity/document dates, net/tax/gross cents, tax rate basis points and variable flag.

Amounts are integer cents. Tax rates are integer basis points (1900 = 19.00%). Credits are identified by type; stored amounts remain positive.

docs.title: 5. Idempotency
docs.text: The key is deterministic for invoice ID, booked revision and export contract version. A receiver must return the original successful result for a repeated key and must not post twice.

docs.title: 6. Response
docs.text:
Success (200 or 201):

{
  "status": "accepted",
  "external_id": "ACC-2026-004712",
  "message": "Imported"
}

external_id is persisted with response time. A non-2xx response keeps the outbox item retryable and stores a sanitised error. Authentication bodies/secrets are not audited.

docs.title: 7. Process
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant M as FLEET Mira
    participant V as Document vault
    participant A as Accounting endpoint
    U->>M: Transfer booked invoice
    M->>V: Download and hash-check originals
    M->>M: Build bundle and idempotency key
    M->>A: HTTPS multipart POST
    alt accepted
        A-->>M: external_id
        M->>M: Mark export successful and audit
    else temporary failure
        A-->>M: error
        M->>M: Persist outbox retry
    end

docs.title: 8. Receiver requirements
docs.text:
• enforce HTTPS and authenticated clients;
  • limit body size and accepted MIME types;
  • stream originals and verify declared hashes where exposed;
  • implement atomic invoice/document handling;
  • persist idempotency keys;
  • return stable external IDs;
  • redact credentials and document contents from logs.

docs.title: 9. Error handling
docs.text: Status Receiver meaning 400/422 permanent contract/validation error; operator correction required 401/403 credentials/permission error 409 idempotency or business conflict; return existing result when equivalent 413 payload exceeds receiver limit 429 retry later; honour Retry-After 5xx transient receiver failure; outbox retry

docs.title: 10. Compatibility
docs.text: Fields are additive within a contract version. Removing/renaming fields or changing amount semantics requires a new version. The legacy DLTNG-ACCOUNTING format token is deliberately not rebranded.

docs.title: Device REST API
docs.text: Status: 2026-11-04 source implementation. The optional device_management_api.create_app() factory starts no listener. This does not accept a built or installed service.

docs.title: Access and hosting
docs.text:
This implementation requires Flask 3.1 or later for host validation. All nine routes require actual HTTPS, an accepted host name and Authorization: Bearer <token>. X-User, X-Role, query tokens and forwarded assertions of HTTPS do not authenticate callers. The factory denies access without an authority and explicit host profile. Supported host profiles are pro_desktop and enterprise_worker; Basic and EnterpriseClient do not provide this entry point. Pro uses SQLite and EnterpriseWorker PostgreSQL. The existing api.drivercard feature must be checked against current licensing at the composition root; allowed is this mandatory callback, never an HTTP caller-controlled value.

Trusted application code composes DeviceApiAuthority(db_path, allowed=licence_check) and create_app(db_path, authority=authority, host_profile=profile, trusted_hosts=[hostname]). licence_check, profile and hostname come from verified host configuration. Without an explicit host list only localhost/loopback host names are accepted, still requiring HTTPS. Certificates, listener, firewall and any strictly configured proxy boundary require separate setup. This change opens no port and accepts no arbitrary forwarded headers.

docs.title: Identity and grants
docs.text:
The new device audience is separate from mobile, driver, portal and webhook credentials. The user must be active and hold current business permissions in app_role_permission. Each credential receives explicit scopes and either a list of permitted device-customer IDs or an explicit all_customers=True grant. No credential is issued without an assignment. The empty customer value "" denotes unassigned devices and must be explicitly granted for restricted credentials. Device customers are separate from workshop customers.

Scope Current business permissions Routes devices.read devices.read List and detail devices.manage devices.read, devices.manage Create, update, deactivate, archive devices.check devices.read, devices.check Status check devices.audit devices.read, audit.read Device audit devices.dashboard devices.read, dashboard.read Dashboard

Assignments also restrict filters, status history, audit, counts and mutations. A supplied customer filter never expands access. Foreign and unknown devices both return 404. Reassignment requires access to the existing device and permission for the target customer; locations must belong to that customer. Device groups retain the existing global catalogue.

docs.title: Credential administration
docs.text:
Administration is available only through trusted Python composition; there is no anonymous login/token endpoint or new administration menu.

# authenticated_admin_session comes from actual login, never HTTP JSON.
credential_id, token = authority.issue_integration(
    authenticated_admin_session, owner_user_id, "Device reader",
    scopes=["devices.read"], customer_ids=[approved_customer_id],
    expires_seconds=86400,
)

Issuers need current users.manage; the owner must hold every requested business permission. Integration credentials use at least 32 random bytes, store only a digest and expire after the explicitly chosen duration: one day by default, at most 365 days. Show the raw value only at issuance; never place it in logs, reports or URLs. authority.revoke(authenticated_admin_session, credential_id) revokes and audits the credential. A new authority for the same database can continue verifying valid integration credentials.

Alternatively, issue_session(authenticated_session, scopes=..., customer_ids=...) supports verified desktop composition, with an eight-hour maximum and validity only in the issuing process. The host must call revoke_sessions() on logout, user/database change and shutdown; the factory does not attach itself to UI lifecycle events.
