LOCAL checks enabled local login, lock and password state. Microsoft/Google SSO checks the enabled provider and unchanged linked identity. Persistent integration credentials are independent of desktop logout and local password flags; account activity, scope, permissions, expiry, revocation, licence and database binding still apply.

docs.title: Routes and responses
docs.text:
Method/path Response GET /api/devices Array of permitted devices; existing search/customer/location/group/status/active/archive filters POST /api/devices 201, projected detail of created device GET /api/devices/<device_id> Detail containing device, groups, status_history PUT /api/devices/<device_id> 200, projected detail POST /api/devices/<device_id>/deactivate ok, device_id POST /api/devices/<device_id>/archive ok, device_id POST /api/devices/<device_id>/status-check status, success, checked_at, last_successful_contact, response_code GET /api/devices/<device_id>/audit Array of permitted audit metadata GET /api/dashboard/devices Counts for accessible non-archived devices only; stale_minutes 1–525600, default 1440

HEAD and OPTIONS inherit route protection. Later undeclared routes deny access. Responses use explicit field lists: no credentials, device base URLs, raw device responses, internal errors or old/new audit payloads. Details have no embedded audit list. New business audits recursively remove known credential fields and raw responses; existing historical audits are not rewritten. API status checks persist no raw responses or error text and log no unfiltered upstream exceptions.

docs.title: Writes and replay
docs.text:
POST creation and PUT require JSON. All five POST/PUT write-operation types require Idempotency-Key, containing 1–128 letters, digits, ., _, :, -. Keys are bound to credential, operation and device ID; a canonical input hash prevents conflicting reuse. Identical replay returns the stored result and changed input returns 409. Current permissions and device assignment are checked on replay too. Requests do not duplicate business changes or audits. Receipt, business mutation and audit commit in one transaction.

At most 1000 write receipts per credential; further writes return 429 and require administrative issuance of a new credential. Receipts are not automatically deleted or silently re-executed after a deadline. Credential issuance/revocation and business changes use verified user identity; business audit records additionally contain credential ID, correlation ID and device-api origin.

Unknown and read-only input fields are rejected; a body ID cannot override the path ID. Omitted credential fields are preserved on update. Changing the device base URL clears credential fields that were not explicitly supplied again, preventing old secrets from being sent to a new destination. URLs containing user info, query or fragment are invalid for new/revised API inputs.

docs.title: Limits and errors
docs.text:
Requests are limited to a 64-KiB body, 8-KiB query and 2048 path characters. Lists use limit=100 by default (1–500) and offset=0 (0–100000), retaining array responses. Customer boundaries apply before pagination. Projected text fields are capped at 4096 characters and successful JSON responses at 2 MiB; excess responses return 503/response_size_limit. Dashboard counts are computed in the database independently of the list page. Each application permits at most eight concurrent device API requests. The minute window allows at most 240 requests per actual peer and 120 per credential/scope; status checks allow ten per credential/minute. Status checks have a maximum 30-second network timeout and 1-MiB device response; these API calls disable redirects and environment proxies. Authorization is repeated before mutations, repository access and successful responses. Completed external contacts or bytes already sent cannot be recalled.

Error object: ok=false, stable error, server-side requestId. Codes: 400 input/host/missing idempotency key, 401 missing Bearer with challenge, 403 invalid/revoked credential or missing permission, 404 unknown/foreign device, 409 idempotency conflict, 413 size, 415 media type, 426 missing HTTPS, 429 load/receipt limit, 503 unavailable verification/operation. No internal exception text. Responses set no-store, nosniff, framing/referrer/CSP protection and no general CORS allowance.

docs.title: Migration and acceptance
docs.text:
Clients using role headers must explicitly migrate to new credentials, customer grants, write keys and reduced responses. There is no anonymous transition mode. Native device UI and outgoing device protocols receive no new HTTP login. Credential and audit schema are initialized by repeatable device migration 2 on SQLite and PostgreSQL. Existing PostgreSQL installations need the normal schema update and its established backup/rollback procedure; request handlers do not migrate databases.

Source anchors: api_identity.py, api_security.py, device_api_service.py, device_management_api.py, device_management.py; regressions: test_device_api_security.py, test_drivercard_api_security.py. Actual executed tests are recorded in the timestamped report. TLS/firewall/frozen/installed acceptance and actual third-party consumer inventory remain separate release steps.

docs.title: 1. Scope and source status
docs.text:
Contract inspected in drivercard_rest_api.py, working tree based on 063f794294f0e05df5756def7b6aabc2367a76f2, 2026-11-04, application source version 1.1.0-beta9. Local changes are not a shipped-build guarantee. Validate the intended target build before integration. This reference describes existing behavior; it introduces no new API behavior.

The parser produces a response from supplied bytes. It does not persist an archive or import. Archive ingestion and mobile intake are separate workflows. Read operations query existing analysis data.

docs.title: 2. Address and formats
docs.text:
The desktop binds its own dynamically assigned loopback port. Use the base URL displayed by the running application; the bundled week view receives that actual address automatically. Driver routes accept loopback clients only and require Authorization: Bearer <session-token>. The authenticated desktop creates an in-memory credential bound to its user, licence and current archive.read permission, with a maximum lifetime of eight hours. Logout, user change and account deactivation invalidate access. Local sessions additionally reject disabled local login, account lock, required password change or password changes. Verified Microsoft/Google SSO sessions instead require an enabled provider and unchanged linked identity mapping; local password flags do not block these SSO sessions. Query parameters and asserted X-User/X-Role headers cannot authenticate a caller. There is no anonymous or unattended integration fallback; external clients require a separately approved authentication and transport integration before migration. Listener availability depends on the host/profile and enabled features; a desktop default is not a deployment guarantee. Use the approved integration entry point for the target installation.

JSON uses UTF-8. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Parse metadata timestamps use local datetime.now() without an explicit offset; do not assume UTC. Public /health returns only ok and service; it does not expose listener configuration, time or database readiness. Durations in normalized parse activities are seconds. Other result columns follow the corresponding repository projection.

docs.title: 3. Common read filters
docs.text:
date_from defaults to today minus 30 days, date_to to today. The first ten characters are parsed as a date; reversed ranges return 400. Name/card filters are last_name, first_name, card_number, driving_license_number. A nonempty value without % or _ is wrapped in %; matching is SQL LIKE, not guaranteed exact matching. time-summary also accepts grouping=day|week|month (default day). EU analysis accepts multi_manning (default false).

import_id, archive_id, limit and offset are not implemented common filters in this controller. Imports returns all repository import rows with empty returned filters, although the common date validation still runs.

docs.title: 4. Operations
docs.text:
Method/path Function and response GET /health HTTP process response: ok, service=drivercard_rest_api; public process liveness only, no database readiness probe POST /api/drivercard/parse Parse supplied bytes; response has ok, meta, card, activities, week_index, events, faults, vehicles_used, positions, raw GET /api/drivercard/imports Existing imports; data.type=imports GET /api/drivercard/time-summary Repository activity totals; data.type=time_summary GET /api/drivercard/activities Activity details; data.type=activities GET /api/drivercard/events Card events; data.type=events GET /api/drivercard/faults Card faults; data.type=faults GET /api/drivercard/vehicles-used Recorded vehicles; data.type=vehicles_used GET /api/drivercard/positions Recorded positions; data.type=positions GET /api/drivercard/day-overview Activity intervals grouped by day; data.type=day_overview GET /api/drivercard/week-overview Activity intervals grouped by ISO week; data.type=week_overview GET /api/drivercard/eu561/violations Technical EU 561/2006 evaluation; ok, data with filters, count, legal_notice and analysis report

List responses use {"ok":true,"data":{"type":"activities","count":0,"filters":{},"items":[]}} (illustrative empty result; actual filters are returned). Day/week responses use the same envelope, with grouped periods, activities and totals inside items; week periods also contain days. EU analysis is a technical pre-check, not an authority or legal decision.

docs.title: 5. Health example
docs.text:
GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:49152

{"ok":true,"service":"drivercard_rest_api"}

No credentials are needed for this minimal health response.

docs.title: 6. Parse input and effects
docs.text:
Use multipart field file with a nonempty filename and body, or JSON:

{"file_name":"synthetic.ddd","ddd_base64":"AA=="}

This is a shape example, not a valid DDD fixture. JSON file_name defaults to drivercard.ddd. Multipart takes precedence when file is present. The handler creates and removes a temporary file and writes diagnostics. It does not return a new import/archive identity or an idempotency receipt. content_base64 and a submitted archive_id do not implement the formerly described import contract. raw contains generation and activity-day data; do not assume a response excludes every original parsed field.

docs.title: 7. Read example
docs.text:
GET /api/drivercard/activities?date_from=2026-10-01&date_to=2026-10-02&card_number=1000

The card filter above is a partial LIKE filter. Day/week endpoints derive views from existing intervals. Parsing bytes through this endpoint does not populate those database read endpoints.

docs.title: 8. Errors
docs.text: Successful handlers return 200. Driver routes return 401/authentication_required when the Bearer header is absent, 403/access_denied for an invalid/revoked/expired or no-longer-authorized session, 403/local_access_required for non-loopback traffic and 503/authorization_unavailable if authorization cannot be checked. A valid token does not override the loopback requirement. Responses use no-store; successful results are rechecked before emission so revocation during work discards the body. Parse rejects missing filename, missing/empty content and invalid Base64 with {"ok":false,"error":"..."} and 400; parser exceptions return 500 with this error envelope. Read filter ValueError returns 400; other repository/analysis failures return 500. The upload limit is now 128 MiB; exceeding it returns 413/upload_too_large. There is no parse 409/422 contract. Standard framework routing errors can have a different body. Clients must not require a separate message property.

docs.title: 9. Compatibility and acceptance
docs.text:
The bundled browser week view uses an authenticated local proxy. REST credentials stay in the desktop/server process; the browser receives a separate HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie after a capability exchange. Proxy POSTs require its exact origin. Health proxy routing resolves /health, and cached preload data remains subject to current authorization. Upstream redirects and environment HTTP proxies are disabled; CSP restricts scripts/connections to the same origin and prevents framing.

Preserve method/path, field names and filter semantics when integrating; anonymous callers must migrate before this source is released. Import-list statistics read the V2 activity observations while preserving activity_count/activity_from/activity_to and ordering. Check valid synthetic DDD, malformed/empty payloads, default and explicit filters, database results and timeline rendering against the intended build. Source inspection is not an executed HTTP, frozen-build or installed-service acceptance. No production data was used for this documentation review.

docs.title: 10. Related integration
docs.text: Mobile archive intake is documented separately in mobile integration. This page does not define future mobile deadline/history query endpoints.

docs.title: FleetMiraApi service
docs.text:
FleetMiraApi exposes FLEET Mira interfaces as an independent HTTPS service on the Enterprise server. Mobile apps and approved integrations can use a stable server address even when no desktop client is open.

Implementation and delivery status

This page describes the new development implementation for 1.1.0-beta9. An older installer does not automatically contain the component. The deployed installer must explicitly include FleetMiraApi. Source tests, installed server acceptance and Android-device testing are separate evidence.

docs.title: Function, purpose and use cases
docs.text:
The module hosts existing mobile, device, driver and telematics APIs and the configured traffic-offence portal. Shared business logic and PostgreSQL remain unchanged. It serves Android/future iOS apps, customer integrations and central network access.

FleetMiraApi checks HTTPS, hostnames, tokens, scopes, user permissions and licence grants. It answers short business requests directly; FleetMiraWorker continues processing mobile imports and other central background work. The API service replaces neither PostgreSQL nor the worker or archive service. Accounting export remains an outgoing connection rather than a new API receiver.

The desktop's local driver API retains its loopback session. Central driver access uses separate integration tokens and explicit global data access. Basic and Pro retain their existing local SQLite/worker composition; the independent server service belongs to Enterprise.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Mermaid diagram source 
flowchart TB
    Mobile["DTCO Android app"] -->|"HTTPS"| API["FleetMiraApi"]
    Integration["Approved integration"] -->|"HTTPS"| API
    Browser["Browser: /health"] -->|"HTTPS"| API
    API --> DB[("PostgreSQL: data and jobs")]
    API --> Logs["Rotating service log"]
    Admin["Enterprise administration"] --> DB
    DB --> Worker["FleetMiraWorker: jobs with leases"]
    Worker --> Processing["Import and background processing"]

API, worker and PostgreSQL can initially share one server. They remain separate processes and services. Distributing them later requires appropriately provisioning intake storage, portal secrets and certificates on the relevant hosts.

For Android sign-in, the app opens a protected browser tab, receives a single-use code after authentication and exchanges it with S256 PKCE for tokens. Access tokens last 15 minutes; refresh tokens renew them within a maximum 30-day app session. Administration issues user-bound integration tokens with explicit scopes and validity. See the operations guide.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Area Requirement Operating system An x64 Windows/Windows Server installation supported by Enterprise setup; the installer requires at least Windows version 10.0. Perform installed acceptance on the actual server version. Installation Enterprise application installer including component api; local administrator rights for installation and Windows service management. Database Reachable PostgreSQL with current Mira schema, application credentials and appropriate TLS configuration. Server setup uses PostgreSQL 17; regular schema migration requires the maintenance account. Background processing FleetMiraWorker using the same Enterprise database for imports and central jobs; archive functions additionally require a configured FleetMiraArchive service. Licence and users A valid central Enterprise entitlement with API access; active users with required business permissions. Administration requires users.manage and settings.manage. HTTPS and DNS A stable DNS name and matching valid certificate chain/private key; clients must trust the issuing CA. Storage Protected writable log/mobile intake directories. Defaults allow up to 1 GiB of logs, plus space for uploads, temporary files and business archives. Uploads are limited to 128 MiB per request. Resources Size CPU, RAM and I/O in addition to PostgreSQL/worker needs using actual concurrency. Source tests do not establish binding load or hardware approval. Software modules The complete Windows package bundles Python, pywin32, Flask, Cheroot with TLS, PostgreSQL drivers and shared business modules. No separate Python installation is required for the installed package. Optional zeroconf enables local service discovery.

The service uses NT SERVICE\FleetMiraApi. Setup configures automatic startup and crash recovery. The account needs read access to its configuration/TLS files and modify access to logs/mobile intake storage. Worker private licence/backup keys are not transferred to the API service.

docs.title: Network and firewall
docs.text:
Direction Connection Allowance Incoming to API server TCP 8443 as the setup default, or the explicitly configured API port Required client networks or the intended VPN/network access only. API/worker/Enterprise clients to database TCP 5432 or the configured PostgreSQL port Authorized application hosts to PostgreSQL only; no public database exposure. Optional local network DNS-SD/mDNS, UDP 5353 Only when local discovery is enabled; replaces neither HTTPS nor authentication and usually does not cross routed network boundaries. Outgoing as needed DNS, time synchronization and explicitly required device/external-system destinations Existing operational policy; licence verification and outgoing background connectors remain in the worker.

Setup does not automatically open an API port. Example restricted Windows firewall rule, to run in administrative PowerShell and adapt to your network:

New-NetFirewallRule -Name "FleetMiraApi-HTTPS" `
  -DisplayName "Fleet Mira API HTTPS" `
  -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 8443 `
  -Profile Domain,Private -RemoteAddress 192.168.10.0/24

192.168.10.0/24 is an example network. For a different port, align the rule, service configuration and client URL. To roll back, remove only your own rule: Remove-NetFirewallRule -Name "FleetMiraApi-HTTPS". Fix certificate warnings instead of disabling verification. A reverse proxy needs a separately approved TLS/trust configuration; arbitrary X-Forwarded-* headers do not prove HTTPS.

docs.title: Installation and configuration
docs.text:
1. Back up database/configuration and satisfy the general Enterprise prerequisites. Use an installer that actually includes the new API service.
  2. Select Fleet Mira API Windows service in server setup, adding Worker and optionally Client for co-location. An unattended example is /COMPONENTS=client,worker,api; provide database credentials through the protected /MIRACONFIG file, never a password in process arguments.
  3. Run regular PostgreSQL schema migration. PostgreSQL failure must never make the API create or use SQLite.
  4. Provision the certificate and key on the API server. Check DNS, certificate validity and service-account read permissions.
  5. In the Enterprise client, open Administration → Communication and integrations → API configuration. Enter, for example, https://fleet.example.internal:8443, the bind address, port 8443 and server certificate/key paths. Review log limits/permitted Android scopes and save.
  6. Open API service, select the instance and Reload. Without configuration the service remains UNCONFIGURED; a running Windows service alone does not prove an open HTTPS port.
  7. Create the required firewall rule and perform the browser test below from an intended client network.
  8. In API credentials, create integration tokens with owner, audience, scopes and validity, or connect the DTCO app through browser sign-in at its saved target. Never place tokens in URLs, screenshots or support logs.

Existing enabled mobile/telematics configurations can be adopted at first startup. Additional existing ports remain as compatibility listeners. Source files are not deleted. The operations guide explains adoption, permissions, revocation and rollback.

docs.title: Setup in the administration interface
docs.text: The administration interface belongs to the Enterprise client; it is not a public web dashboard. Sign in with an authorized user, expand Administration → Communication and integrations and open the required workspace. Sessions start with an empty workspace area; selecting a navigation entry opens its tab. These screenshots show the actual application components with isolated PostgreSQL example data. Adjust server names, paths and permissions to your installation.Click an image to open it at full resolution.

docs.title: Save the API configuration
docs.text:
• URL: the HTTPS address reachable by clients, including its port, for example https://fleet.example.internal:8443.
  • Server: the local bind address. 0.0.0.0 binds all IPv4 interfaces; the firewall restricts access to approved networks.
  • Port: must match the URL and firewall; the example uses 8443.
  • Certificate / Private key: absolute file paths on the API server. The certificate file contains the required certificate chain. The private key stays on the server and is never distributed to clients.
  • Logs: retention in days, file size and total budget in MiB. Example values are 30 days, 50 MiB and 1024 MiB.
  • Permissions / dtco-android: allowed scopes for browser-based app sign-in. Enable only required scopes; current user permissions further restrict access.

Save writes the central PostgreSQL configuration. Then select the instance under API service and choose Reload. Discard reloads saved values. When replacing certificates, also check file permissions, chain and validity. After saving, host validation accepts the host in the configured URL; do not assume alternate client addresses will work.

docs.title: Check the Windows service and API instance
docs.text:
The Windows service is named FleetMiraApi and starts automatically. On the server, inspect it using services.msc or the local FLEET Mira API shortcut. The central API service page shows the reported instance and its latest heartbeat. An old heartbeat does not prove the process is still running.

Action / indicator Use Refresh Load instances and their latest reported state from PostgreSQL. Diagnostics Send a diagnostics request to the selected running instance. RUNNING / listener_alive The listener was active at the latest heartbeat. Also perform the HTTPS check. UNCONFIGURED Configuration or TLS setup is missing; the Windows service can run without an HTTPS listener. licensed / logging_available Inspect the reported operating entitlement and logging availability. Pause API / Resume API Temporarily suspend or resume business requests. The public process check at /health/live does not test business readiness. DEBUG (15 min) Temporarily enable additional technical logging for troubleshooting. Reload Reload saved configuration, then check heartbeat and HTTPS.

These actions are processed as central requests. If the service is stopped or PostgreSQL is unavailable, use the local console or Windows service management. A successful database query does not replace a listener check.

docs.title: Set up user-bound API credentials
docs.text:
Under API credentials → Create token, select the active owner, a meaningful label, the correct API type (mobile, devices, telematics or drivercard), required scopes and validity of 1–365 days. Set customer IDs or All customers according to the intended business access; mobile tokens do not support customer restrictions through this field. Telematics requires explicit global access.

The token secret is displayed once after creation. Transfer it securely to the intended integration and store it as a secret there; never include it in URLs, documentation or screenshots. The searchable list shows metadata. To remove access, select the credential, choose Revoke token and confirm. This does not extend or renew existing tokens.

For the DTCO Android app, browser-based sign-in is the normal workflow: choose the server address in the app, start browser sign-in and authenticate with the intended Mira user. The app automatically obtains tokens through the PKCE code exchange and handles renewal. Manually copying an integration token is unnecessary. Android scopes, active user permissions and the registered callback address must match the configured app.

docs.title: Use logs for troubleshooting
docs.text: Under Logs, select the instance and choose Refresh. Refresh automatically retrieves new sanitized lines regularly while the page is visible. Search and severity filters narrow the display; Export saves the displayed lines as JSON Lines. First compare the timestamp, HTTP status and technical event code with the reported failure; briefly enable DEBUG if needed and check again. Never include tokens, passwords or keys in support material.

docs.title: Configure certificate trust on clients
docs.text: For a private enterprise or test CA, verify the fingerprint and distribute the public CA certificate through the approved device-management process. Windows browsers need it in the appropriate trusted root store; Android devices require the corresponding managed or user CA configuration. The DTCO app accepts system and user CAs. Both server certificate and CA must be valid; the requested DNS name or IP address must appear in the server certificate SAN. Never install the private server or CA key on clients. Repeat the browser health check and app connection after distribution.

docs.title: Fleet Mira Health in the browser
docs.text:
Open https://<Server>:8443/health. Fleet Mira Health is accessible without signing in and shows API, worker, PostgreSQL, current and last completed worker jobs, and resource measurements. The public view is English. Dark Material 3 is the default regardless of browser/system appearance; the appearance switch allows an explicit light selection, remembered in this browser.

Area Meaning API / worker / PostgreSQL State with icon, readable text and code; host, version and latest heartbeat. API heartbeats older than 45 seconds and worker heartbeats older than 60 seconds are out of date. Worker jobs Current and last completed job per worker with type, state, start, end and duration; queued/running counts. No payloads, user names or file names. Host Total/used RAM, CPU usage, logical and physical cores. Shared hosts are grouped. Service process and disk Process RAM, process CPU and available cores; total, used and free capacity on the disk containing that service's data directory. Process CPU: 100% represents one fully used logical core. Database Size of the actual connected PostgreSQL database. This does not measure free disk space on a remote database server.

API and worker use bundled psutil outside browser requests, at most every ten seconds, and publish measurements through their heartbeats. Each sample identifies its time and host/service. Missing measurements are unavailable and old samples are marked. Operating-system metrics for a remote PostgreSQL host are not collected without a measurement source there. No additional firewall rule is needed.

The visible page updates every ten seconds without resetting focus or scroll position. Selecting text pauses updates. Refresh updates manually. During a database outage the public page remains accessible and shows the failure and available local API reports with their age. ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED instead means no listener is responding: check the service and local console.

The desktop view has three large columns in this order: FleetMiraWorker, FleetMiraApi, PostgreSQL. Each service area combines its state and process measurements; database size is shown directly under PostgreSQL. Below are Server information with host and disk measurements and Jobs with queue counts and current/last jobs. Narrow screens stack these areas vertically.

docs.title: PostgreSQL performance and Fleet Mira record totals
docs.text:
The PostgreSQL area additionally shows version, SELECT 1 response time, connections to the current database, visible active connections, server-wide connections, configured connection limit, cache hit ratio, transactions per second and deadlocks since the displayed statistics reset. Response time measures the query on an existing connection; transaction rate is averaged between two valid samples. After service start or a statistics reset, the rate is initially unavailable. The cache ratio describes PostgreSQL buffer access, not the operating-system cache. See the PostgreSQL documentation for statistics semantics and access rights.

The separate Fleet Mira: total records card sits immediately below Jobs in the lower right column. On narrow screens it also follows the jobs card directly. The PostgreSQL column contains database status, size and performance only. The records card counts exact table rows:

Display Source Vehicles fleet_vehicle, including archived vehicles Personnel fleet_person, including archived personnel records; not user accounts DDD archives ddd_archive, including soft-deleted archives; not individual tachograph facts Licence checks fleet_license_check, stored check events including negative results; not due dates Cost entries fleet_vehicle_cost_entry, including drafts, credits, reversals and archived entries; record counts rather than monetary totals

The API heartbeat collects performance at most every 30 seconds and record totals at most every 60 seconds. Browser refresh does not initiate extra measurement queries. Connections and queries are time-bounded and read-only. Measurement errors affect displayed telemetry, not service operation. The API database user requires SELECT access to the five counted tables. No broader monitoring role is granted automatically. If other sessions' states are hidden, the active-session count is explicitly unavailable. Only aggregates, sample times and freshness are exposed; no names, query text or amounts are returned.

docs.title: Protected logs
docs.text:
Connection opening to the local archive service tolerates temporarily missing or busy named-pipe instances within a five-second total deadline. Only opening is retried. Trust verification and the archive request then execute once; failures after sending do not automatically replay that archive call. Persistent service unavailability remains an error and uses bounded job retries. Signatures, independent checkpoints and permissions are not relaxed.

Under Jobs, the public view shows only the historical total of terminal failures and the last failed job with its type and finish time. It exposes no failure list, attempts, error codes or causes. After administrator sign-in, the ten latest failure cases including queued retries appear below the logs, with allowlisted codes and readable guidance. Payloads, user/file names and raw errors remain excluded. Neither restarts nor queue cleanup reset the failure total. Ready still describes service availability.

Automatic current-state checks are coalesced into one queued or running job per type and exact parameter set. A shared database lock also protects concurrent worker planners. This covers archive evidence checks, intake cleanup, mailbox/notification sweeps, backup retention, automatic download checks per task and approved GPS polls per connection. Explicit effective dates, individual vehicle/file requests, manual commands, backup creation and dated invoice processing remain independent. Different tasks or connections are never mixed. The next normal planning pass catches subsequent changes.

Cleanup retains every record. Only never-attempted, explicitly recognised redundant routine wake-ups can become CANCELLED with PERIODIC_SUPERSEDED. The newest queued entry in a group is kept; existing running or attempted work is protected instead. Failures, retries, leases and unknown parameters are unchanged. Preview writes no business data; applying cleanup is repeatable. Every worker planning the same database must use the updated version.

Missing or unreadable GPS keys require protected provisioning on the worker and a successful connection test. The connection becomes ACTION_REQUIRED, pausing periodic requests. Secret-store and archive-integrity failures are not retried automatically. Network failures retain bounded retries. Already queued scheduled downloads no longer execute disabled tasks. Failure history and archive checkpoints are neither deleted nor reset.

Sign in opens /health/login. Only an active Mira administrator with users.manage, settings.manage, local sign-in enabled and any mandatory password change completed can access up to 30 sanitized recent log entries. Integration tokens do not replace this sign-in. Afterwards the user's profile language and region apply; sessions expire after 30 minutes or Sign out. Account status and permissions are checked on every request. If the identity store fails, only the public view remains visible.

HTTP redirects such as 303 are redirects, not failed requests. Error codes receive understandable guidance. Images show the actual interfaces with isolated PostgreSQL example data.

For technical process checks, /health/live remains public. Non-HTML requests to /health retain the minimal JSON response for compatibility. Process liveness alone confirms neither licensing nor worker readiness. Service control and token administration retain their existing authorization requirements.

docs.title: Public reachability check
docs.text:
The small unauthenticated process check remains available for monitoring and an initial HTTPS test:

https://fleet.example.internal:8443/health/live

{"ok":true,"service":"FleetMiraApi"}

This confirms HTTPS and a responding process. It does not confirm a valid license, current worker heartbeat or business readiness. Non-HTML requests to /health retain this minimal JSON response for compatibility. Requests to /api/devices without a token must return HTTP 401 when business operation is enabled; HTTP 503 is not a successful business test. Write/import tests belong in an approved isolated test environment.

docs.title: Diagnose a stopped API service
docs.text:
On the server, open FLEET Mira API from the Start menu or run DLTNGDownloadTool.exe --api-console. The console displays separate API and worker cards, readable state descriptions, process IDs, the last Windows error code and recent sanitized API events. It refreshes every five seconds. For stopped or pending local services, the directly queried Windows state takes precedence over an old database heartbeat. A running process without a current heartbeat is not shown as business-ready.

Start service is available for a stopped API service; Stop service is available for a running service. Appropriate Windows rights are required. Permission failures produce a readable message. This local console has no authenticated Mira user and therefore uses English; central Enterprise administration uses the signed-in user's language. The image shows a running example service, not a control operation against production data.

Observation Next check Connection refused / Windows service stopped Open the local console, inspect the error code and logs, fix the cause and start the API service. Timeout Check routing, bind address and firewall access. Certificate warning Correct CA trust, SAN/server name, validity and certificate chain. Not configured Check certificate/key files, service account read permissions, port and saved configuration. Out-of-date worker heartbeat Check FleetMiraWorker on the server and its database connection. Sign-in fails Check active account, local sign-in, required password change and administrator permissions. License unavailable Check the central Enterprise license and worker license validation. HTTP 400 Use the configured server address and an allowed hostname.

docs.title: Monitoring, logs and troubleshooting
docs.text:
API service provides diagnose, pause/resume, bounded debug mode and reload. API credentials manages owners, grants, validity and revocation. Logs provides search, severity filtering, automatic refresh and sanitized row export. By default, logs/api/api.jsonl rotates daily and at 50 MiB; retention is at most 30 days with a 1024 MiB total budget. Debug mode ends after 15 minutes.

When API or database is unavailable, use the local FLEET Mira API shortcut or DLTNGDownloadTool.exe --api-console. It inspects the Windows service and protected local logs; start/stop requires appropriate Windows rights. A completely stopped remote service cannot start itself through its own HTTP endpoint.

docs.title: Mobile fleet, download reminders and historical activities
docs.text: Implemented in the development source tree, extending mobile intake for Pro (SQLite, in-process worker) and Enterprise (PostgreSQL, FleetMiraWorker). Basic has no mobile listener; Enterprise Client performs no central evaluation. Installed release acceptance remains a separate gate.

docs.title: Access and known consumers
docs.text:
Regular migration adds component mobile_fleet version 1 and durable table mobile_fleet_request. The existing configured mobile HTTPS listener hosts these routes. Each call requires an active user, valid revocable Bearer token, current role rights and product entitlement. Scope fleet.read requires permissions fleet.read and archive.read; history additionally requires scope history.read and permission compliance.dashboard.read. Existing upload tokens acquire no new scopes automatically.

python mobile_admin.py --data-root C:\ProgramData\FleetMira --administrator ADMIN create-token --label Android-Fleet --fleet --read-only --days 365

Without --read-only, --fleet adds to existing upload scopes. This local CLI requires interactive administrator authentication. Secrets are displayed once and must not enter documentation or logs.

Confirmed consumer: Android DTCO Download 0.5.0-dev onward, FleetHttpsApi/FleetReadWorker. Internal consumers: Pro worker tick and Enterprise dispatcher job mobile_fleet_read. Evidence: test_mobile_fleet.py and Android FleetLiveInstrumentedTest. Other external consumers are unknown; missing references do not prove absence of use.

docs.title: Endpoints below /api/mobile/v1/fleet
docs.text:
Method / path Purpose / response Changes and permissions GET /capabilities Product/API/contract version 1, server/user identity, token expiry, features, historyZone, page size 100, maximum 31 days No business change; fleet/archive rights and fleet.read POST /requests JSON {"kind":"FLEET"} or {"kind":"HISTORY","personId":"…","from":"YYYY-MM-DD","to":"YYYY-MM-DD"}; Idempotency-Key; 202 with ID Durable token-owned request; four outstanding requests per token; HISTORY requires additional rights GET /requests/{id} QUEUED, RUNNING, COMPLETE, FAILED, error code, metadata, collection counts, expiry Owner token and still-valid rights; no business change GET /requests/{id}/pages?collection=drivers&offset=0&limit=100 Immutable page: id, collection, offset, items, total, nextOffset Owner token, still-valid rights, completed result

FLEET collections: vehicles, drivers, deadlines. HISTORY: days, weeks, activities, findings, sources. Inclusive dates allow at most 31 days through today in the analysis time zone. Driver assignments must be confirmed and unambiguous. Responses omit addresses, birth dates, secrets and internal archive paths. History includes required card/source identifiers, technical rule codes and existing engine notices.

HTTP: 426 without HTTPS; 403 for missing/revoked access or entitlement; 404 for unknown/other-token IDs; 409 for invalid contracts, idempotency conflict or incomplete results; 410 expired results; 413 above 4096 request bytes; 429 full queue. Responses use Cache-Control: no-store; results expire after one day. Codes include ACCESS_REVOKED, FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE, SUBJECT_AMBIGUOUS, SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND, RESULT_TOO_LARGE, EVALUATION_FAILED. Expired leases resume after restart; late former workers cannot overwrite newer results.

docs.title: Business meaning
docs.text:
Snapshots include the authorized company's entire active vehicle and driver/personnel inventory, including unlinked personnel. Existing managed download deadlines and confirmed archives are reused. Reads neither create nor modify business deadlines. Missing, outdated and conflicting assignments remain unresolved. Untracked vehicles receive no invented deadline; leadDays=0 remains zero days. Deadlines use UTC like the existing deadline service. Historical analysis uses the configured Fleet Mira time zone.

History reuses ComplianceEvaluationService, trusted archives, modules, rules and evaluation audits. Day/ISO-week totals use the same normalizer. DST days have 23/25 hours; unknown time and gaps are not rest. Cards and generations remain distinct. Activities are clipped to the selected period; rule findings may retain explanatory context from the existing evaluation. This is a historical technical precheck, not a live remaining-driving-time counter.

docs.title: Android: primary server, cache and reminders
docs.text:
Settings select one active Fleet Mira target as primary server; other upload targets remain. Fleet provides local vehicles plus remote vehicles, drivers and deadlines. Drivers open day/week/activity/assessment/source views. Manual refresh complements approximately six-hour background synchronization; Android can delay execution. Wi-Fi is default, mobile data is configurable per target. A local WLAN without Internet is explicitly bound. USB sessions take priority.

Each binding has a random cache generation. Complete pages are staged and atomically published together; interruption cannot replace a complete snapshot. Server/account/token changes, known access withdrawal, expiry and disabling block/remove remote data, preserving local original DDD files and vehicle histories. Retention is at most 30 days, ten historical periods and a 64 MiB remote-payload budget; database files can be larger because of indexes/WAL. Views show their saved timestamp; revocation cannot be learned while disconnected.

Reminders require opt-in and Android notification permission. From 09:00 UTC daily summaries cover due/upcoming downloads and unresolved tracked download states, using only server dates and lead times. The phone contains no statutory intervals. Snapshots older than 24 hours or known access loss do not trigger new reminders. The server generation timestamp also counts; resuming a download later does not make old results fresh again. Notifications contain counts only and open deadlines; Android power saving may delay them.

docs.title: Impact and evidence
docs.text:
Four additive routes and scopes; existing device/parser/upload/diagnostic endpoint protection is unchanged. Old servers require an update. New clients need the updated server and explicit token grants. Fallback: unselect the primary server and disable the listener through the existing operational procedure. Original archives remain; do not start older software against the upgraded schema.

Reviewed baseline: working sources dated 4 November 2026: mobile_fleet.py, mobile_integration.py, mobile_api.py, worker_runtime.py, database_runtime.py, tachograph_compliance.py, ddd_drivercard_compliance_561.py, time_basis.py. Dated artifacts/test-reports record actual tests and remaining release gates. Existing security gaps remain assigned to separate project-specific impact analyses.

docs.title: Shared action ribbons
docs.text: FLEET Mira retains its dashboard, left IconNavbar and right work tabs. ui_actions.py provides edition-neutral ActionBar, ActionButton, ActionDefinition and FormFooter components. Administration uses these through its existing compatible classes. Business permissions, validation and signal connections remain with each workspace.

docs.title: Interaction contract
docs.text:
• Buttons display a shared vector icon at 24 logical pixels, visible text and a translated tooltip. Minimum height is 40 logical pixels; font metrics and operating-system scaling determine the required width.
  • Create, Open/Edit and Duplicate appear on the left, followed by workflow actions and Import/Export. Destructive actions appear separately at the end of the left groups. Refresh stays on the right.
  • Group captions describe Record, Actions, Import/Export and View. No additional ribbon-tab level is introduced.
  • A subtle continuous outer border encloses both buttons and group captions.
  • Group captions use grey text (#a6a6a6) and are centered beneath the complete visible group. Dividers use the same grey (#a6a6a6), are one logical pixel wide, span the button and caption height and separate adjacent groups on the same row; wrapping never creates dividers between rows. Captions and dividers are visual only and do not take keyboard focus. Form footers have neither group captions nor dividers.
  • At narrow widths, secondary actions move into More actions. Primary actions remain directly available and may wrap onto additional rows. A menu entry invokes the existing button; selection state, license visibility, checked state and submenus are preserved.
  • Form footers remain outside scrolling content. Save is rightmost; Discard or Cancel precedes it. Cancel ends a dialog; Discard restores form changes.
  • All text and state explanations use the shared catalogue for 25 languages. Region affects formatting only.

docs.title: Adopted workspaces
docs.text:
Administration adopts the contract through AdministrationActionBar and AdministrationFormFooter. Shared ribbons also cover the lease overview and detail, finance master data, costs and supplier invoices, record documents, personnel and vehicle master data, deadline types and actions, traffic-offence actions, driving-license evaluation, record exports, standard-driver assignment, device actions, the tachograph archive and report output. Dashboard actions and localized standard-dialog actions receive the same icons and minimum heights.

User management separates search, ribbon, table and status. Search and Refresh have technical IDs; refreshing retains the selected user ID while it remains visible. Shared Fleet grids also retain selection and scroll position when their models change, without taking input focus.

Application settings use FormEditState: saving requires changes, a valid advertisement URL and the existing permission. Discard restores the loaded form state. Automatic refresh does not overwrite pending edits. Closing the tab, signing out or exiting offers Save, Discard and Continue editing. Failed saving does not permit closing. A change of authenticated user does not carry over the previous user's form edits.

docs.title: Technical contracts and verification
docs.text:
The application-wide rollout attaches through apply_action_presentation() when a widget tree is translated or opened. ui_action_catalog.py registers label aliases, technical function identities, presentation roles and explicit exceptions for contextual widgets. ui_action_symbols.py draws the vector motifs. Equivalent functions share a motif; distinct functions receive distinct motifs. Translated word fragments and random hash patterns are not used for assignment.

Contextual functions receive their unambiguous assignment through the technical widget ID from their first construction in the authenticated user's language. For example, trafficOffenceCaseClose registers the existing case/close motif: the English caption “Close case” can represent multiple German sources and therefore does not determine this business function. Regressions inspect the actual traffic action bar in all 25 initial languages and after subsequent language changes; captions, permissions and callbacks remain unchanged.

Existing action rows are adopted with their original buttons. Search and filter fields precede the ribbon; field actions and step/time navigation retain their positions. Existing save, discard, validation and permission flows remain owned by the workspace. The rollout does not introduce a blanket save transaction or global form validation. Existing persistent form footers remain in place. The rollout report lists the covered program points and acceptance limits.

The cursor policy in ui_common.py, installed at application startup, replaces direct or inherited text-entry cursors on non-editable surfaces with the arrow cursor, including buttons, navigation, tabs, labels and read-only text views. Global text-cursor overrides are removed so individual widgets can display their appropriate cursor again. Text selection and copying remain available. Editable fields retain their text-entry cursor; changing read-only or enabled state updates the cursor. Link, hand, resize and wait cursors remain intact. The policy also covers subsequently opened dialogs and their text viewports.

Filters attach directly to widgets. The main window registers during construction; newly activated windows are attached through their own widget trees in a deferred callback. Background events are not filtered and Qt-wide widget registries are not traversed.

Ordinary interaction surfaces receive an explicit arrow cursor, reapplied on entry even when QWidget.cursor() already reports an arrow. This lets Qt update its native cursor representation again. Regression tests verify that repeated assignment and preserve special interaction cursors. Windows acceptance must also inspect the actual operating-system cursor: the screen-capture output used for diagnosis showed an arrow while Windows reported a text-entry cursor over buttons and the empty workspace. A passing offscreen test or the pointer drawn in a capture alone therefore does not establish a successful native correction.

Leasing actions use explicit semantic icon keys: Activate shows a play triangle inside a circle, End a finish flag, and Terminate early a calendar with a cancellation cross. Documents have a folded corner; invoice receipts have a serrated lower edge. Plus signs, chain links and repeat arrows distinguish adding, linking and recurring invoices. Costs/credits show coins with a plus sign. Open uses a document with an outgoing arrow; Export an arrow leaving a tray. Explicit icon keys survive language changes and overflow menus. Raster checks ensure distinct motifs at 100, 125 and 150 percent scaling.

Action definitions include a key, role, source label, tooltip source, icon motif and optional shortcut. Existing widgets can be explicitly assigned a role and adopted; business permissions are never inferred from labels at runtime. sharedActionRole, sharedActionBar, sharedFormFooter and destructiveAction supplement existing Administration properties and widget IDs.

Tests cover ordering, overflow, callbacks, license visibility, language switching, keyboard navigation and destruction of pending layout timers. Pilot workflows run against SQLite and an explicitly marked disposable PostgreSQL test host. Installed Enterprise acceptance inspects ribbons semantically and performs a settings Discard round trip without persisting configuration.

docs.title: Consistent administration UI
docs.text:
The shared graphical presentation, overflow menu and form edit states are specified in the action ribbon contract.

Administration pages use the shared structural contract from administration_ui.py. Business logic, permissions, and edition separation remain independent of this presentation contract. As in Fleet Management, an IconNavbar on the left shows functional groups as parent nodes and Administration pages as child nodes. A child opens one closable and movable work tab on the right. An already open page is focused instead of duplicated, and a new login starts with an empty workspace.

Functional group Administration pages Operations Sources, Tasks, Telematics, Backups Users and security Users, Single sign-on, Roles and permissions, Tachograph trust, Rule sets Communication and integrations Notifications, AI connector, Traffic offences Finance and system Cost analysis, Receipts/Documents, Settings, Audit log, Logs, Raw configuration

Administration and Fleet Management use the same recursive context-menu behavior. Expandable nodes show the fixed pairs Expand/Collapse item, Expand/Collapse group, and Expand/Collapse all. A leaf shows group and all; empty space only shows all. Actions that do not apply remain visible and disabled. Group actions always affect the complete subtree of the top-level parent. Expansion and splitter width are stored per user.

Group and page titles, tooltips, context menus, open work tabs, functional subtabs, and Pro badges are translated together into the authenticated user's language. English is used before authentication. Region changes only date, number, currency, and similar formatting, never navigation labels. The persisted navigation/admin page key remains compatible but does not automatically open a page at session start. Inaccessible pages remain visible as disabled children, explicitly licence-hidden pages remain hidden, and groups without an accessible page remain visible but disabled.

Table and tree views use stable logical column identifiers and the shared per-user UI-state store for SQLite and PostgreSQL. On a profile change, only pending edits are saved to the previous profile in their edit order. Unchanged parallel views sharing a key must not overwrite its state. Explicit saves and resets discard older pending changes of that key while retaining later edits. Changes made before authentication or without a valid model are discarded. The column menu marks only an actual visibility choice as an edit; cancellation and reset cannot cause a delayed restoration of an older layout. Its reset action uses the existing reviewed translation key in all 25 languages.

Each page is marked as list management, settings form, operational/status, read-only, or tab container. List pages show introduction, filters, action bar, data grid, and status in that order. Forms organize related fields in named sections and keep their form footer visible outside scrollable content.

Action bars place Create, Open/Edit, Duplicate, workflow actions, and destructive actions on the left. Refresh is always on the right. Form footers always place Save/Apply at the far right. Destructive actions are technically marked, use object-specific labels, and require confirmation when they change data.

Selection-dependent actions are disabled without an applicable record. Double-click performs the same open or edit operation as the corresponding button. Pages, sections, action bars, form footers, important grids, and actions have stable technical widget IDs for tests and Enterprise acceptance.

The permitted hierarchy has exactly three levels: IconNavbar parent, child work tab, and at most one functional subtab level inside a page. Functional subtabs are reserved for at least two independent peer workflows; semantic groups structure fields inside a workflow.

docs.title: Asynchronous UI, lazy tabs and background services
1. Design rules
docs.text:
The Qt event loop must remain responsive while SQLite queries, backups, signature verification and tachograph processing run. Three rules enforce this:

  1. The Qt main thread constructs and changes widgets/models only.
  2. Database, file, network and CPU work runs in workers or dedicated services.
  3. Invisible workspaces and detail tabs are constructed and loaded only when needed.
flowchart LR
    U["User input"] --> Q["Qt main thread"]
    Q --> L["Lazy-tab factory"]
    Q --> J["UiJobController"]
    J --> R["Read pool: 4"]
    J --> W["Write lane: 1"]
    J --> P["Prefetch lane: 1"]
    R --> D["Worker-owned SQLite connection"]
    W --> D
    P --> D
    D --> C["DTO / list / dictionary"]
    C --> Q
    B["Background services"] --> A["Activity registry"]
    J --> A
    A --> S["Status bar"]
    H["UI heartbeat"] --> S

docs.title: 2. Startup order
docs.text:
The application applies a pending restore, runs central versioned database bootstrap, opens runtime repositories with ensure_schema=False, installs UiJobController and UiHeartbeatMonitor, creates the window, authenticates the user, loads only the visible start view and then starts background services.

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as QApplication
    participant Restore as Pending restore
    participant Bootstrap as DB bootstrap
    participant Jobs as UiJobController
    participant Window as MainWindow
    participant Services as Background services

    App->>Restore: Verify marker and atomically replace if present
    App->>Bootstrap: Configure WAL and run migrations once
    Bootstrap-->>App: quick_check = ok
    App->>Jobs: Install pools and heartbeat
    App->>Window: Build UI without runtime DDL
    Window->>Services: Start timers, backup and optional REST
    Window->>Jobs: Load visible view only

docs.title: 3. Lazy tabs
docs.text:
FileWidget._add_lazy_tab() stores a lightweight placeholder and factory. On currentChanged, the previous page is asked to cancel_load(), a QSignalBlocker prevents recursion, the factory creates the real widget, and the placeholder is replaced at the same index. ensure_loaded() then starts one data job if required.

Vehicle deadlines, costs, invoices, tachograph references, M files, activities, events, speed, technical data, calibrations, positions and audit are lazy. Constructors must not perform large queries. Each page should provide a stable job key, ensure_loaded() and cancel_load().

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Placeholder
    Placeholder --> Constructing: tab activated
    Constructing --> LoadedWidget: factory completes
    LoadedWidget --> LoadingData: ensure_loaded / refresh
    LoadingData --> Ready: current job succeeds
    LoadingData --> Cancelled: tab changed or closed
    Cancelled --> LoadingData: activated again
    Ready --> LoadingData: refresh
    Ready --> Disposed: record rebuilt

docs.title: 4. UiJobController
docs.text:
A UiJobSpec defines a stable key, visible name, work(token, report), lane, priority and metadata. Read jobs use a four-thread pool. Writes are serialised through one worker. Prefetch has one worker.

Submitting the same key cancels the previous token and increments a generation. Signals are delivered only when handle, generation and key are still current. Destroying the owner cancels its token, so an old slow result cannot update a new or closed view.

JobProgress reports text, phase and optional current/total. JobResult includes request ID, duration and metadata such as wait time, phase time, record count and cache hit. Workers return thread-neutral values only; no widget, model or other QObject may cross the worker boundary.

sequenceDiagram
    participant View
    participant Controller as UiJobController
    participant Pool as Worker pool
    participant DB as SQLite

    View->>Controller: submit(key, next generation)
    Controller->>Controller: cancel old token for key
    Controller->>Pool: start QRunnable
    Pool->>DB: open connection in worker
    DB-->>Pool: rows / DTOs
    Pool->>Controller: success(request_id, result)
    Controller->>Controller: validate key, generation and token
    Controller-->>View: emit only current result
    View->>View: update model in Qt thread

docs.title: 4.4 Shared table-controller lifetime
docs.text:
UserTableStateController is a Qt child of its table or tree view; its timer is a child of the controller. The controller obtains its view through parent() and retains no additional reverse Python reference to the view. The existing _user_table_state_controller reference on the view remains available for shared binding and reuse.

A view with a Qt parent remains valid until that owner is released. Afterwards the view, controller and timer are invalid; the event filter and profile switch must handle this state safely. An unparented view should be released on the Qt main thread when its last user reference disappears, rather than through later cyclic collection in a worker.

The two lifetime regressions check native release and Qt parent ownership without a database or worker. Only the short unit comparison of immediate release saves and restores the previous automatic GC state; the application does not change its GC policy. This check identifies no specific object from an earlier hang and does not replace an unchanged context or full test run.

docs.title: 4.5 Controlled UTC time in UI tests
docs.text:
Time-dependent UI tests must use the same controlled calendar day for test data and business evaluation. The traffic-offence deadline test covers the UTC instants 2026-10-05T23:59:59+00:00 and 2026-10-06T00:00:01+00:00; its due date is derived from each UTC instant. The test environment's local day boundary therefore cannot change the expected deadline evaluation.

The test uses monkeypatch to replace only the datetime binding in fleet_management; the binding is restored after each case. Production time calculations, all 17 business assertions and the existing five-second waits remain unchanged. The controlled clock replaces neither real repository evaluation nor asynchronous UI refresh.

docs.title: 5. Worker database pattern
docs.text:
Every worker opens and closes its own connection through the shared runtime factory. Connections are never passed from the UI thread. Schema changes belong to startup bootstrap only.

def work(token, report):
    token.throw_if_cancelled()
    repo = VehicleUnitRepository(db_path, ensure_schema=False)
    report(JobProgress("Loading calibrations", phase="query"))
    rows = repo.list_vehicle_facts("ddd_vu_calibration", vehicle_id, lower, upper, limit, offset)
    token.throw_if_cancelled()
    return [dict(row) for row in rows]

Write jobs commit in the write lane and trigger a new read job only after commit. Filters are captured before worker submission, and large result sets are paginated.

docs.title: 6. Background services and status
docs.text:
BackgroundActivityRegistry is a thread-safe map from stable task key to display text and optional progress. Every service must clear its entry in finally. The status bar polls at 400 ms and prioritises shutdown, active/recent UI stall, background work, transient messages and finally Background: ready.

The BackupCoordinator owns one daemon thread and one non-reentrant run lock. A cycle handles small batches: up to 5 tachograph archives, 20 local financial migrations, 20 financial backups, 10 REST export retries and 50 remote presence checks, plus a due database snapshot. Backup progress pauses in 100-ms increments while a user write job is waiting. SQLite backup uses small page batches; network transfer and read-back occur outside functional transactions.

The scheduler and notification timer runs every 30 seconds. Notification delivery uses a non-blocking lock and daemon worker. Scheduled tasks and the DriverCard REST API run in dedicated threads. Signature re-verification and deadline reconciliation use the serial write lane.

flowchart TD
    A["Service starts"] --> B["Activity registry: set"]
    B --> C{"User write waiting?"}
    C -->|"Yes, backup"| D["Wait briefly and expose status"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Process bounded batch"]
    D --> C
    E --> F["Keep DB transaction short"]
    F --> G["Network/read-back outside transaction"]
    G --> H{"More work?"}
    H -->|"Yes"| E
    H -->|"No/error"| I["Activity registry: clear in finally"]

docs.title: 7. UI heartbeat and UI_STALL
docs.text:
A Qt timer beats every 250 ms. A separate watcher marks UI_STALL after one second without a beat and logs additional main-thread stack samples after 5, 15 and 30 seconds. The log includes delay, active jobs/background tasks and a compact main-thread stack. Recovery is logged on the next beat.

The heartbeat diagnoses blocking; it does not make blocking code asynchronous. A stack ending in SQLite, file or network code in the main thread must be moved to a worker.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Responsive
    Responsive --> Stalled: no beat for 1 s
    Stalled --> Stalled: stack samples at 5/15/30 s
    Stalled --> Recovered: next Qt beat
    Recovered --> Responsive: retention expires

docs.title: 8. Controlled shutdown
docs.text:
System and tray exits share one idempotent path. Normal status timers are stopped and the visible shutdown sequence is: stop scheduler/notification timer, stop DriverCard REST, stop backup coordinator, hide tray, display completion, cancel UiJobs, wait for pools for a bounded period, stop heartbeat, then close Qt.

sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant UI as MainWindow
    participant REST as DriverCard REST
    participant Backup as BackupCoordinator
    participant Jobs as UiJobController
    participant App as QApplication

    User->>UI: Exit
    UI->>UI: Lock shutdown status and stop timers
    UI->>REST: stop()
    UI->>Backup: stop(timeout)
    UI->>Jobs: cancel tokens and clear queues
    Jobs->>Jobs: bounded waitForDone
    UI->>App: close

docs.title: 9. Troubleshooting and acceptance
docs.text:
Search app.log for UI_STALL, inspect main_stack, correlate active task names and follow the same request ID through UI_JOB start/success/failed/cancelled. Verify that repositories use ensure_schema=False, result sets are bounded, cancellation is checked between phases and no UI callback performs blocking I/O.

A new page or service is accepted only when construction and tab switching perform no substantial main-thread query, stale results are ignored, worker connections are thread-owned, writes are serial and committed before refresh, activity state is always cleared, shutdown remains idempotent, and navigation remains responsive during parallel backup load.

docs.title: 1. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This document is the technical reference for the SQLite database format used by FLEET Mira storage format V2. It covers the physical database contract, versioned bootstrap, the normalized tachograph fact model, provenance and deduplication, the surrounding business schemas, integrity rules, migration from the legacy format, and supported operational access.

The schema is an internal application contract. Integrations must use the documented application services and APIs for writes. Read-only SQL is useful for diagnostics and controlled reporting, but direct inserts, updates, deletes, schema changes, or trigger changes are unsupported because they can bypass audit, hash verification, derived-data refresh, and migration bookkeeping.

Related documents:

  • Tachograph data parsing, storage and access
  • Asynchronous UI and background services
  • Archiving, backup and restore

docs.title: 2. V2 invariants
docs.text:
Storage format V2 is identified by all of the following conditions:

  1. app_schema_state.storage_format is 2.
  2. ddd_archive has the integer surrogate key archive_pk in addition to the stable public text ID id.
  3. The normalized fact core (ddd_fact_kind, ddd_fact, ddd_fact_source, and all typed payload tables) is complete.
  4. Required fact and card/time indexes exist.
  5. No legacy archive-owned fact table listed by the migration map remains in the database.
  6. The stored schema fingerprint matches the SQL definitions of the V2 archive, fact, payload, and fact-index objects.

The bootstrap rejects a populated ddd_archive table without archive_pk. A legacy database must therefore be rebuilt with the dedicated V2 migration; it is never upgraded in place by normal application startup.

flowchart LR
    S["SQLite file"] --> M["app_schema_state"]
    M --> F{"storage_format = 2"}
    F --> A["ddd_archive.archive_pk"]
    F --> C["normalized fact core"]
    F --> I["required indexes"]
    F --> H["schema fingerprint"]
    A --> V["validate_storage_schema"]
    C --> V
    I --> V
    H --> V

docs.title: 3. Physical SQLite configuration
docs.text:
Setting Runtime value Rationale Page size 8 KiB for newly created databases Reduces B-tree depth and page overhead for the fact store. Journal mode WAL during application runtime Allows readers to continue while the serialized write lane commits. synchronous NORMAL WAL durability/performance balance. Busy timeout 30,000 ms Gives bounded concurrent work time to finish instead of immediately returning SQLITE_BUSY. WAL auto-checkpoint 1,000 pages Bounds WAL growth during ordinary operation. Foreign keys Enabled on every application connection Enforces declared relationships and cascades. Auto-vacuum INCREMENTAL on a new database Permits controlled space reclamation.

The distributable empty database is finalized as a compact single file in DELETE journal mode and vacuumed. Application startup switches it to WAL. The -wal and -shm files are therefore normal runtime companions and must be included in shutdown/checkpoint planning, but not copied independently as a database backup.

PRAGMA user_version is not the migration authority. FLEET Mira uses component rows in app_schema_migration and format state in app_schema_state.

docs.title: 4. Versioned bootstrap
docs.text:
bootstrap_database() is the only supported schema initialization entry point. It runs before the UI and background services construct repositories. Each component migration is recorded once with component, version, UTC application time, and duration.

Component Current bootstrap version Schema owner archive 2 archive metadata, transfer state, and global audit dependencies authentication 1 users, roles, permissions, login security, and UI state device_management 1 devices, tenants, locations, groups, and status history drivercard 2 driver-card import identity and signature evidence fleet 5 persons, vehicles, links, due dates, RFID, licence checks, and notification responsibility routing finance 2 suppliers, invoices, tax summaries, document analysis, costs, financial originals, e-invoices, and exports leasing 2 lease contracts, versioned schedules, recurring invoices, occurrences, and reconciliation vehicle_unit 4 VU import evidence, trust anchors, and normalized V2 fact schema compliance 4 snapshots, rule-module configuration, and immutable catalog metadata backup 1 targets, replication state, jobs, and database snapshots task_execution 1 backend-neutral task runs, source snapshots, and per-file outcomes reporting 3 odometer history, cost-report parameters, and report templates task_execution 1 task runs, source snapshots, file results, and daily report evidence

The version is a per-component migration level, not the product version and not the storage-format number. A schema change must increment the owning component version. After migrations, startup validates V2, calculates its schema fingerprint, updates app_schema_state, commits, and runs PRAGMA quick_check when any migration was applied.

docs.title: Migration ledger
docs.text:
app_schema_migration uses (component, version) as its primary key. app_schema_state is a key/value registry and currently owns at least:

Key Meaning storage_format Physical tachograph storage generation; must equal 2. storage_schema_fingerprint SHA-256 over the normalized schema object's SQL definitions in deterministic order.

If no component migration ran and the calculated fingerprint differs from the registered fingerprint, startup fails. This prevents an unversioned manual DDL change from being silently accepted.

docs.title: 5. High-level data model
docs.text:
erDiagram
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_FACT_SOURCE : contains
    DDD_FACT_KIND ||--o{ DDD_FACT : classifies
    DDD_FACT_KIND ||--o{ DDD_FACT_SOURCE : classifies
    DDD_FACT ||--o{ DDD_FACT_SOURCE : proven_by
    DDD_FACT ||--|| TYPED_PAYLOAD : stores
    DDD_CARD_IDENTITY ||--o{ TYPED_PAYLOAD : normalizes
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT : describes
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT : describes
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_VU_SECTION : segments
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_COMPLIANCE_SNAPSHOT : evaluates
    FLEET_PERSON ||--o{ FLEET_DRIVERCARD_LINK : owns
    FLEET_VEHICLE ||--o{ FLEET_VEHICLE_VU_LINK : owns
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ FLEET_VEHICLE_VU_LINK : links
    FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE ||--o{ FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE_TAX_SUMMARY : taxes
    FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE ||--o{ FLEET_VEHICLE_COST_ENTRY : allocates
    FLEET_FINANCIAL_DOCUMENT }o--|| FLEET_FOREIGN_INVOICE : evidences
    FLEET_RECURRING_INVOICE ||--o{ FLEET_RECURRING_INVOICE_OCCURRENCE : schedules
    FLEET_LEASE_CONTRACT ||--o{ FLEET_RECURRING_INVOICE : governs
    BACKUP_TARGET ||--o{ BACKUP_ARCHIVE_STATE : replicates

The schema separates four concerns:

  • Evidence: immutable originals, archive metadata, parser/signature records, raw hashes, and audit.
  • Canonical facts: deduplicated observations independent of any one archive.
  • Provenance: every occurrence of a fact in an archive, including section and raw-record identity.
  • Business projections: people, vehicles, due dates, odometers, costs, reports, and backup state derived from or linked to evidence.

docs.title: ddd_archive
docs.text:
ddd_archive is the root for every C- or M-file import.

Column group Important columns Meaning Keys archive_pk, id Internal integer join key and stable public archive ID. File identity file_name, file_name_normalized, file_hash_sha256 Display/search name and SHA-256 of uncompressed DDD bytes. Stored object stored_path, compressed_size, stored_hash_sha256 GZIP object location, size, and hash. Source source_id, task_id, source_host, remote_path, source/download timestamps Transfer provenance. Lifecycle archived_at, is_deleted, deletion actor/time/reason Logical archive lifecycle. Classification ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status Parser and trust outcome. Identity/range identity_label, VIN, registration, data_from, data_to Search and entity-linking projection. Parser result parsed_at, parser_message Last parse attempt.

Active archives are unique by uncompressed file_hash_sha256. Logical deletion preserves the archive and audit row while removing it from active aggregate queries.

docs.title: Parser and signature evidence
docs.text:
Table Purpose ddd_drivercard_import Parsed card identity, generation, holder/licence metadata, parser version, signature summary, and import result. ddd_drivercard_signature Per signed EF block: generation, file ID, algorithm, certificate/trust fingerprints, verification time, and result. ddd_vehicle_unit_import VU generation, VIN, registration, serial, covered range, warnings, signature summary, and correlation ID. ddd_vu_section Section index/code, generation, source byte range, and SHA-256 of the exact signed bytes. ddd_vu_signature Per VU section signature result and certificate evidence. ddd_vu_unknown_record Bounded unsupported records with offsets, raw payload, and 32-byte raw hash so parsing remains loss-aware. tachograph_trust_anchor Versioned trust material used by signature verification.

Archive-owned evidence tables reference the public archive ID and normally use ON DELETE CASCADE. The compressed original remains the authoritative source for a future reparse.

docs.title: Core tables
docs.text:
Table Key Responsibility ddd_fact_kind kind_id Stable registry of typed fact kinds. ddd_card_identity card_pk Deduplicated normalized card number plus the best display form. ddd_fact fact_pk One canonical semantic observation, its full hash, cluster hash, kind, and optional event epoch. ddd_fact_source archive/kind/time/ordinal One occurrence of a fact in one archive, including section, record, raw hash, and source-only generation. ddd_fact_<kind> fact_pk Typed payload in compact SQLite-native fields.

ddd_fact_source is a WITHOUT ROWID table. Its composite primary key is ordered for deterministic per-archive replacement. It references ddd_archive, ddd_fact_kind, and ddd_fact; deleting an archive cascades its source rows. Orphan canonical facts are removed explicitly after archive replacement or removal.

docs.title: Encodings
docs.text:
Logical value Stored form UTC timestamp Signed integer Unix seconds. Calendar day Integer day offset from 1970-01-01. Activity 0=BREAK_REST, 1=AVAILABILITY, 2=WORK, 3=DRIVING. Card number card_pk into ddd_card_identity. Text Unicode NFC, control-character removal, and collapsed whitespace. Raw digest Exactly 32 bytes. Speed data One BLOB containing the complete 60-second block; 0xFF remains a missing sample.

Card normalization uppercases and retains alphanumeric characters only. All-placeholder values are treated as absent. The longer available display representation wins without changing the normalized identity.

docs.title: Fact and cluster hashes
docs.text:
The canonical fact_hash is SHA-256 over:

  1. ASCII fact-kind name and a zero byte;
  2. deterministic compact JSON of all encoded payload fields, sorted by key;
  3. a zero byte and the raw BLOB for fact kinds such as speed blocks.

UNIQUE(kind_id, fact_hash) stores an identical observation once even when many archives contain it.

The cluster_hash uses only the fact kind's domain-specific cluster fields. It groups records that represent the same logical slot/time/key but may disagree in other values. If a cluster has more than one distinct full fact hash, aggregate queries set has_conflict=true; variants are retained rather than overwritten.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
ddd_fact_source records:

  • archive and kind;
  • source ordinal;
  • canonical fact;
  • event epoch or the reserved no-event sentinel for time-free facts;
  • section index and code;
  • record index;
  • SHA-256 of the exact raw record, or a deterministic fallback hash;
  • card generation when generation belongs to source evidence rather than semantic identity.

This design allows a canonical row to be deduplicated without losing which files, sections, records, or generations proved it.

docs.title: Reparse transaction
docs.text:
For one archive and one fact kind, replace_archive_records() performs:

  1. delete the old ddd_fact_source rows for that archive/kind;
  2. normalize and encode each parser record;
  3. calculate full and cluster hashes;
  4. insert or reuse ddd_fact;
  5. insert the typed payload if this is a new fact;
  6. insert the archive-specific source row;
  7. remove canonical facts no longer referenced by any archive.

The original archive row, signature evidence, and other archives remain unchanged.

docs.title: 8. Fact-kind catalog
