docs.text: Kind / payload table Stored semantic fields Cluster identity vu.activity / ddd_fact_vu_activity slot, change time, activity, card-present flag, crew flag, card slot + change time vu.card_session / ddd_fact_vu_card_session slot, card, names, expiry, insert/withdraw times slot + card + insert/withdraw times vu.event / ddd_fact_vu_event type, begin, end type + begin + end vu.fault / ddd_fact_vu_fault type, begin, end type + begin + end vu.overspeed / ddd_fact_vu_overspeed begin/end, maximum and average speed begin + end vu.speed_block / ddd_fact_vu_speed_block start epoch, 60-byte speed BLOB start epoch vu.technical / ddd_fact_vu_technical record type, value, detail JSON record type vu.calibration / ddd_fact_vu_calibration purpose, workshop, VIN, registration, calibration times purpose + calibration time vu.position / ddd_fact_vu_position position type, time, coordinates, raw hex type + time vu.border / ddd_fact_vu_border crossing time, coordinates, raw hex crossing time vu.load / ddd_fact_vu_load time, operation, coordinates, raw hex time + operation vu.odometer / ddd_fact_vu_odometer source day, midnight time, odometer source day card.activity / ddd_fact_card_activity card, activity, start/end, duration, day, crew, slot card + start/end + slot card.event / ddd_fact_card_event card, event codes/text, begin/end, vehicle, place card + numeric type + begin/end card.fault / ddd_fact_card_fault card, fault codes/text, begin/end, vehicle, place card + numeric type + begin/end card.vehicle / ddd_fact_card_vehicle card, use interval, odometers, distance, registration, VIN, block counter card + use interval + registration card.position / ddd_fact_card_position card, source, record/position times, country/region, odometer, coordinates, accuracy, authentication card + source + record/position times

docs.title: Aggregate queries
docs.text:
list_facts() returns one canonical fact across a caller-supplied archive scope. It:

  • ignores logically deleted archives;
  • filters by ddd_fact.event_epoch;
  • returns source count and archive IDs;
  • chooses a preferred source by verified parse/signature status, then generation (G2_V2, G2_V1, older), then newest archive;
  • reports conflicting variants by cluster;
  • caps a page at 1,000,000 rows.

docs.title: Single-archive queries
docs.text: list_archive_observations() starts at ddd_fact_source, preserves the source ordinal, section/record identity, raw hash, and generation, and returns only observations from that file. It deliberately does not collapse repeated source records.

docs.title: Required indexes
docs.text:
• ix_ddd_fact_kind_time supports kind/time pagination.
  • ix_ddd_fact_source_fact supports source aggregation and orphan checks.
  • Card-bearing, time-bearing payloads have (card_pk, time, fact_pk) indexes.
  • Archive search indexes cover active hash uniqueness, type/date, parse/signature status, normalized name, and archive time.

Indexes are dropped during bulk V2 rebuild and recreated only after all archives have been reparsed, followed by ANALYZE and PRAGMA optimize.

docs.title: 10. Compliance and audit
docs.text:
ddd_compliance_snapshot stores immutable, reproducible evaluation output: archive or subject scope, assessed range, ruleset and algorithm versions, source manifest, module manifest, configuration hash, report JSON, report SHA-256, creator, and time. Triggers reject updates and deletes.

compliance_rule_module_config stores the global enabled state and JSON settings per rule module. compliance_balm_catalog stores immutable catalog-version metadata; triggers reject update and delete operations.

Audit is split by responsibility:

Table Scope audit_log Global user, administration, and cross-domain actions. ddd_audit_log Archive, parser, signature, export, and tachograph lifecycle. fleet_audit_log Fleet, deadline, RFID, finance, and related business objects.

Audit rows store technical object IDs and actors. They are append-oriented and are resolved by the UI to the current business record.

docs.title: Authentication and application state
docs.text: Tables Purpose app_role, app_permission, app_role_permission Fixed roles and permission grants. app_user Argon2id login identity, role, locale, lock state, and password lifecycle. app_login_attempt Authentication attempt history and lockout evidence. app_user_ui_state Per-user view, table, filter, and layout state. app_user_migration, user_roles Controlled compatibility/migration state for earlier user models. app_schema_migration, app_schema_state Version ledger and physical-format contract.

docs.title: Device management and transfer state
docs.text: Tables Purpose customers, locations Tenant/site reference data. devices Device identity, endpoint configuration, protected access fields, inventory, status projection, and lifecycle. device_status_history Time-ordered status checks per device. device_groups, device_group_members Operational grouping. processed_files Download/import idempotency state for source files. task_execution_run Durable scheduled/manual task run, trigger, time range, status and totals. task_execution_source Per-run source snapshot, availability, error and transfer totals. task_execution_file Successful and failed file-level transfer and processing evidence.

docs.title: Fleet master data and links
docs.text:
Tables Purpose fleet_person, fleet_vehicle Person and vehicle master records with logical archival. fleet_drivercard_link Unique card-to-person assignment and source archive evidence. fleet_vehicle_vu_link Vehicle-to-M-file assignment, match basis, and confirmation state. fleet_mobile_device Fleet-related mobile-device assignments. fleet_due_type, fleet_due Configurable person/vehicle deadlines and managed download schedules; vehicle rows support time, mileage and earliest-of-both limits with captured completion evidence. fleet_license_check Driving-licence check results. fleet_rfid_assignment Current and historical RFID-to-person assignments. fleet_rfid_import_file, fleet_rfid_import_row Imported terminal files, row fingerprints, validation, and processing results.

Open tachograph download schedules are protected by a partial unique index on object, manager, and active state. Active RFID UIDs and current person assignments are also unique.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Tables Purpose fleet_notification_rule Enabled rules, schedules, thresholds, message configuration, and fleet/system responsibility routing. fleet_notification_recipient Delivery targets with independent fleet-manager and system-manager membership and one shared To/CC type. fleet_notification_delivery Durable delivery attempt, retry, and result history.

docs.title: Finance and e-invoices
docs.text:
Tables Purpose fleet_supplier Supplier identity, contact, tax, VAT, endpoint, and company identifiers. fleet_cost_category Cost classification and fixed/variable defaults. fleet_foreign_invoice Invoice, credit-note or recurring-invoice header, source, dates, totals, optional uniform VAT rate, workflow, duplicate override, reversal, and audit actors. fleet_foreign_invoice_tax_summary Authoritative VAT category, basis, tax and gross totals for uniform and mixed-rate documents. fleet_vehicle_cost_entry Vehicle/category allocation, validity period, signed amounts, tax, workflow, reversal, recurring-occurrence and reclassification links. fleet_lease_contract Vehicle/supplier lease terms, factor inputs, authoritative actual rate, mileage evidence and lifecycle. fleet_lease_component Recurring and one-time contract components, including effective-factor relevance. fleet_lease_schedule_item Versioned planned payment schedule with stable instalment identity across contract changes. fleet_lease_document_link Links a contract to immutable documents from its vehicle record. fleet_lease_cost_link Links actual vehicle cost or credit positions, including invoice positions, to a contract. fleet_recurring_invoice Immutable recurring-invoice assignment, repeating amounts, active period, posting mode and contract/schedule references. fleet_recurring_invoice_mode_change Audited effective-dated AUTO/MANUAL changes that affect only future unposted periods. fleet_recurring_invoice_occurrence Idempotent monthly due item, reconciliation state, worker outcome and resulting cost entry. fleet_financial_document Local original/manifest identity, SHA-256, archive status, optional backup state, retention, legal hold, and supersession. fleet_document Versioned personnel/vehicle record documents with SHA-256 verified local archive, backup identity, archive lifecycle and controlled purge evidence. fleet_einvoice_import Syntax/profile, original/XML hashes, validator result, documents, supplier match, contract reference and object references. fleet_einvoice_line Structured source lines and adjustments with exact monetary values and allocation status. fleet_einvoice_allocation Cent-accurate line split into vehicle cost entries, including confirmed suggestions. fleet_invoice_document_analysis Versioned supplier-invoice-v1 local/cloud findings, confidence, evidence and explicit cloud consent. fleet_invoice_match_feedback Confirmed and corrected matching signals used by local learning. fleet_ai_connector_provider Shared Azure/Vertex provider, region, model, credential reference and connection-test state; secrets remain outside the database. fleet_finance_export Durable accounting export/outbox state, correction kind and retries. fleet_finance_settings Finance/export/report calculation settings.

Money uses integer cents; VAT rates use integer basis points. Reversal objects retain links to their originals. A non-overridden active invoice is unique by supplier, case-insensitive document number, and document date. Original files live in the financial archive, not in SQLite; the database stores paths, hashes, sizes, manifests, and state.

docs.title: Odometer and reporting
docs.text:
Tables Purpose fleet_vehicle_odometer_reading M-, C-, manual, and imported readings with source, quality, approval, and archive link. fleet_report_template Versioned system/user report templates, context, ownership, defaults, and JSON definition.

M-file midnight readings are authoritative. Manual and C-file values may fill missing boundaries but cannot replace a valid M value. Cost/km is calculated from complete vehicle-month intersections rather than persisted as an uncontrolled aggregate.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text:
Tables Purpose backup_target Provider, root, active state, protected credentials/key, encryption, and health timestamps. backup_archive_state Per-target tachograph archive replication state, attempts, hashes, and next retry. backup_database_snapshot Snapshot hashes, sizes, remote identity, retention class, verification, and correlation ID. backup_job Coarse-grained run progress and result.

A partial unique index permits only one active backup target. Backup metadata does not replace the local archive state in ddd_archive or fleet_financial_document.

docs.title: 12. Complete table inventory
docs.text:
The current V2 schema contains these logical groups. A deployed database may contain no business rows, but its reference rows and schema objects are initialized.

docs.title: 13. Legacy-to-V2 migration
docs.text:
The supported migration is an out-of-place rebuild performed by scripts/migrate_demo_database_v2.py.

flowchart TD
    A["Legacy database"] --> B["Preflight quick/FK checks"]
    B --> C["Verify every GZIP and original DDD hash"]
    C --> D["Bootstrap empty V2 work database"]
    D --> E["Copy authoritative business rows"]
    E --> F["Reparse every active C/M original"]
    F --> G["Rebuild odometers and download due dates"]
    G --> H["Compare counts, distinct facts, ranges, speed digests, signatures"]
    H --> I["Create indexes, ANALYZE, optimize, FK/quick checks"]
    I --> J["VACUUM and size check"]
    J --> K{"--apply"}
    K -->|"no"| L["Keep validated candidate"]
    K -->|"yes"| M["Rename source to V1 backup, candidate to source"]

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
• source exists and is not already V2;
  • work database, WAL, and SHM do not exist;
  • a requested backup target does not already exist;
  • free space is at least 512 MiB or 110% of source size, whichever is larger;
  • source quick_check and foreign_key_check pass;
  • each active C/M archive has a readable GZIP object;
  • stored-object and uncompressed-original SHA-256 values match the archive row.

docs.title: Rebuild
docs.text: Authoritative business tables are copied by common column name. Derived tachograph tables, migration state, audit projections, automatically managed download due dates, and non-manual odometer projections are rebuilt. Active archives are reparsed from original bytes into the new fact model. Fact indexes are created after bulk loading.

docs.title: Semantic validation
docs.text:
For every fact kind the migration compares:

  • observation count;
  • distinct semantic count;
  • minimum and maximum event time;
  • per-archive observation counts;
  • exact expanded speed-byte count and digest;
  • archive signature status.

It then validates the schema, foreign keys, quick check, 8 KiB page size, and post-vacuum database. A large source must meet the migration's compaction threshold.

docs.title: Atomic activation
docs.text: --apply is refused while source WAL/SHM files exist. The source is renamed to the V1 backup, then the validated candidate is renamed to the source path. If the second rename fails, the backup is restored. The V1 backup is not deleted automatically.

docs.title: 14. Deployment database contract
docs.text:
scripts/create_deployment_database.py creates a fresh V2 database, validates integrity and foreign keys, validates the storage schema and 8 KiB page size, confirms format 2, and verifies the expected seed counts. Business tables must be empty. The initial administrator is active, uses English/en-GB, and must change the initial password.

After validation, the database is vacuumed into one file and accompanied by archive.db.sha256. Release tooling must verify that checksum against the exact database file after the final write.

docs.title: 15. Operational checks
docs.text:
Use a read-only connection for diagnostics:

SELECT key, value
FROM app_schema_state
ORDER BY key;

SELECT component, version, applied_at, duration_ms
FROM app_schema_migration
ORDER BY component, version;

PRAGMA quick_check;
PRAGMA foreign_key_check;

Fact counts and provenance:

SELECT k.name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.fact_pk) AS canonical_facts,
       COUNT(s.fact_pk) AS source_observations,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.archive_pk) AS source_archives
FROM ddd_fact_kind k
LEFT JOIN ddd_fact f ON f.kind_id = k.kind_id
LEFT JOIN ddd_fact_source s ON s.fact_pk = f.fact_pk
GROUP BY k.kind_id, k.name
ORDER BY k.kind_id;

Archive health:

SELECT ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status, COUNT(*) AS archives
FROM ddd_archive
WHERE is_deleted = 0
GROUP BY ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status
ORDER BY ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status;

Do not use diagnostic SQL to repair data. Restore a verified database or re-run the owning import, migration, reconciliation, or rebuild service so hashes, provenance, audit, and projections remain consistent.

docs.title: Enterprise tenant architecture
docs.text: An Enterprise tenant is an independent customer with its own PostgreSQL database and protected data root. Device/location groups inside a customer are independent of this boundary. Start the user guide under Enterprise.

docs.title: Identity and access
docs.text:
Global users, platform administrators and versioned customer memberships live in a separate control database. Matching email addresses or usernames do not establish membership. A user's role can differ per customer; customer administration grants no platform privileges.

FleetMiraApi authenticates centrally and authorizes the selected customer on every interface. URL prefixes and token tags are routing hints, not authorization. OAuth, file access and integrations remain bound to the authorized context.

docs.title: Native clients and databases
docs.text:
A client receives only an individually revocable, short-lived PostgreSQL lease for its authorized customer. The server determines target and role; users cannot supply authoritative DSNs or file roots. Runtime roles do not own tables, provision roles or bypass RLS.

Revocation also covers existing connections. Switching tenants replaces the complete client process context, including database references, files and caches. Enterprise has no SQLite fallback. Basic and Pro retain their shared SQLite implementation and in-process worker.

docs.title: Provisioning and background operation
docs.text:
Platform administrators request customers through the wizard. Inputs are limited to customer name, identifier, initial administrator and optional add-on license. Trusted templates, database targets and storage roots are configured server-side.

FleetMiraWorker processes durable jobs with leases and fencing. The local provisioning service performs narrowly scoped privileged steps. The worker host starts a separate process context per customer; no additional Windows service is installed per customer. Customer archives, integration secrets, jobs and restores stay isolated.

docs.title: Licensing and restore
docs.text:
A base license includes one customer. Further customers require add-ons immutably bound to the base license, platform and customer. Sign-in or a successful TCP connection alone does not establish business entitlement.

Tenant backup and platform protection are different responsibilities. The control database and protected keys are part of platform recovery. Customer restore must not merge identities from other customers or rebind their databases. Existing installations are converted only through explicit maintenance with verified backup and rollback.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Installation and services/Health describe operational procedures. Source checks, frozen applications and actual installed service/UI acceptance are distinct evidence. Customer-specific networks, load, external integrations and key transfers need their own verification.

docs.title: Tachograph data parsing, storage and access
1. Scope and guarantees
docs.text:
This document describes the technical path of driver-card C files and vehicle-unit M files from the immutable DDD original through parsing, signature verification, database storage, cross-archive deduplication and repository access.

  • The compressed DDD original is the auditable source of truth.
  • Archive, signature, section and raw-record evidence remains archive-specific.
  • Reparsing replaces only derived observations for that archive.
  • person and vehicle aggregate views deduplicate across every linked archive.
  • A single-archive view still reproduces only that file's observations.
  • Deduplication never changes parser or signature status.
flowchart LR
    A["DDD input"] --> B["Local GZIP original"]
    B --> C["Archive metadata and SHA-256"]
    B --> D{"Binary classification"}
    D -->|"C file"| E["DriverCardFullParser"]
    D -->|"M file"| F["VehicleUnitParser"]
    E --> G["C signature verification"]
    F --> H["M signature verification"]
    G --> I["Archive-specific C tables"]
    H --> J["Archive-specific M tables"]
    I --> K["Canonical aggregate view"]
    J --> K
    K --> L["Repository"]
    L --> M["UI / reporting / compliance"]
    I --> N["Single-archive view"]
    J --> N

docs.title: 2. Archive and common import pipeline
docs.text:
ddd_archive holds the archive ID, file name, original and stored hashes, storage path, sizes, source, timestamps, DDD type, generation, parse/signature status, identity fields and covered date range.

TachographImportService.import_archive_id() performs these steps:

  1. Load the archive row and reject a logically deleted archive unless explicitly allowed.
  2. Read the DDD bytes from the GZIP object.
  3. Classify the binary content; the file name is not authoritative.
  4. Record classification and an audit event under a new correlation ID.
  5. Run the C or M parser.
  6. Verify exact signed bytes against the trust store.
  7. Replace archive-specific derived observations and update archive status.
  8. Reconcile entity links, download deadlines and cached evaluations.
Column Content Purpose file_hash_sha256 SHA-256 of uncompressed DDD bytes proves the original functional content stored_hash_sha256 SHA-256 of the stored GZIP object detects storage damage or modification 
sequenceDiagram
    participant Import as TachographImportService
    participant Archive as ddd_archive
    participant File as GZIP original
    participant Parser as C/M parser
    participant Verify as Signature service
    participant DB as Observation tables

    Import->>Archive: Load archive metadata
    Import->>File: Read exact DDD bytes
    Import->>Parser: Classify and parse
    Parser-->>Import: Structure, identity and source references
    Import->>Verify: Verify signed blocks/sections
    Verify-->>Import: VALID / INVALID / UNVERIFIABLE / MISSING
    Import->>DB: Replace observations for archive
    Import->>Archive: Update generation, range and status

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text:
DriverCardFullParser preserves every EF and signature boundary. Each segment has a five-byte header: two-byte file ID, one-byte kind (0 G1 data, 1 G1 signature, 2 G2 data, 3 G2 signature), and a two-byte big-endian length. Payloads extending past the file or trailing bytes after the last segment are parse errors. Offset, length and SHA-256 are calculated for every payload.

Important EFs include:

EF Data 0501, 0525 application identification, generation and record counts 0520, 0521 card holder and driving-licence identity 0504 daily driver activity 0502, 0503 events and faults 0505 vehicles used and odometers 0506, 0524 places and GNSS positions 0526–0530 G2V2 authentication, borders and loading data C100, C101, C108, C109 card, CardSign, CA and link certificates

Generation is derived as G1, G2 or G2V2 and mapped to G1, G2_V1 or G2_V2 in the archive row.

The activity ring buffer is followed by its oldest/newest pointers. Daily-record headers and payloads are read cyclically, so a record may start in the final EF bytes and continue at offset zero; traversal stops only after the record identified by activityPointerNewestRecord. A length-guided linear scan is the guarded fallback. Daily records are deduplicated by date and presence counter. Minute changes become intervals for BREAK_REST, AVAILABILITY, WORK and DRIVING. Event/fault arrays use counts from application identification. Vehicle, place and GNSS records retain timestamps, registration, VIN where present, odometers, coordinates, accuracy and authentication state. Empty records are not emitted.

flowchart TD
    A["C file bytes"] --> B["Validate segment headers and boundaries"]
    B --> C["Build EF segments with offset and SHA-256"]
    C --> D["Read application identification"]
    D --> E["Determine generation and record counts"]
    E --> F["Identity and card metadata"]
    E --> G["Activity ring buffer"]
    E --> H["Events and faults"]
    E --> I["Vehicles, places and GNSS"]
    F --> J["Normalised observations"]
    G --> J
    H --> J
    I --> J
    J --> K["Verify signed EFs"]
    K --> L["Replace archive-specific C rows"]

docs.title: 4. M-file parser
docs.text:
Every section starts with 0x76 and a TREP code.

Generation TREP codes Logical sections G1 01–05 overview, activities, events/faults, speed, technical G2 v1 21–25 the same areas encoded as RecordArrays G2 v2 31–35 G2-v2 records including additional GNSS/border/load data

Mixed generations, impossible lengths, data after a signature, or incomplete mandatory structures fail parsing. A missing detailed-speed section is an optional-download warning, not a signature error.

G1 uses fixed or count-driven structures followed by a 128-byte signature. Two 194-byte certificates at the start of the overview are excluded from the signed data as required by Annex IB. VIN is read as 17 characters. Country and code-page bytes are skipped before the 13-character registration number. The covered range comes from VuDownloadablePeriod, not current VU time.

G2 uses RecordArrays with type, size and count. size × count is checked before reading. Certificate records (0x04, 0x0F) and the single signature record (0x08) remain separate from functional records. Each functional record receives section index/code, record index and SHA-256 of exact bytes.

Both paths decode identity, covered period, activities, card sessions, events, faults, overspeed, speed, technical/calibration, position, border, load and midnight-odometer observations. Unknown bounded records remain available as raw evidence and warnings.

docs.title: Compact speed storage
docs.text:
All generations use ddd_vu_speed_block: Unix start_epoch, exactly 60 speed bytes including 0xFF, and one binary 32-byte source SHA-256. 0xFF stays in the stored block but is omitted from measurement results. Date filtering, offset and limit apply after second-by-second expansion.

flowchart TD
    A["M file bytes"] --> B{"TREP generation"}
    B -->|"G1"| C["Fixed/count-driven sections"]
    B -->|"G2 v1/v2"| D["Validate RecordArrays"]
    C --> E["Separate signed body and 128-byte signature"]
    D --> F["Separate certificates, records and signature"]
    E --> G["Normalise observations"]
    F --> G
    G --> H["SHA-256 per source record"]
    G --> I["60-second speed blocks"]
    H --> J["Verify each section"]
    I --> J
    J --> K["Replace archive-specific M rows"]

docs.title: 5. Signature model
docs.text:
tachograph_trust_anchor stores generation, key ID, SHA-256 fingerprint, certificate/key material, validity, revocation, source and active state.

  • C G1 uses card/CA certificates and RSA PKCS#1 with SHA-1 over exact data blocks.
  • C G2/G2V2 uses CardSign/MSCA and optional link certificates with ECDSA over signed EFs.
  • M G1 uses RSA PKCS#1/SHA-1; M G2 verifies each section with its certificate-defined ECC/hash chain.
  • Per-block results are in ddd_drivercard_signature; per-section results are in ddd_vu_signature.

The newest plausible signed functional timestamp is the certificate reference time. Archive time is a warned fallback. Overall precedence is INVALID, UNVERIFIABLE, MISSING, then VALID.

docs.title: Archive and evidence
docs.text: ddd_archive, ddd_audit_log, fleet_audit_log, tachograph_trust_anchor and app_schema_migration preserve source, audit, trust and schema-version information.

docs.title: C tables
docs.text: ddd_drivercard_import, ddd_drivercard_activity, ddd_drivercard_event, ddd_drivercard_fault, ddd_drivercard_vehicle_used, ddd_drivercard_position and ddd_drivercard_signature hold typed archive observations. Legacy-compatible raw_json and source_json columns remain but new imports store NULL because all required values can be reproduced from the original and typed columns.

docs.title: M tables
docs.text:
ddd_vehicle_unit_import, ddd_vu_section, ddd_vu_signature, ddd_vu_raw_record, the activity/session/event/fault/overspeed tables, ddd_vu_speed_block, technical/calibration tables, position/border/load tables, and ddd_vu_odometer_midnight hold typed observations. ddd_vu_technical.details_json stores the complete structured VU identification used by the field tree. fleet_vehicle_vu_link links every matching M archive to a vehicle master record.

erDiagram
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT : "is C file"
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o| DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT : "is M file"
    DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_DRIVERCARD_ACTIVITY : contains
    DDD_DRIVERCARD_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_DRIVERCARD_SIGNATURE : proves
    DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_VU_SECTION : contains
    DDD_VEHICLE_UNIT_IMPORT ||--o{ DDD_VU_SPEED_BLOCK : contains
    DDD_ARCHIVE ||--o{ DDD_FACT_PROVENANCE : supplies
    DDD_CANONICAL_FACT ||--o{ DDD_FACT_PROVENANCE : sourced_by
    DDD_FACT_KIND ||--o{ DDD_CANONICAL_FACT : types

Important indexes cover archive name/date/type/status, normalised card number plus generation, archive/time and card/time activity access, vehicle/archive links, and canonical fact time/cluster/provenance. ddd_vu_speed_block is WITHOUT ROWID; its primary key beginning with archive and start time is already the required access path.

Runtime connections use WAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=30000, synchronous=NORMAL and a 1,000-page automatic checkpoint. Schema work runs once before UI creation; repositories open with ensure_schema=False during normal operation.

docs.title: 7. Cross-archive deduplication
docs.text:
Archive-specific typed tables remain exact provenance. Aggregate views use one of two compatible paths:

  1. Materialised ddd_canonical_fact and ddd_fact_provenance rows.
  2. A compact SQL fallback over typed tables using ROW_NUMBER, COUNT and GROUP_CONCAT when no materialised provenance exists.

The compact production migration deliberately uses the fallback to avoid duplicating all payloads. Both paths return source count, source archive IDs and preferred navigation source.

Materialised normalisation uses Unicode NFC/collapsed whitespace, alphanumeric uppercase identifiers, UTC seconds, exact numeric/coordinate values and exact blobs. Placeholder-only identifiers are empty. fact_hash is a binary SHA-256 over kind and full normalised content; cluster_hash hashes identifying cluster fields. Variants in one cluster remain separate and can be marked as conflicts.

For card observations, the complete normalised card number is the only cross-archive and cross-source identity. card_generation remains source metadata in the raw observation and provenance, but is neither part of the fact hash nor a C/M matching filter. G1 card/G1 vehicle, G1 card/G2 vehicle, G2 card/G1 vehicle and G2 card/G2 vehicle combinations are therefore handled identically.

The fallback partitions by every functional field. Navigation preference is verified/valid, then G2 v2, G2 v1, G1, then newest archive. This never changes functional content. Speed blocks partition by start epoch and the complete 60-byte blob before expansion.

Vehicle technical data is deduplicated by record type, value and the complete normalised detail structure. Existing rows without details_json are reconstructed in a worker from the immutable compressed M original. The vehicle record shows each identical variant once with its source count; archive identifiers and file names remain navigation metadata. New imports persist details_json directly and include it in the technical fact hash.

flowchart TD
    A["Vehicle or person"] --> B["Resolve linked active archives"]
    B --> C{"Materialised provenance exists?"}
    C -->|"Yes"| D["Select fact_hash and group sources"]
    C -->|"No"| E["Partition typed rows with window functions"]
    D --> F["Detect cluster variants"]
    E --> G["Select exact duplicate representative"]
    F --> H["Apply date filter"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["Sort, limit and offset"]
    I --> J["DTOs for UI/reporting"]

docs.title: 8. Repository access
docs.text:
list_vehicle_facts, count_vehicle_facts, list_vehicle_speed_seconds, list_person_facts, and list_archive_observations are the primary internal interfaces. Aggregate access resolves linked archives, deduplicates, filters, sorts and only then paginates. Single-archive access filters directly by archive ID and preserves section/record order.

UI calls execute through UiJobController workers. Each worker opens its own SQLite connection and returns only lists, dictionaries or DTOs. Widgets and models are updated only by the UI-thread callback.

docs.title: 9. Idempotency, migration and diagnostics
docs.text:
Reimport replaces derived rows for one archive. Parser failure does not discard previously verified details. Maintenance migration operates on a SQLite copy, verifies every original/hash and count, removes JSON caches, compacts with VACUUM INTO, runs PRAGMA quick_check, and performs an atomic or next-start staged replacement with a rollback backup.

Administrators may use read-only checks such as:

PRAGMA quick_check;
PRAGMA journal_mode;

SELECT component, version, applied_at, duration_ms
FROM app_schema_migration ORDER BY component;

SELECT ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status, COUNT(*)
FROM ddd_archive WHERE is_deleted = 0
GROUP BY ddd_type, generation, parse_status, signature_status;

Direct database writes are unsupported; use import, reparse, link, migration and restore services so audit, hashes and cache invalidation remain consistent.

docs.title: Workshop Management: architecture and release
docs.text: The shared workshop area is intended for Pro and Enterprise. Basic retains the same schema; licensing hides the area. Business rules have no edition branches. Pro uses SQLite and the in-process worker; Enterprise uses PostgreSQL and FleetMiraWorker. The separate Windows service FleetMiraArchive provides only storage, integrity and key operations.

docs.title: Shared data and services
docs.text:
Empty linked detail lists return without reading unrelated master-data lookup tables. Populated lists retain their labels, order and exact numeric fields; a new load resolves current labels again. This shared read behavior is covered with real disposable SQLite and PostgreSQL repositories. It adds no cache, write or edition-specific path.

workshop_management.py contains the repository and master-data, work-order, quotation, purchasing and inventory services. workshop_billing.py implements outgoing invoices, immutable snapshots, corrections and accounting transfers. workshop_runtime.py composes the services; database access and serialization use database_runtime.

Vehicles, personnel, suppliers, cost categories and record documents reuse the existing areas. Commercial customers are independent of device tenants. Referenced master data is archived. UUIDs and expected versions prevent lost changes. Repeatable commands have persistent idempotency keys.

Quantities use integer units of 0.0001; prices and inventory values use 0.000001 EUR. Invoice amounts are integer cents. Decimal and explicit commercial rounding replace binary floating-point calculations. Price provenance, rules, tax definitions and document language are frozen into each document. Purchase and sale prices have inclusive validity boundaries; overlapping periods for the same price source are prevented. Work-order lines use their service date and purchase lines their order date. Price-list rules and explicit manual overrides retain their provenance. AW/hour conversion preserves the original quantity, unit and factor; invoice representation does not change material quantities.

flowchart LR
  QT[Quotation / revision] --> WO[Work order]
  TM[Templates / labour texts] --> WO
  PO[Purchase order] --> GR[Goods receipt]
  GR --> SJ[Immutable stock journal]
  WO --> SJ
  WO --> ID[Invoice draft]
  MI[Manual article invoice] --> ID
  ID --> SS[Frozen snapshot / number]
  SS --> VL[XML / PDF-A validation]
  VL --> AR[Protected archive / receipt]
  AR --> II[Issued invoice]
  II --> EX[DATEV / CSV-ZIP / REST]

docs.title: Inventory and cost protection
docs.text:
Earmarked work-order articles are nonbinding demand. Explicit partial consumption links the actual line to its plan and retains outstanding demand; replay does not post twice. Actual consumption posts material. Quantity changes post the difference; price and text changes do not issue stock. Returns and corrections preserve every original movement.

Direct invoices for stocked articles reserve the actual quantity during finalization. This protects the resumable process from competing withdrawals and consumes the reservation exactly once when issuing. Work-order rebilling creates no second withdrawal. Invoice corrections do not return material.

Valuation supports warehouse moving average, article-wide valuation and fixed valuation prices. Changes after the first posting require a reason and produce traceable value entries. Own vehicles can allocate approved actual workshop costs to an existing cost category. The projection uses the existing vehicle-cost repository and posts only changes on renewed approval. Purchasing and outgoing invoicing create no additional vehicle costs.

docs.title: Finalization, archive and audit
docs.text:
Finalization persists the snapshot, number and durable job before external file effects. Invoices and corrections have independent transactionally protected annual number ranges. Changed vehicle/customer mappings require user confirmation bound to current versions before rebilling. Free services need explicit approval and a reason. Generators and validators run offline with verified resources: Mustang 2.25.0, XRechnung 3.0.2 with KoSIT 1.6.3 / configuration 2026-08-31, ZUGFeRD 2.5.2 EN16931, Stimulsoft 2025.1.3 through Node 24.21.0 and veraPDF 1.30.2. Resources, fonts and generators are hashed. Stimulsoft requires the existing valid licence.

XML and PDF derive from one snapshot. Validation covers schema/Schematron, PDF/A-3, actual embedded XML bytes and semantic snapshot comparison. The archive service validates independently and signs the attested hashes. Failed validation cannot create an issued invoice.

Leases protect concurrent finalization and exports. After a crash, uploaded bytes and signed receipts are reused. An explicitly abandoned finalization retains its number and signed abandonment proof. An already sealed finalization resumes. Uncertain REST outcomes require audited reconciliation; automatic retries require confirmed recipient idempotency protection.

Append-only tables and frozen invoices have database guards. PostgreSQL additionally restricts application privileges. The shared worker independently seals workshop audit, stock movement, number and cost-projection evidence. Missing or changed previously sealed rows block further financial processing. Initial adoption marks existing evidence as a baseline. Subsequent packages hold bounded deltas and signed predecessor references; recovery and exports verify the full chain. A standalone auditor export requires no invoice and includes actual field definitions, foreign keys, business relationships, originals and evidence. DATEV uses versioned v700 field contracts including debtor master data and the configured finalization flag. Ordinary users cannot write archive files or keys; pipe access verifies the service identity and installed client executable.

The audit regression identifies human and technical events by their business action. On SQLite and PostgreSQL it checks actor, reason, shared correlation and object references, including the fleet_audit_log mirror; an additional case deliberately uses equal timestamps. Sorted UUID order does not establish business-event chronology. Production timestamps, audit data and append-only guards remain unchanged.

docs.title: Retention and individual review
docs.text:
workshop_retention.py registers versioned rules for booking documents (eight years), books/records/inventories (ten years) and relevant business correspondence (six years). The period begins from the actual creation event; backdated service or invoice dates do not shorten it. Linked documents share the longest deadline. Reasoned extensions and legal holds remain traceable as immutable events; releasing a hold never shortens a minimum deadline. Database guards and event-journal comparison detect unlogged projection changes.

The Retention workspace shows document classes, deadlines, holds and review reports. Individual review covers every linked document and records permission, time, reason and decision. Even an eligible review does not physically remove data. Removal of sealed packages remains technically locked; introducing such an operational action requires joint approval of all dependent data, evidence chains and statutory periods.

docs.title: UI and acceptance
docs.text:
The primary area uses a horizontal splitter, IconNavbarController, six groups and 30 workspaces. Sessions start empty. Static workspaces are reused and record details are focused by identity. Details contain business data, documents and history. Language changes update navigation and open tabs; region controls number entry and display independently.

The product matrix, database parity catalogue and Enterprise acceptance catalogue register the area. Source tests cover both databases, workflows, concurrency, failures and all 25 UI languages. Semantic Enterprise acceptance covers navigation, a customer roundtrip and actual inventory, purchasing, pricing, planning and billing processes in an explicitly marked disposable PostgreSQL system.

A production release also requires installed Pro/Enterprise service tests under the intended user permissions, backup/restore on a fresh host, tax-specialist review of the configured examples, a complete auditor export and documented operating procedures. Passing source or build tests does not replace these acceptance steps. Authenticode is required for stable publication.

docs.title: Later Fleet import
docs.text:
workshop_import_contract.py prepares typed source identities, reviewed mappings and separate comparison/opening values. The wizard itself belongs to the later implementation package. Names and registrations are not automatic merge keys. Historical invoices are not reissued; continued auditability of the legacy system remains part of the migration procedure. Legacy credentials are absent from source code.

See user workflows and accounting and archive operations.

docs.title: Connector Framework
docs.text:
The FLEET Mira Expansion Package Framework is the target concept for customer-specific modules, integrations and workflows based on FLEET Mira. An Expansion Package groups the required connectors, integrated screens, mapping rules and permissions.

Concept and development baseline

Status: 17 September 2026. These pages describe a proposed extension architecture, not a released framework feature. The shared application core and worker runtime exist; package registration, the extension protocol and Integration Gateway still require implementation and acceptance testing.

docs.title: The three concept documents
docs.text:
Document Audience Contents Developer handbook Developers and integrators Architecture, extension points, data contracts, workflows, security, testing and deployment with Mermaid diagrams Customer concept Customers and project owners Benefits, components, example processes, introduction and scope Product flyer Initial discussions and overview Compact visual summary of the concept

Download the web edition

The ZIP contains the German and English Markdown editions, illustrations and Mermaid source text. It does not contain the original Word files.

docs.title: Architecture at a glance
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    U["Mira Client<br/>Core UI and UI Extensions"] -->|"Action through Mira Services"| Q["Job storage"]
    Q -->|"Claim job"| W["FleetMiraWorker"]
    W -->|"Job"| C["Backend Connector<br/>isolated process"]
    C -->|"API or SQL"| E["External system"]
    E -->|"Response"| C
    C -->|"Result or DTO"| W
    W -->|"Validate and apply"| G["Integration Gateway<br/>Domain Services and Repositories"]
    G -->|"Validated changes"| D[("Mira business data")]

Reading guide: An arrow represents a named operation or data hand-off. The Core is a logical software layer, not an additional mandatory server service. External connectors do not write directly to Mira Core tables.

docs.title: About these documents
docs.text:
The revised architecture accounts for the existing shared product runtime. Basic and Pro retain SQLite with an in-process worker; Enterprise uses PostgreSQL and the separate FleetMiraWorker. The expansion concept starts with Enterprise/Custom; enabling other editions requires explicit classification and testing.

FLEET Mira is intended as the successor product. A permanent connection to the previous fleet system is outside the target architecture. Examples use general categories such as External system, ERP/Accounting and Telematics. Any required one-time data migration would be a separate project, not an ongoing connector.

docs.title: Customer concept
docs.text:
FLEET Mira Custom is intended to extend the shared FLEET Mira application with the interfaces and workflows a business needs. Related functions are delivered as an Expansion Package. Operation, permissions and monitoring remain integrated into Mira.

Concept status

This description explains the proposed extension architecture as of September 2026. Availability, specific integrations, scope and dates are confirmed per project. The framework is not yet a generally released product feature.

docs.title: What an Expansion Package contains
docs.text:
A package may contain a connection to another system, suitable screens, mapping rules and automated workflows. Only required components are implemented. A SAP integration, for example, needs different settings from a vehicle synchronisation package.

Component Meaning in daily work Connector Sends agreed data to the connected system and reads its responses Integrated interface Displays settings, review cases and progress directly in Mira Rules and mappings Unambiguously relates vehicles, cost centres or ledger accounts Permissions Defines who may view, change, start or approve Additional storage Keeps required package information separate from the standard data model Reports Makes results and pending work traceable

docs.title: How the exchange works
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    A["Employee reviews or starts"] --> B["Mira stores the job"]
    B --> C["Central worker processes"]
    C --> D["Package connects external system"]
    D --> E["Response is validated"]
    E --> F["Result or review case in Mira"]

Transfers run in the background. Employees do not need to operate an additional connector application. Business approvals remain where required. Technical failures result in controlled retry or a visible review case.

docs.title: Example customer projects
docs.text:
Invoice hand-off to SAP: An invoice is reviewed in Mira, assigned to a vehicle and cost type, and approved. The agreed SAP coding is validated. The package then transfers the job and records the response. Transfer does not automatically mean that an invoice has been paid.

External system: An agreed package exchanges approved data with an external business system. Field mapping, the leading system and permitted changes are explicitly defined. Responses requiring review appear in Mira for processing.

Telematics: A package may exchange vehicle mappings and approved operational data with a telematics service. Scope, timestamps and polling intervals follow the confirmed contract of the selected service.

Customer-specific rules: Extra validation, approvals or reports may live in a dedicated customer package. A standard connector remains separate from customer-specific exceptions.

docs.title: Data responsibility
docs.text:
Before implementation, each data area has an agreed leading system, field mapping and conflict procedure. New records and updates need unambiguous identities. Ambiguous matches are reviewed rather than silently merged based on similar names or registration plates.

FLEET Mira is introduced as the successor product. Ongoing coupling with the previous fleet system is not planned. Any necessary one-time migration of existing data must be separately designed, validated and accepted.

Transfers contain explicitly agreed data only. Technical mappings, checksums and error records support reliable operation; a complete additional payload mirror is not created automatically.

docs.title: Operation and future development
docs.text:
External credentials remain on the execution server. Existing Mira roles and logs are intended to govern extensions too. Responsible users see successful runs, open jobs and errors and can make targeted corrections.

Packages and standard software are intended to evolve independently. Compatible versions are explicitly tested. Updates may need migrations and backup; returning to an older executable alone may be insufficient. These checks form part of the agreed operational procedure.

docs.title: Introduction in five steps
docs.text:
1. Assessment: Identify systems, data, access, responsible people and desired workflows.
  2. Target concept: Agree field mappings, leading systems, permissions, failure cases and acceptance criteria.
  3. Implementation: Configure the standard package and add required customer functions.
  4. Pilot: Reconcile representative cases in a test environment and review the results.
  5. Approval: Hand over operation, monitoring, backup and responsibilities.

docs.title: Services and quotation
docs.text:
FLEET Mira Custom is an Enterprise-based solution with separately agreed integration and development services. Licensing, analysis, implementation, migration, training and ongoing maintenance are separate quotation items. This concept establishes no binding prices, SAP certifications or guaranteed delivery dates.

The goal is a shared, maintainable product foundation with clearly bounded customer functions. The appropriate extension is chosen and accepted against the actual workflow.

Visual product flyer · Developer handbook

docs.title: Developer handbook
docs.text:
This document describes the target architecture of the FLEET Mira Expansion Package Framework. It is a baseline for implementation planning, interface contracts and acceptance testing. A package should connect external systems and customer-specific workflows without creating a customer-specific fork of the Mira product.

Design status

Web edition 1.0, 17 September 2026. Classes, manifests, tables and permissions described here are proposed contracts. Naming them does not imply that they are already implemented. Existing services should be reused, with missing extension points added deliberately.

docs.title: Architecture decisions
docs.text: Area Decision Product foundation Shared codebase; Custom is an extension and service offering, not a separate Core fork User interface PySide6 extensions within Mira navigation Background processing One shared handler in WorkerRuntime; Enterprise hosts it in FleetMiraWorker Connectors Versioned isolated processes controlled by the worker; initially no additional Windows service Mira business access Integration Gateway, Domain Services and Repositories External access Only approved package API, file or SQL adapters Storage Separate logical ownership of Core, framework and package data; no vendor-specific Core fields Cross-cutting services Reuse existing jobs, permissions, audit and secret management

docs.title: Existing components and new extension points
docs.text:
Existing reference points include worker_runtime.py, worker_coordination.py, database_runtime.py, user_management.py, global_audit.py, administration_ui.py and ui_jobs.py. Existing telematics adapters provide operational and integration examples. Their current implementation is not yet a generic Expansion Framework.

New work includes validated package registration, a manifest contract, a connector process manager, a gateway interface and defined UI extension points. A competing second queue, role or audit system is not intended. Existing import and retry mechanisms must be checked for their actual guarantees before being reused.

docs.title: Logical layers and process boundaries
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph Client["Enterprise Client"]
        UI["Core UI and Package UI"]
        S["Mira Services<br/>Permission check and job submission"]
        UI -->|"User action"| S
    end
    subgraph Server["Server and worker"]
        Q[("Framework jobs and status")]
        W["FleetMiraWorker<br/>WorkerRuntime and Expansion Manager"]
        G["Integration Gateway<br/>Domain Services and Repositories"]
        D[("Mira Core and package data")]
        Q -->|"Lease and job"| W
        W -->|"Validated result"| G
        G -->|"Transaction"| D
        W -->|"Progress and result status"| Q
    end
    subgraph Package["Separate connector process"]
        C["Backend Connector<br/>Adapter and mapping"]
    end
    E["External system"]
    S -->|"Store authorised job"| Q
    Q -->|"Read status"| S
    W -->|"Job through versioned protocol"| C
    C -->|"Result or DTO"| W
    C -->|"API or approved SQL"| E
    E -->|"Response"| C

Core denotes shared libraries and business services. It does not imply an additional central HTTP server. The Enterprise Client may submit jobs to PostgreSQL through existing Mira repositories. Central background effects run exclusively in the worker. The UI receives no external-system credentials.

The UI Extension runs in the client process; only the Backend Connector runs outside the worker process. Process isolation alone is not a security sandbox. A signed, approved package is still trusted executable code and requires a restricted operating account.

docs.title: Expansion Package structure
docs.text:
expansion-example/
  manifest.json
  backend/          Connector, transport, mapping, DTOs
  ui/               Navigation, settings, mappings, status
  database/         Versioned package-data migrations
  workflows/        Job definitions and business rules
  permissions/      Permission names and translations
  reports/          Optional reports
  schemas/          JSON schemas and examples
  tests/            Contract, mapping and integration tests

A package includes only the components it needs. A customer package may depend on a standard package and add rules or screens. Customer rules are not embedded as special cases in the standard connector.

docs.title: Manifest and registration
docs.text:
The following manifest is a proposal, not an installable format currently supported by the product:

{
  "id": "example-sap",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "vendor": "eh-systemhaus e.K.",
  "expansion_api": "1",
  "core_compatibility": ">=1.0,<2.0",
  "backend": {"entrypoint": "backend/connector.exe", "protocol": "1"},
  "ui": {"entrypoint": "ui.extension:register"},
  "capabilities": ["vehicle.pull", "invoice.push"],
  "permissions": ["example.view", "example.configure", "example.execute"],
  "database": {"namespace": "integration_example", "version": 1},
  "dependencies": []
}

Version ranges are examples. The implementation must define binding ranges for Core, SDK, protocol, UI and schema. Installation validates package ID, origin, signature, checksums, dependencies and paths. Paths must remain within the approved package directory; manifest values must not become arbitrarily composed shell commands.

The registry records installed and active versions, compatibility, schema version, capabilities and error state. Installation, activation and permission are distinct states. An incompatible package remains visible but is not loaded. Each package has one active version per defined installation or tenant.

docs.title: UI integration
docs.text:
A UI Extension registers navigation entries, workspace factories and actions through a bounded host interface. The host supplies context, authorisation, translation, regional formatting and service access. A possible interface includes navigation_items(), create_workspace(page_id, context) and register_actions().

Integration follows the existing administration and workspace patterns:

  • Non-selectable navigation group, selectable workspace and at most one local subtab level.
  • Search/filter area, shared action bar, data grid and status area for lists.
  • Dedicated record-detail work tabs for substantial editing; reopening focuses the same record.
  • Stable technical widget IDs and an empty work-tab area at session start.
  • Permission checks in both UI and called service; hidden buttons do not authorise an action.
  • Network and database work outside the Qt main thread.
  • All visible text in the 25 supported application languages; documentation in at least German and English.

For Enterprise/Custom, navigation could offer “Administration → Integrations → SAP”. Configuration, mappings, jobs and logs become suitable workspaces or a single local subtab level. An additional deep navigation hierarchy is unnecessary.

docs.title: Worker and process protocol
docs.text:
The Expansion Manager handles discovery, compatibility, activation and state. A subordinate connector process host launches approved programs, limits duration and output, and terminates hung processes. Scheduling, retry and job ownership remain in the shared worker runtime.

Version 1 should evaluate a versioned, framed JSON/NDJSON protocol over standard input/output. stdout contains protocol messages only; bounded, sanitised diagnostics use a separate channel. Messages identify protocol version, package, action, job and correlation. Larger datasets are transferred in bounded batches. Spool files are permitted only when needed, with ACLs, size limits, checksums and expiry.

{
  "protocol": 1,
  "job_id": "example-job",
  "correlation_id": "example-correlation",
  "package": "example-sap",
  "action": "vehicle.pull",
  "checkpoint": null
}

Results distinguish succeeded, retryable_error, validation_error and outcome_unknown. Errors contain stable codes and sanitised messages, never credentials. Subprocess termination, incomplete output or a lost connection after a possible creation must not be treated as a definitely unsuccessful write.

docs.title: Data contracts and Integration Gateway
docs.text:
Adapters translate external formats into small versioned DTOs, such as vehicle, person, cost centre or approved invoice line. Business identity, source tenant, external ID, date semantics, required fields and deletion semantics are explicit. Missing, empty and null are not automatically equivalent.

flowchart TB
    A["External response"] --> B["Connector mapping"]
    B --> C["Versioned DTO"]
    C --> D["Integration Gateway"]
    D --> E["Validation and permission"]
    E --> F["Domain Service"]
    F --> G["Repository and transaction"]
    G --> H["Mira business data and audit"]

Connectors never write directly to Mira Core business tables. The gateway also defines which objects a package may read. A SQL connector for an external system is different: it may execute explicitly agreed, parameterised SQL operations there.

docs.title: Storage and ownership
docs.text:
Area Owner Examples Mira Core Mira repositories and business logic Vehicles, people, costs and documents Framework Host repositories Package versions, technical mappings, checkpoints, jobs and run status Package data Registered package repositories and migrations Required account or workflow mappings External system Explicit backend adapter API requests or approved SQL

For Enterprise, logical separation into public, integration, integration_<package> or custom_<customer> is proposed. These are proposed schema names. Actual migrations must fit the existing database abstraction. New shared repository functions must introduce neither PostgreSQL-specific branches in business code nor direct sqlite3 connections. Affected shared functions must produce the same business result on SQLite and PostgreSQL.

By default the host manages package data through registered repositories too. Direct database access by an isolated connector is unnecessary and is not generally authorised. Required mappings are supplied to the job through controlled interfaces.

Technical object mappings are unique at least by environment, installation/tenant, external account, package, object type and external ID. A complete payload mirror is not an automatic framework feature. Retention, personal data and required comparison states are defined per package.

docs.title: Outbound processing
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant M as Mira Service
    participant DB as Mira Database
    participant W as FleetMiraWorker
    participant C as Connector
    participant X as External system
    U->>M: Approve transaction
    M->>DB: Business change and outbox in one transaction
    DB-->>M: Commit
    W->>DB: Claim job with lease
    W->>C: Job and idempotency key
    C->>X: External operation
    X-->>C: Confirmation and external ID
    C-->>W: Result
    W->>DB: Confirm mapping, status and audit

HTTP requests occur outside the business transaction. The worker must expect at-least-once delivery. If the target supports idempotency keys, the same key is reused for the same business job. Otherwise the outcome is reconciled before retry. An uncertain creation remains held for review. A local commit and an external HTTP effect are not one atomic transaction.

docs.title: Inbound processing and conflicts
docs.text:
The connector reads all relevant pages, validates the contract and returns DTOs. The host resolves technical identities and applies approved fields in a transaction. A checkpoint advances only after a complete fetch and the defined safe processing state. Fetch completeness and successful business application are reported separately.

Delta filters are permitted only if they include later updates to old records. Otherwise periodic full reconciliation is required. Registration plate, date or description alone do not justify an automatic merge. An existing external ID and explicit mapping take precedence; ambiguous matches enter the review queue.

System ownership is defined per field. Locally changed imported fields are compared with the last confirmed write state. A conflict must remain visible rather than disappear through silent overwriting.

docs.title: Permissions, secrets and audit
docs.text:
Package permissions join existing role management, for example view, configure, map, execute and approve. The worker rechecks package activation, action and job origin. External connections, secrets and target credentials remain on the worker side; client configurations contain references only.

Audit records relate the user or system actor, package version, action, object, result and correlation ID. Tokens, passwords and complete personal payloads do not belong in technical logs. Package installation, migration, permission changes and manual conflict decisions are also traceable.

A central status view shows the last successful run, oldest open job, pending reviews and data freshness. Retries use bounded backoff and Retry-After where applicable. Data errors and missing business mappings require correction rather than endless automatic retry.

docs.title: SAP package example
docs.text:
A SAP package may include connection setup, account/cost-centre mappings, approval, export status and reports. Valid rules map a cost type to company code, account, tax code and, where applicable, profit centre. This is a business mapping with validity dates and review status, not uncontrolled text conversion.

flowchart TB
    A["Review invoice"] --> B["Assign vehicle and cost type"]
    B --> C["Validate SAP coding"]
    C --> D["Approve"]
    D --> E["Outbox"]
    E --> F["Worker and SAP Connector"]
    F --> G["SAP confirmation"]

SAP illustrates package architecture here; it does not imply an already available connector or a particular SAP API.

docs.title: External systems and telematics
docs.text:
FLEET Mira is the successor product. The framework extends Mira and connects external business systems; ongoing synchronisation with the previous fleet system is not planned. Any required one-time migration belongs to a separate migration project.

flowchart TB
    UI["Mira Package UI"] -->|"Validated request"| Q["Mira job storage"]
    Q -->|"Lease and job"| W["FleetMiraWorker"]
    W -->|"Job"| P["Backend Connector"]
    P -->|"Approved API / SQL"| E["External system or telematics"]
    E -->|"Response"| P
    P -->|"DTO and technical status"| W
    W -->|"Validate and apply"| G["Mira Integration Gateway"]
    G -->|"Business logic and repository"| D[("Mira business data")]

Each concrete package needs a confirmed interface contract covering authentication, required fields, date semantics, pagination and update behaviour. Choosing API, file or direct SQL concerns the external target system, not a bypass into Mira Core tables.

The following rules apply:

  • Reconcile only explicitly agreed, semantically matching fields. Do not automatically add vendor-specific information as new Core fields.
  • New records are possible when identity, required fields and system ownership are confirmed.
  • Keep technical mappings, checksums and errors separate from business data. Do not retain mirrored payloads without a justified package contract.
  • Define data ownership and local editing per field. External statuses must not trigger local completion without agreed rules.
  • Configure schedules and data freshness per system. Without a reliable change filter, use complete reconciliation to capture updates to older records too.
  • External writes require clear retry and reconciliation rules. Resolve uncertain creation outcomes before writing again.
  • A SQL adapter uses fixed approved table/column names, bound parameters, restricted permissions and local transactions.
  • HTTP effects, external SQL transactions and Mira transactions are not automatically atomic. Failure boundaries and restart recovery belong to the package contract.

Implementation uses existing Mira host facilities for operation, scheduling, jobs and monitoring. An additional independent scheduler or Windows service is not planned.

docs.title: Versioning, installation and recovery
docs.text:
Core, Expansion API, package, UI and schema have separate versions. A package is validated and installed into a versioned directory, then migrated and activated under control. Running jobs finish or stop at a confirmed checkpoint before switching. New jobs start only with a consistent backend/UI/schema combination.

flowchart TB
    A["Install package"] --> B["Check signature and compatibility"]
    B --> C["Check backup and migration"]
    C --> D["Run migration"]
    D --> E["Activate and smoke-test"]
    E --> F["Monitor"]
    F --> G["Prepare update"]
    G --> B
    E -->|"Failure"| R["Deactivate and apply verified restore"]

Replacing an executable is not sufficient rollback after an incompatible data migration. Recovery requires backward-compatible schema or a verified backup/restore procedure. Program files are read-only; mutable configuration and state remain separate. UI bundles load only from approved packages, not arbitrary user-writable Python paths.

docs.title: Repository strategy and CI/CD
docs.text:
Mira Core retains host integration and shared business logic. A separate expansion repository may group SDK, protocol, schemas, testkit and standard packages. Customer packages may have private repositories. Separation is useful only when versioning and contract checks are reproducible; this document does not create those repositories.

The pipeline checks manifests, dependencies, package boundaries, unit/contract tests, migrations, UI compatibility and absence of secrets. It builds versioned artefacts, produces checksums, signs Windows components for release and tests installation, update and recovery. A release references tested Core, SDK, schema and package versions.

docs.title: Implementation and acceptance
docs.text:
1. Review the existing architecture and binding package contracts; define the Enterprise pilot and field ownership.
  2. Implement minimal registration and package validation; integrate a test package without external writes.
  3. Add a shared worker handler, process protocol, leases and error classes.
  4. Implement the gateway and technical mappings with transaction/conflict checks.
  5. Integrate the UI Extension with existing navigation, permissions and translations.
  6. Integrate the first external-system package using a confirmed contract and isolated test environment.
  7. Demonstrate pilot operation, restart recovery, update and restore before production approval.
Acceptance test Expected result Incompatible or modified package No activation; understandable error status Missing permission Action rejected on the service side too Repeated job No additional external or local creation Two workers Exclusive lease; a former owner cannot continue writing Crash after possible commit Uncertain outcome remains held and is reconciled Local field change Visible conflict; no silent loss API limit or expired token Bounded recovery without secrets in logs Version change Tested combination; traceable migration and restore UI and languages Shared navigation rules, stable IDs, complete translations Shared database function Same business result on SQLite and PostgreSQL

This document extends the documentation, not the application's delivered capabilities. General architecture rules remain binding during implementation.

docs.title: Product flyer
docs.text:
FLEET Mira Custom connects fleet processes with business IT. Expansion Packages group interfaces, integrated operation and customer-specific rules on a shared product foundation.

Target concept from September 2026

The illustration describes the proposed architecture. Packages and interfaces are implemented and approved per project.

Open full-resolution illustration

Operate in Mira Process centrally Connect systems Settings, mappings, review and status in the familiar workspace FleetMiraWorker controls jobs, retries and monitoring Package adapters connect ERP/accounting, external business systems and telematics

One package with the components required: Backend Connector · UI Extension · Workflow and Mapping · Permissions · separate package data and reports where needed.

Project path: Assessment → agreed concept → implementation → pilot → operational approval. Licensing, project services and maintenance are agreed separately.

Product role: FLEET Mira is the successor product. A permanent interface to the previous fleet system is not planned.

Architecture rule: External connectors change Mira Core data only through validated Mira services. Direct SQL may form part of an explicitly agreed adapter to an external system.

Customer concept · Developer handbook

docs.title: FLEET Mira Enterprise
docs.text: Enterprise runs FLEET Mira for separate customers on a centrally managed platform. Each tenant is an independent customer with its own PostgreSQL database, files and background context. A device or location group within one customer is not an Enterprise tenant.

docs.title: Which edition fits?
docs.text:
Edition Database Background processing Deployment Basic / Pro Local SQLite database Inside the application Single workstation according to license scope Enterprise PostgreSQL; separate control and customer databases Independent FleetMiraWorker Servers, multiple clients, RDP/Citrix and separate customers

User identities and memberships are managed centrally. A customer role applies only to that customer; a customer administrator does not become a platform administrator. One user can belong to multiple customers with different roles.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C[Enterprise Client] --> A[FleetMiraApi]
    A --> P[(Control database)]
    A --> T[(Tenant databases)]
    W[FleetMiraWorker] --> T
    W --> F[Tenant-bound archives]
    W --> R[Local provisioning service]

The client signs in centrally and opens only an authorized tenant. It does not start a local worker. API, worker, archive service, provisioning service and PostgreSQL remain independent of an open client. Enterprise has no SQLite fallback.

An all-in-one server hosts these independent components together. In a distributed installation, clients connect through the configured HTTPS address; database and file access must be reachable and protected according to the actual topology. A successful single-server test does not replace network or load acceptance.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Verified downloads and checksums
  2. Installation and setup
  3. Set up tenants
  4. Activate base and add-on licenses
  5. Backup and restore
  6. Services and Health page

Beta9 R3

This is an unsigned beta release. Verify the published SHA-256 values and test updates with a verified restore. Licensed customer capacity consists of a base license including one tenant and separate add-on licenses for further tenants.

docs.title: Verified build: 1.1.0-beta9, R3, 8 November 2026
docs.text:
Use both packages from the same release. The Enterprise client and server components share one codebase. Basic/Pro installers are not intended for Windows Server or terminal servers.

File Size in bytes Download Enterprise application and services 806318386 Enterprise installer PostgreSQL server 365528643 PostgreSQL installer Checksums Text file SHA256SUMS-Enterprise-R3.txt Build identity JSON enterprise-r3-manifest.json Protected setup inputs PowerShell Permission audit and ACL backup

Release notes and all files

docs.title: Verify the download
docs.text:
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath .\FLEET-Mira-Enterprise-1.1.0-beta9-Setup-x64.exe
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath .\FLEET-Mira-PostgreSQL-Server-1.1.0-beta9-Setup-x64.exe

Enterprise: 1e818799ce07b7bbfbba53e3ed4605f134a4a16c15b9d47cee795489711d8999.

PostgreSQL: a1a3ad0ac3264a13351d5ae88403ad9f1d5475af49cb824d322db42e8ebc4f89.

Do not install if a value differs. Also verify the standalone PowerShell routine against the release checksums and review it before execution.

Unsigned beta

R3 is not Authenticode signed. This documentation does not remove Windows publisher warnings. These are the exact verified R3 packages; existing release assets are not replaced. The build identity explicitly records the source commit and its dirty working-tree state.

docs.title: Requirements and next steps
docs.text:
64-bit Windows, administrative installation rights, sufficient local storage, planned backup destinations, and appropriate DNS/TLS and network access are required. The verified single-server environment used Windows Server 2025 and PostgreSQL 17.10; other topologies require their own acceptance. Further tenants require an appropriate add-on license in addition to the base license.

Continue with installation and setup. Older downloads remain in the release list; their functionality must not be assumed equivalent to R3.

Some existing beta screens retain German labels in other language profiles. The documentation identifies this limitation; R3 installers are published unchanged.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
Component Responsibility Verification FleetMiraApi HTTPS, central sign-in, tenant authorization and enabled interfaces Health page, API status and local console FleetMiraWorker Central jobs, periodic tasks, license checks and tenant workers Heartbeat, job status and actual result PostgreSQL Control database and separate customer databases Connectivity, availability, backups and free space FleetMiraArchive Authorized access to bound archives Archive access and integrity evidence FleetMiraProvisioner Locally restricted privileged provisioning Provisioning status; no public listener

The client enqueues central work. A running Windows service or registered worker node alone does not prove business readiness. Check heartbeat age, licensing, database and job results together.

docs.title: Health in the browser
docs.text:
Open the configured address with /health, for example https://fleet.example.internal:8443/health. The public overview displays technical status without business records. Before user authentication the language is English; authenticated views use available profile language and region.

API, worker and PostgreSQL appear in separate sections. Resource values identify measurement time and origin; missing values are not zeros. Stale heartbeats are marked explicitly. Sections stack vertically on small screens.

Sign in as an authorized platform administrator for protected logs and administration. The public overview grants no service control, token administration or access to other customers' data. Multi-tenant operation requires central platform privileges in addition to relevant business tenant authorization.

docs.title: Local console
docs.text:
If HTTPS is unavailable, open FLEET Mira API on the server or run locally:

DLTNGDownloadTool.exe --api-console

The console displays local service state and sanitized events. Start/stop requires appropriate Windows rights. Without Mira sign-in its language remains English. A completely stopped API service cannot serve its own website.

docs.title: Common diagnosis
docs.text:
Observation Next step HTTPS unavailable Check DNS, certificate, bind address, firewall and local API service Process running, worker stale Allow delayed startup; check service identity, PostgreSQL connection and worker log License blocked Check platform license and matching tenant add-on; do not use a local substitute key Job queued Check maintenance state, active processing and queue; do not merely count nodes Job failed Check sanitized error and actual external effect; avoid unverified duplicate jobs Customer access denied Check active central identity, membership and role for that customer

/health/live and the minimal JSON response prove process liveness, not valid licensing or successful background processing. After repairs, recheck sign-in, tenant access and an authorized test job.

For detailed settings, API privileges, certificates and diagnostic fields, see the FleetMiraApi reference.

docs.title: Set up tenants
docs.text: The English selection dialog calls customer tenants Clients. This guide uses “tenant” for the isolated customer context.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Set up the platform according to the installation guide. Sign in centrally as a platform administrator. An administrator of an existing customer cannot create further customers or administer global users.

Check the following first:

  • FleetMiraApi, FleetMiraWorker and the local provisioning service are available and ready.
  • An active central user is designated as the new tenant's first administrator. Matching email addresses do not create automatic identity links.
  • The base license is active. It includes the first tenant; every further tenant requires an add-on matching this platform, base license and tenant identity.
  • Database templates, data roots and archives are configured through trusted server-side setup. The client does not accept database passwords, connection strings or storage roots.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. After central sign-in, open Clients → Administration → Clients → Set up tenant.
  2. Enter a readable customer name and a unique technical identifier.
  3. Select an active central user as the first tenant administrator. Their role in other customers remains independent.
  4. Review the summary. Back returns to previous inputs; the header arrow can return to the tenant overview.
  5. Select Set up. Processing continues on the server; closing the wizard does not cancel an already submitted request.
  6. Refresh provisioning status. The customer is published for sign-in only after successful setup.

docs.title: License additional tenants
docs.text:
When entitlement is missing, the request waits for an add-on license. Obtain the key matching this request and activate it through the provided licensing action. Do not use a key already bound to another tenant. Activation and provisioning can require several refreshes.

Follow the licensing guide. Do not bypass a failed request by creating databases manually or rebinding a key. Technical errors and missing entitlement are separate conditions.

docs.title: Select and switch tenants
docs.text:
