After sign-in, the client displays authorized customers. Select the required tenant; a single membership can proceed directly. A status window reports session setup, database connection, settings, license checking and dashboard startup.

Switching tenants ends the previous client context and opens the new customer with its own connection and caches. Save open work first. Closing the main window normally exits the entire client; independent server services continue running.

docs.title: Verify the result
docs.text: Open both customers separately and check the displayed tenant identity. Check memberships and roles for each customer. A user without membership must not open that customer. Then configure backup and service monitoring. Accounts, paths and company details in these images are sample data only.

docs.title: Cost analysis and reporting
docs.text:
The Cost analysis workspace evaluates booked vehicle costs only. Credits and reversal entries retain their accounting sign. Users can select net or gross amounts.

Open the workspace through Fleet management > Fleet > Cost analysis. By default, a newly opened analysis covers January 1 of the current year through today. Administrators can select the last twelve months or a configurable rolling number of days as the global default under Administration > Cost analysis > Calculation parameters. A changed default applies the next time the cost analysis is opened; filters already edited in an open workspace remain unchanged.

Choose period, optional vehicle, All/Fixed/Variable, net or gross and a report template, then select Refresh analysis. Total cost is the period-allocated booked cost including credits and cancellations. It is the TCO data basis for the selected period; it is not claimed to be lifetime-complete when categories or periods are missing.

The KPI strip separates Total cost, eligible cost, eligible kilometres, cost/km and data basis. Total cost remains complete while cost/km uses only jointly reliable vehicle-months.

docs.title: Mileage basis
docs.text:
M files provide an end-of-day odometer value for each included UTC day. FLEET Mira stores it at the following day's 00:00 UTC boundary. Vehicle-use, place and three-hour GNSS records from C files supplement the history.

Cost analysis and mileage reports use the same OdometerBoundaryResolver. Only qualified VALID or WARNING readings are eligible; manual, unknown, unverified and conflicting values are excluded.

Source priority is:

  1. signature-valid M-file midnight reading;
  2. GPS-server telematics sensor;
  3. C-file vehicle use;
  4. C-file place;
  5. C-file three-hour GNSS;
  6. GPS-server telematics GPS.

Cost per kilometre is calculated at vehicle-month level. The first and last month are clipped to the selected range. A vehicle-month is included only when it contains at least one cost entry, reliable period boundaries and positive mileage. Missing boundaries follow the same administrative rule as mileage reports: incomplete, interpolated or bounded extrapolation. For a missing opening boundary, the central policy can extrapolate backwards from the first qualified following days; for a missing closing boundary, it projects forwards from preceding readings. During the current local day, an available qualified actual reading is used; otherwise the central policy can extrapolate up to the current calculation instant. The same estimated mileage is therefore available to cost/km. Opening and closing readings are rounded to whole kilometres first; the difference is then exactly closing minus opening. The Odometer readings per vehicle and day report exposes the same boundaries and estimation supports for direct audit.

Total cost continues to include every cost in the selected range. Eligible cost, eligible mileage and cost/km include matching vehicle-months only. Vehicles or months without costs or mileage therefore no longer suppress metrics for complete subsets.

Coverage is shown as eligible cost-bearing vehicle-months. The column heading explains the metric generally; each value's tooltip states the actual number of cost and eligible months and lists the vehicle's concrete monthly mileage warnings. The interface displays Complete for full coverage, Partial for a usable subset, and Mileage data missing when costs exist without a cost/km basis. No costs and No data identify individual vehicles or months without costs or without either data type.

Import tachograph data reparses older M archives that do not yet contain extracted daily odometer values. Values that cannot be matched uniquely by VIN or registration remain visible for resolution.

Under Administration > Cost analysis > Odometer history, filter by vehicle, import older tachograph data or enter a manual reading. Manual readings require timestamp, value and note and rank below M-file midnight readings.

docs.title: Cost rules
docs.text:
• Variable costs belong to the period containing their document date.
  • Fixed costs are allocated by day across their validity range.
  • Fixed costs without a complete validity range produce a data-quality warning.
  • Vehicle-months with mileage but no cost entry are not treated as zero-cost input for the fleet ratio.
  • Entries that net to zero still count as an existing cost basis.
  • When an entry is cancelled, the cancelled original and its booked counter-entry are evaluated together and therefore net to zero.
  • Comparisons cover the immediately preceding equal-length period and the previous-year period.

docs.title: Views and KPIs
docs.text:
• Vehicles shows fixed, variable and total cost, eligible subset, kilometres, cost/km, coverage and quality per vehicle.
  • Categories identifies the categories driving the TCO data basis.
  • Trend compares monthly values including cost/km and coverage.
  • Comparisons contrasts current period, direct predecessor and prior year and evaluates changes using the administrative materiality threshold.
  • Bookings lists included entries with vehicle, supplier, category and allocated amount.
  • Data quality explains missing boundaries, unassigned mileage and incomplete fixed-cost periods.

docs.title: Stimulsoft
docs.text:
View report opens the local Reports.JS viewer. Export requires finance.reporting.export. Users with reporting.templates.write can clone a system template and edit the copy. System templates remain immutable.

The Reports.JS runtime is loaded from assets/stimulsoft or STIMULSOFT_ASSET_DIR. Licensing is read only from STIMULSOFT_LICENSE_KEY or STIMULSOFT_LICENSE_FILE.

The report host listens on 127.0.0.1 only and uses a random session token for each opened report.

docs.title: Deadlines and record documents
docs.text: Deadlines and documents are maintained directly against a person or vehicle record. Both use stable object IDs, permission checks and record-level audit events, so the complete history remains available from the related record.

docs.title: Evaluate deadlines
docs.text:
Open Fleet management → Personnel → Deadline evaluation or Fleet → Deadline evaluation. Search and filters cover object, due type, state, basis, trigger, mileage quality, evaluability and date range.

Figure: Filterable personnel deadlines with lead-time and completion states.

Status colours distinguish items outside the lead period, approaching or due today, overdue and completed. Printing, print preview and PDF include only the visible filtered rows and columns.

docs.title: Time and mileage rules
docs.text:
Personnel deadlines are time-based. Vehicle deadlines may use:

  • Time: due date, time lead and optional time recurrence;
  • Odometer: target mileage, mileage lead and optional mileage recurrence;
  • Earliest of both: the first reached limit determines the state and completion trigger.

The evaluation shows the latest reliable odometer reading, its timestamp and source, target and remaining mileage, trigger and data quality. Without a valid reading, a combined deadline keeps its time evaluation but marks the mileage part as partial. A mileage-only deadline remains not evaluable until a reliable reading exists.

System-managed download and driving-licence deadlines cannot be moved or completed manually. Their source workflow updates them automatically.

docs.title: Maintain a record document
docs.text:
1. Open a person or vehicle record and select Documents.
  2. Add a file by selection or drag-and-drop.
  3. Enter title, document date, type and optional notes.
  4. Review Valid until. A new value is calculated from the document date and the configured record-document retention period.
  5. Save and verify the preview for PDF or image documents.

Figure: An anonymised person record containing documents, deadlines, licence checks and audit.

Figure: An anonymised vehicle record containing documents, deadlines, finance and tachodata.

New versions retain the document relationship and history. The byte-identical original is written atomically to the primary document archive. A configured backup job copies and reads it back separately; successful local creation does not claim that an external backup already exists.

docs.title: Archive, restore and purge
docs.text: Logical archiving is available from the document context menu and requires the appropriate write permission. Local restore and permanent purge are restricted administrative actions. Permanent purge requires confirmation and a mandatory reason; the evidence record and audit trail remain.

docs.title: Reports and audit
docs.text: The report dashboard provides Personnel deadlines and Fleet deadlines. Fleet reports additionally include time/mileage basis, trigger, odometer quality and evaluability. Every create, change, completion, archive, document view, restore and purge operation is represented in global and record-level audit.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: State Action Mileage deadline is not evaluable Import/link a current M file or add a verified manual odometer reading. Combined deadline shows partial The time result is valid; investigate the missing or implausible mileage reading. Valid-until date is unexpected Check document date, region display and the separate record-document retention setting. Document preview is unavailable Verify the file type and open the byte-identical original with an authorised local application. Backup is still pending Keep the local original; inspect the backup task and worker status instead of adding the document again.

docs.title: Driver-card analysis
docs.text: The analysis is always bound to one selected C file and archive ID. M data is comparison evidence only. Quarantined files remain viewable but cannot feed an effective combined evaluation.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Figure: Card identity, validity, authorities, generation and data range.

The header identifies the anonymised driver, card and file. A quarantine banner explains missing or invalid signature verification. Empty values mean that the selected file does not contain the information or it could not be read safely.

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
Figure: Sortable UTC intervals with C/M availability.

Data availability filters all intervals, C and M available, C only or M only. C remains the base. Rows include start, end, duration, activity, card, slot and counterpart archives; double-click and context actions open unambiguous sources.

The single-file view remains archive-scoped. Personnel record > Day/Week/Violations, by contrast, combines all valid card links for that person, including card changes. The heading identifies record or archive scope and must be considered when interpreting totals.

docs.title: Day chart
docs.text:
Figure: One UTC day with driving, work, availability and rest/break.

The date, arrow buttons and Go to change the visible day. The availability track indicates C/M coverage, while activity tracks show business intervals. The detail grid remains sortable.

Read left to right in UTC. Colour and label distinguish driving, other work, availability and rest/break; gaps and overlaps are not smoothed. Hover a segment for start, end, duration, source and availability. Day totals apply to the visible day, not the entire file.

docs.title: Week chart
docs.text:
Figure: ISO week from Monday to Sunday.

Seven UTC days are shown together. Empty days remain visible and are not interpreted as activity. Totals and tooltips refer to the selected file and visible period.

Week arrows move between ISO weeks; Go to selects the week containing a date. Review coverage and card validity first, then daily patterns and weekly totals. An empty or partially covered day is not evidence of rest.

docs.title: DDD week view Web
docs.text:
Figure: Secure in-app entry point to the browser-based week view.

The page starts the local web view through a tokenised hand-off; local archive paths do not appear in its URL. Documentation deliberately does not load a signed original DDD into an external page.

docs.title: Events and faults
docs.text:
Figure: Technical event and fault records.

Codes, periods, vehicles and descriptions come from the selected card. An empty page means no matching record exists; it does not mean records were removed.

docs.title: Vehicles used
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle references with usage range and odometer values.

Only vehicles reported by this C file are listed. A vehicle-record link is offered only for an unambiguous master-data match.

docs.title: Positions
docs.text:
Figure: PLACE and GNSS records with nation, region and coordinates.

Open position map displays visible coordinates. Nation and region are shown as readable text plus technical value where possible. See Position maps.

docs.title: Violations
docs.text:
Figure: Reproducible technical pre-check for the selected C file.

The list explains rule, article, actual/target value, deviation and legal basis. It does not replace legal assessment of national exemptions, AETR or Article 12 cases. Saving a snapshot requires archive.manage; export requires archive.export.

Select evaluation period and enabled rule modules and recalculate whenever context changes. Results identify ruleset/module version, assessment range, calculation basis and severity; optional BALM amounts are guidance, not a fine decision. Review coverage and notices before each finding. Cross-module findings are consolidated only for the same driver, period and fact pattern.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
Figure: Certificate chain and signed-EF results.

VALID confirms a verified chain and all present signatures. INVALID and UNVERIFIABLE quarantine the file; the unchanged archive object remains available for evidence-preserving export.

docs.title: Importing e-invoices and XRechnung
docs.text: The guided importer processes UBL Invoice, UBL Credit Note, CII and hybrid PDF with embedded invoice XML. It reads the file safely, validates its structure and runs the bundled KoSIT validator. Nothing is written to the ledger until Create foreign-invoice draft is selected.

docs.title: Read and validate the file
docs.text:
Open Fleet > Import XRechnung, select an XML or PDF, or drop it onto the supplier-invoice list. This entry point opens the common maximised document review. The file appears at the top with local/AI state, progress and XRechnung state; Validate XRechnung determines syntax, profile, Customization ID, hashes and available components. The PDF or XML remains visible on the left while header, tax and positions are reviewed in the supplier-invoice form on the right.

Invalid documents are rejected without creating a draft. The KoSIT report remains available in the session and can be exported. Warnings require a business review; the summary identifies validator version and error/warning counts.

docs.title: Verify invoice data
docs.text: Compare document number and type, document/delivery/due dates, buyer reference or cost centre, currency, payment terms, and net, VAT and gross totals with the original. Credit notes are detected as a separate document type. Unsupported currencies or inconsistent totals are rejected.

docs.title: Match the supplier
docs.text: FLEET Mira compares VAT, tax, endpoint and company identifiers plus name and address with supplier master data. Review score and reason, then accept the best suggestion or select another supplier. If none exists, create a supplier from invoice data and verify it before continuing.

docs.title: Assign lines to vehicles and categories
docs.text: Every source line must be assigned completely to one or more vehicles and a cost category. ML suggestions are aids, not automatic booking decisions. Split line distributes a line to several vehicles or categories to the cent; Remove split removes the selected allocation. Source quantity, unit, net, VAT and gross remain traceable.

docs.title: Reconcile totals
docs.text: The tab compares invoice, source-line and allocation totals. Open net and gross must be zero for every line. Rounding differences, residual amounts or an unconfirmed supplier block creation of the draft.

docs.title: XML, PDF and validation report
docs.text: Invoice XML shows the structured source and KoSIT report the validation details. Hybrid PDF adds a PDF document tab. Preview uses an isolated temporary profile and never replaces the byte-identical original.

docs.title: Create the foreign-invoice draft
docs.text:
Choose Save as draft or Accept as verified after validation, supplier, assignments and totals are complete. FLEET Mira atomically creates the invoice, source reference, assignments and locally verified original. Failure leaves no partial invoice. An already imported source hash is handled as a possible duplicate.

Open the resulting invoice tab, check its status bar, e-invoice data and originals, and complete the normal verification and booking workflow. Import requires finance.manage and the Pro E-invoice import feature; verification and booking additionally require finance.verify and finance.book.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
State Action KoSIT status rejected Open the report and request a corrected source document. Supplier is ambiguous Check identifiers in supplier master data or create a controlled record. Create action disabled Confirm the supplier and assign every line exactly. Totals differ Correct splits, VAT rates and rounding residuals. Hybrid PDF has no XML Request supported XML or a proper hybrid PDF.

Language of some beta dialogs

Some older labels remain German in the English profile. The current Material 3 captures show the actual beta interface without retouching.

docs.title: Foreign invoices
docs.text: Double-click a foreign invoice to open its own work tab. The status strip shows workflow, validity, local document and export states plus net/gross total, allocated amount and difference. Green means an exact cent-level match; red blocks verification.

docs.title: Capture from a document
docs.text:
In Pro and Enterprise, From document is available beside New. PDF, image, XML and hybrid PDF files open the same maximised review screen as document-assisted lease creation. The original, page controls, zoom and evidence locations are on the left; the familiar supplier-invoice form, tax rows, positions and recurring-invoice amount periods remain editable on the right. The document table shows local analysis, latest AI analysis, XRechnung state, progress and errors for each file.

Focusing a candidate automatically opens the correct document and page. Blue is a preview; only Apply or the candidate checkbox accepts the value and its concrete evidence location. Unique candidates may be preselected transiently. Ambiguous candidates remain open until the user accepts one or confirms a manual value. Cancelling discards the technical session and all temporary documents.

Dates, numbers, percentages and monetary amounts use the signed-in user's region in the form, candidate list and hints; ISO dates, integer cents and basis points remain unchanged internally. A wheel gesture over a date, selection or numeric editor scrolls the form and does not change the field value.

flowchart TD
    A["Supplier invoices"] --> B{"Entry point"}
    B -->|"New"| C["Manual invoice form"]
    B -->|"From document"| D["PDF, image, XML or hybrid PDF"]
    B -->|"Import XRechnung"| D
    D --> E["PDF text, OCR or structured invoice data"]
    E --> F["Optional consented AI analysis"]
    F --> G["Review document and evidence on the left"]
    G --> H["Confirm header, tax and positions on the right"]
    H --> I{"Invoice kind"}
    I -->|"Single"| J["Assign position to one vehicle"]
    I -->|"Collective"| K["Allocate positions across vehicles"]
    I -->|"Recurring"| L["Review amount periods and components"]
    J --> M{"Finish"}
    K --> M
    L --> M
    M -->|"Minimum data available"| N["Save as draft"]
    M -->|"Complete and exact"| O["Accept as verified"]

Import XRechnung remains visible as a separate entry point but uses this same review workspace and starts with structured validation. Valid XML totals and tax rows are authoritative; OCR and AI never replace them silently.

docs.title: Header and supplier
docs.text:
The saved invoice record refreshes status labels, totals and dates from its loaded data using the current language and region. Completing document-assisted capture stops session timers, closes preview and removes its temporary preview copy. A saved original remains in the financial archive; declining discard keeps capture open.

Under Fleet > Foreign invoices > New, enter supplier, document type, invoice kind, number and date, delivery/validity period and payment terms. In the manual tax table, enter the taxable base for every VAT rate; FLEET Mira calculates read-only net, VAT and gross totals with commercial cent rounding. A 19% row is preselected and additional rates including 0% are supported. A credit or cancellation also references its original invoice.

The Supplier tab shows master data and e-invoice identifiers used for the document. Document data also shows dates, the VAT rate or complete tax breakdown, and net, VAT and gross totals.

docs.title: Positions
docs.text:
Every position belongs to one vehicle and category. Document date, valid from/to and Variable are inherited and locked. Costs increase and credits reduce the allocated amount. All positions must match invoice gross exactly.

For collective invoices, Split position distributes one source amount across any number of vehicles and allocates a possible VAT cent deterministically. A draft assignment is edited directly. After booking, Correct assignment creates a counter-entry on the wrong vehicle and a new posting on the correct one; already exported data receives a separate RECLASSIFICATION correction export.

docs.title: Original documents
docs.text: Add original document first writes the file atomically to the local financial archive, reads it back and verifies SHA-256. Locally verified enables verification, booking, preview and export. Back up documents now optionally replicates pending objects; failed external backup never blocks the business workflow. Preview uses a temporary copy.

docs.title: E-invoice
docs.text: For structured imports this tab shows syntax, profile, validator, errors/warnings and every source line with its allocation count. Original, XML and KoSIT report remain separate verified document roles. See Importing e-invoices and XRechnung.

docs.title: Document analysis
docs.text:
Image PDFs and scans are analysed locally first using embedded text or the bundled PDFium/Tesseract OCR runtime. Rules and confirmed historical assignments provide review-only supplier, vehicle and lease-contract suggestions. Cloud analysis through an Azure or Vertex provider configured under Administration > AI connector requires explicit consent for each document. The original, hash, result, model, confidence and evidence remain traceable together; no assignment is confirmed automatically. If the OCR runtime or language model is unexpectedly unavailable, the analysis ends with a technical failure and is never stored as an apparently successful empty suggestion.

A recurring invoice may be saved without a contract assignment and linked later. An unambiguously recognised active lease contract is only proposed and must be confirmed explicitly. The direct Recurring invoice from document action in an active lease file instead fixes vehicle, supplier and contract and stores the verified invoice and assignment together.

docs.title: Verify, book and correct
docs.text:
1. Complete header and positions in Draft.
  2. Ensure the required original is locally verified.
  3. Bring the difference to 0.00 and Verify.
  4. Use finance.book to Book immutably.
  5. Optionally export through accounting REST or CSV/ZIP.

Booked records are never overwritten or deleted. Cancel creates a counter-entry with a mandatory reason; a linked credit represents a commercial correction. Both preserve origin and use the correct sign in analysis.

docs.title: Export history and audit
docs.text:
Only booked or cancelled invoices may be exported. Idempotency keys prevent duplicates; external ID, timestamp and error remain visible for retries.

Creation, edits, verification, booking, cancellation, document verification and export are recorded. Navigation and preview create no event. Reading requires finance.read, editing finance.manage, verification finance.verify, booking finance.book, and export finance.export; Pro adapters also require their licence feature.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: State Action Verify disabled Check local document state and difference; e-invoice lines must be assigned completely. Difference red Correct position amounts, signs and rounding residuals. Document backup failed The local original remains usable; fix the target and retry backup. Booked invoice locked Create a cancellation or linked credit instead of overwriting it.

docs.title: Lease contracts
docs.text: Lease management combines contract terms, pre-calculation, payment schedule, contract documents, recurring invoices and actual costs from supplier invoices. Manual contract management is available in every edition. Document analysis, XInvoice, OCR, local ML and the optional AI connector follow the Pro/Enterprise licence boundary; the Report dashboard is likewise available in Pro and Enterprise.

docs.title: Overview and contract record
docs.text:
Open Fleet → Lease contracts. Filter the overview by contract number, vehicle, supplier and status. New starts manual entry. From document starts a temporary document-assisted intake. Double-click or Open lease contract opens the contract in a dedicated work tab; reopening an existing contract focuses its tab instead of creating a duplicate.

Figure: Lease overview with search, status filter, and manual and document-assisted creation.

The contract record separates Contract, Calculation, Payment schedule, Documents, Supplier invoices, Recurring invoices, Costs/Credits and Audit. This keeps vehicle, supplier, period, rate and status distinct from actual postings and archived evidence.

Figure: Contract record with anonymised vehicle reference and M-data evidence.

docs.title: Current end-to-end workflow
docs.text:
The highlighted evidence heading identifies the currently selected field. The heading, evidence rows, evidence quality and loading status follow the signed-in user's language after a language change and after document preview completes. Quantities, numbers and dates follow the region independently. The current selection and explicitly accepted evidence are retained. Document quotations retain their original wording.

The current workflow uses the same lease form for manual and document-assisted creation. OCR, XInvoice and AI provide proposals only; vehicle, supplier, contract values, recurring-invoice phases, activation and posting mode are always confirmed in one final review. Post automatically does not create all future instalments as costs immediately: FLEET Mira prepares the monthly occurrences and posts each one only on its due date.

flowchart TD
    A["Lease overview"] --> B{"Creation method"}
    B -->|"New"| C["Complete the shared lease form manually"]
    B -->|"From document"| D["Add contract, recurring invoice, PDF, image or XML"]
    D --> E["Evaluate PDF text, OCR and XInvoice data locally"]
    E --> F{"Required value missing, conflict or low confidence?"}
    F -->|"Yes and consent granted"| G["AI connector adds reviewable proposals"]
    F -->|"No or no cloud consent"| H["Use local proposals or complete values manually"]
    G --> I["Review document on the left and form on the right"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["Accept concrete evidence and resolve conflicts"]
    J --> C

    C --> K["Review vehicle, supplier and contract values"]
    K --> L{"Enter a recurring invoice?"}
    L -->|"No"| M["Prepare contract for final review"]
    L -->|"Yes"| N["Edit amount phases and additional components"]
    N --> O["Confirm periods, net, tax, gross and component assignments"]
    O --> M

    M --> P["Combined final confirmation"]
    P --> Q{"Activate lease contract?"}
    Q -->|"No"| R["Contract remains a draft; recurring invoice may be PENDING_ACTIVATION"]
    Q -->|"Yes"| S["Activate contract and create payment schedule"]
    S --> T{"Recurring-invoice posting mode"}
    T -->|"AUTO – default"| U["Prepare monthly occurrences idempotently"]
    T -->|"MANUAL"| V["Provide due occurrence as READY_FOR_REVIEW"]

    U --> W{"Is the period already due?"}
    W -->|"No"| X["Visible only in payment schedule and recurring invoices"]
    W -->|"Yes"| Y{"Complete and conflict-free?"}
    Y -->|"Yes"| Z["Post monthly occurrence automatically"]
    Y -->|"No"| AA["REVIEW_REQUIRED with an understandable correction action"]
    V --> AB["User reviews and posts"]
    Z --> AC["Costs/credits, planned/actual reconciliation and accounting export"]
    AB --> AC

The most important transitions are:

  • Without activation, the contract remains a draft; an already confirmed recurring invoice waits as PENDING_ACTIVATION.
  • In AUTO mode only due, complete and conflict-free periods are posted. Future periods remain visible in the payment schedule and the Recurring invoices tab.
  • READY_FOR_REVIEW requires manual posting; REVIEW_REQUIRED signals a business or technical conflict and prevents an automatic partial posting.
  • A period appears under Costs/Credits and enters planned/actual reconciliation and accounting export only after it has been posted.

docs.title: Manual entry
docs.text:
The existing lease form remains the shared destination for manual and document-assisted creation. One contract belongs to exactly one vehicle and one supplier. Required fields carry a trailing *:

  • vehicle and supplier;
  • contract number;
  • start, end and term;
  • net list price;
  • actual net lease rate.

List price and actual rate must be greater than zero. Empty required values receive a red border and a localised hint. Date, number, currency and percentage fields use the authenticated user's region; ISO dates, integer cents and basis points remain authoritative internally.

Excess and shortfall mileage prices use EUR/km with four decimal places, for example 0.1138 EUR/km and 0.0375 EUR/km. They are stored precisely as micro-euros rather than rounded whole cents. OCR and AI distinguish finance rates from adjacent service rates; explicit locally readable evidence checks the scaling of AI proposals. Migration preserves the value of existing cent-based prices; previously accepted incorrect prices must be checked again against the original.

Numeric fields can be cleared completely with the keyboard. Empty is not the same as 0: required fields remain marked red and must be completed before saving. The optional Due day can remain empty, including after reopening; monthly due dates continue to follow the First due date.

The mouse wheel only scrolls the contract area. The active editor, cursor position and existing text selection remain unchanged when scrolling down and back up. This applies to manual creation, editing and document-assisted creation. Clicking another field or using Tab/Shift+Tab changes the input focus.

Contract date and handover date default to the current date. The start initially follows the contract date. End and planned return are derived from start and term, while the first due date follows the start. Contradictory inputs are never silently overwritten.

The vehicle selector searches vehicle number, registration and VIN. The supplier selector searches supplier number, name and creditor number. Only an explicitly selected result is stored.

Figure: Shared lease form with required markers, regional editors and dependent contract dates.

docs.title: Creating from documents
docs.text:
From document accepts a contract, recurring invoice, PDF, image, standalone XInvoice XML or hybrid PDF/XInvoice. Multiple documents can contribute to one intake, but an intake creates exactly one contract for one vehicle and at most one primary recurring invoice.

flowchart TD
    A["Lease overview"] --> B{"Creation method"}

Source precedence prevents an uncertain proposal from silently replacing better data: valid XInvoice data is authoritative for invoice and tax values, followed by embedded text and local rules, the bundled PDFium/Tesseract OCR runtime, and finally approved AI proposals. Every transfer to a cloud provider requires explicit consent for that document. A missing OCR component produces a visible technical failure rather than SUCCEEDED with an empty result.

While document analysis is running, the document list, viewer and Cancel remain available; contract fields and Save are locked. A business-level analysis failure does not prevent manual completion. The document list shows document type, source, XInvoice status, analysis status, progress and errors. Local and AI analysis appear on separate lines in the status column. The additional progress indicator visualises queued work, running processing as an animated bar, and terminal success or failure for each document. Without cloud approval it shows AI analysis: Not requested; a running or completed request also names the provider. If several AI runs exist, the latest request is authoritative. Verify validates XInvoice content in PDF, XML and hybrid documents. A subsequent local location search for legacy AI results runs separately in the background: Evidence locations: Being prepared and an animated bar remain visible while the form and document navigation are already responsive again.

Figure: Maximised responsive review screen with document controls, highlighted evidence, candidates and the unchanged lease form.

docs.title: Conflicts, missing values and evidence
docs.text:
Initially, the candidate list is empty and the document is shown as a whole page. Clicking a form field, deliberately navigating with Tab, or choosing Evidence location activates its proposals and document highlights. The highlighted heading above the list identifies the active field. Scrolling, automatic form refreshes and changes to which fields are visible do not change the candidate list or the last preview.

An actual click or Tab/Shift+Tab keystroke is required, not merely a form focus change. The mouse wheel changes neither the active input field nor the proposals or visible document area.

Document-assisted entry no longer opens a separate conflict window. The creation window opens maximised, verifies the actual Windows screen geometry after its first show, and can still be minimised and restored through the normal window controls. At 1920×1080 the initial split is approximately 55/45; a stored form pane that is too narrow is raised to a usable minimum width. The more compact document list uses about 20 percent less height. The selected original retains sufficient room on the left while Evidence locations and suggestions, editors and field actions remain visible without horizontal clipping on the right. The splitter position is stored per user within that usability boundary. Document selection, page, zoom, fit, rotation and opening in the default application remain available.

The mouse wheel scrolls the form content while the pointer is inside the contract area. If the pointer is over a date, integer, decimal, amount, percentage, or selection editor, its value is not changed; the wheel gesture is passed to the surrounding contract area. Numeric editors have no increment/decrement buttons and values are entered directly with the keyboard. Clearing a candidate selection or deleting the input with the keyboard leaves the numeric field visibly and internally empty until the user deliberately enters a value.

Clicking Evidence location or a candidate row automatically opens the matching document, page and highlight. Every physical evidence occurrence uses its own scaling-safe row, even when the same value appears on several pages or in several documents. The regionally formatted value appears above document name, page, analysis source, confidence and location quality, with an individual Apply button on the right. Row height follows font and display scaling so multiple candidates cannot overlap. Focus or hover highlights the considered location in blue but does not change the form. Apply and activating the candidate checkbox use the same operation: value and concrete occurrence ID are stored together, the check mark is enabled, and row and document overlay turn green. Clearing the active checkbox removes both selection and field value. An explicit empty state prevents polling or a later analysis from silently restoring the proposal. The selection survives field changes and restores its document, page and focus when the field is revisited. Editing the form directly or choosing Accept manual value stores the manual value and automatically removes the prior evidence selection.

An unambiguous proposal with exactly one occurrence is selected as AUTO within the transient intake. Its checkbox, candidate row and overlay immediately show that state. With multiple physical occurrences or a business conflict, no concrete location is implied and explicit selection remains required. An occurrence explicitly accepted by the user is stored as USER. The whole contract still receives its binding confirmation only in the final confirmation dialog.

Final validation considers both stored evidence selections and the form values that are actually visible and explicitly confirmed at the end. Selecting an existing vehicle or supplier, or staging a new one, also confirms the associated master-data fields such as model or supplier address. Values that were already reviewed therefore do not block finalisation a second time. If a genuine document conflict remains outside these review surfaces, the message uses localised form labels such as Contract date or Model and returns to the affected field; technical schema names are never shown.

Colour represents user state: the focused candidate preview is blue, the accepted location is green and other visible occurrences are muted grey. Independently, line style represents technical quality: exact locations use solid outlines and locally approximated text/value matches use dashed outlines. Equal ambiguous matches retain every locally verifiable coordinate; only genuinely unavailable locations receive no fabricated box. Values available only in XInvoice XML retain their BT reference or XML path. Derived values name their input fields and reuse those fields’ evidence.

Editor borders use four unambiguous states in document-assisted entry: red (#d84315) means a required value is missing, orange (#ef6c00) means a required proposal has unresolved multiple candidates or occurrences, green (#2e7d32) means a required value was selected automatically and unambiguously, explicitly accepted, or entered manually, and blue (#1976d2) means an optional value came from document analysis or manual input. A valid zero such as 0% VAT remains distinct from a genuinely empty editor.

The viewer, candidates and field binding use the domain-neutral DocumentReviewWorkspace. The backwards-compatible extension of document-evidence-anchor-v1 includes document ID and SHA-256, a stable occurrence ID, one-based page, normalised top-left rectangles, source text, optional BT/XML reference, method, quality, confidence and model version. The concrete temporary field selection is stored backend-neutrally with origin AUTO or USER in selection_json. An explicitly cleared field receives a null tombstone in resolution_json. Discard or successful finalisation removes these session states after confirmed training/audit evidence has been retained. The same review area can therefore be reused later for supplier invoices and traffic offences without introducing lease dependencies.

    A["Focus field or candidate"] --> B["Select document and page automatically"]
    B --> C{"Locatable evidence occurrences?"}
    C -->|"One or more"| D["One candidate row per physical location"]
    C -->|"No"| G["Keep source visible; fabricate no box"]
    D --> E["Focus: blue preview"]
    E --> H{"Explicit user action"}

    H -->|"Apply or activate checkbox"| I["Store value and occurrence ID; green + check mark"]

Figure: A two-line candidate with document and page provenance; the preview highlights its position without changing the form value before explicit acceptance.

Vehicle and supplier are selected only in the main form. If no unambiguous match exists, New: Vehicle and New: Supplier are available beside their selectors. These records are initially staged and shown with number and description in the final summary; no second master-data creation is offered there. The shared final confirmation creates them. VIN, registration, supplier identifiers and internal numbers are checked again for duplicates immediately before saving.

Document-assisted entry is a modal, temporary session, not a resumable draft. Cancel, closing the window or cancelling final confirmation all use the same discard path after a warning. No intake, documents, analyses, locations or number reservations remain visible afterwards. The worker also cleans up abandoned, non-finalised sessions.

docs.title: Contract first, recurring invoice later
docs.text:
The lease contract and recurring invoice do not have to be available in the same intake. A contract can first be created manually or through From document. If it is stored as a draft, it must be activated from the contract file with Activate before the later assignment.

If no recurring invoice is available yet and the contract document contains no explicit first due date, FLEET Mira uses the recognised contract start as First due date and derives the due day from it. This also allows a contract that started in the past to be stored without the temporary current-date default creating monthly instalments outside the contract term. A first due date recognised from the document or changed by the user always takes precedence. The Recurring invoice section remains disabled in this case; detected invoice or phase proposals are not stored with the contract.

There are two equivalent routes for a recurring invoice that arrives later. Open the active lease contract and select Recurring invoice from document when vehicle, supplier and contract are already known. PDF, image, XML or hybrid PDF then opens the same split document review as contract creation. Master-data references are fixed while amount periods, additional components, tax and posting mode remain reviewable and editable. Accept as verified creates the supplier invoice and contract assignment atomically.

Alternatively select Supplier invoices → From document and invoice kind Recurring invoice when the contract assignment is still open. A recognised active contract is only proposed and must be confirmed explicitly. Without an assignment the recurring invoice can be stored and later linked through Assign recurring invoice. Import XRechnung uses the same review workspace with structured validation selected initially.

Post automatically requires a locally verified original and conflict-free periods; otherwise use Review manually. Assignment prepares monthly occurrences but posts only periods that are already due and conflict-free.

    A["Create the lease contract manually or from a document"] --> A1{"First due date explicitly available?"}
    A1 -->|"No"| A2["Use contract start as first due date"]
    A1 -->|"Yes"| A3["Keep recognised or manual due date"]
    A2 --> B{"Contract active?"}
    A3 --> B

    B -->|"Yes"| D{"Capture recurring invoice"}
    C --> D

    G --> H["Review original on left and fields/periods on right"]

    I -->|"Yes"| J["Store verified invoice and assignment atomically"]
    I -->|"No"| K["Store recurring invoice and confirm or omit proposed contract"]

    J --> L

If the contract and recurring invoice are already available together, the combined document-assisted intake remains available. The flow above is intended for invoices received only after the contract has been concluded.

docs.title: Multi-phase amount periods
docs.text:
Manual and document-assisted entry use the same recurring-invoice editor. Enable the optional Recurring invoice section in the lease form and enter document number, document date, validity, posting mode and, when available, the original document. Without a verified original only Review manually is available; verifying a document later can enable AUTO for future, unposted periods.

A recurring invoice may contain any number of amount periods. Each period stores its type, valid-from/-to dates, one-time or monthly recurrence, and whether it is the Regular default phase. Amount lines distinguish lease rate, service, insurance, maintenance and other components. The user enters net amount and VAT rate; VAT and gross are calculated to the cent and are read-only. Additional amount lines must be assigned to a contract component.

When document analysis recognises a recurring additional service such as Technical service, FLEET Mira creates a proposal under Additional components and links the corresponding amount lines in every phase to the same transient component. If the initial partial period and regular phase differ, the component table uses the regular monthly amount while the partial-period override remains attached to its invoice phase. All proposals remain editable before final confirmation.

The Period column uses the signed-in user's regional date format. Net, VAT and Gross are right-aligned; the net amount is highlighted in bold white type on a blue background for quick orientation. In document-assisted entry, selecting a phase row shows the locally verifiable period location and its related amount lines in the original document on the left. All visible evidence locations for that recurring-invoice phase are highlighted together with a blue outline and blue background. After a document, page or zoom change, the viewer automatically centres the currently focused evidence location in the visible viewport. If reliable page coordinates are unavailable, FLEET Mira does not fabricate a highlight and the phase remains fully available for manual review.

A short first billing period is normally entered as Initial partial period with ONCE, followed by the monthly rate as the Regular phase with MONTHLY. Copy previous phase duplicates a period so that only dates, recurrence and changed amounts need editing. The regular default phase determines the actual lease rate in the contract header; initial or final partial periods remain period-specific overrides.

Phase Period Amount line Net Initial partial period 20 Aug 2024–31 Aug 2024 Lease rate EUR 107.80 Initial partial period 20 Aug 2024–31 Aug 2024 Technical service EUR 6.44 Regular phase 1 Sep 2024–19 Aug 2026 Monthly lease rate EUR 294.00 Regular phase 1 Sep 2024–19 Aug 2026 Monthly technical service EUR 17.56 
flowchart TD
    A["Create lease contract"] --> B{"Manual or document-assisted?"}
    B -->|"Manual"| C["Enter recurring invoice and amount phases"]
    B -->|"From document"| D["PDF text or OCR with evidence locations"]
    D --> E["Gemini 2.5 Flash structures phases and amount lines"]
    E --> F{"Complete and consistent?"}
    F -->|"No"| G["Optional review pass with Gemini 2.5 Pro"]
    F -->|"Yes"| H["Prefill the shared phase editor"]
    G --> H
    C --> I["Validate dates, VAT, components and totals"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["User confirms every phase"]
    J --> K["Generate a period-correct payment schedule"]
    K --> L["AUTO only for conflict-free occurrences with a verified original"]

For document analysis, local extraction searches for phrases such as first lease instalment, following months, monthly, from, until and until the end of the term, together with lease and service lines. Google Gemini returns phases as a structured list with page and short evidence text. Gemini 2.5 Flash is the default. Missing, overlapping, arithmetically inconsistent or locally unverifiable phases can be checked—under the same document consent—by the review model configured in AI Connector, with Gemini 2.5 Pro proposed by default. Both models only provide proposals to the shared editor.

Before confirmation, FLEET Mira requires gap-free, non-overlapping recurring-invoice coverage, exactly one regular monthly default phase, cent-exact net/VAT/gross values and complete component assignments. A confirmed partial period is not a variance. Genuine differences above one cent are explained using the period, user-facing amount-line name, expected value and entered value, and remain excluded from AUTO until corrected or sent to justified manual review. Changes version only unposted schedule items; posted periods stay unchanged.

When amount phases exist, their earliest start determines the contract's first due date. FLEET Mira creates only monthly instalments that remain fully inside the contract term. A combination of first due date, term and contract end that would create instalments outside that range is rejected on save with a user-facing explanation. This prevents a historical contract start from being replaced accidentally by today's date as the first due date.

When a recurring invoice is detected and confirmed, Activate leasing agreement and Book automatically are preselected. Before finishing, posting mode can be changed to Review manually. The final summary offers Activate leasing agreement again as an editable option and immediately updates the displayed status. Back returns to the entry form without discarding the intake; the final summary still requires explicit confirmation of the reviewed values and automatic posting.

flowchart TD
    A["Confirmed recurring invoice"] --> B["Link contract, supplier invoice and tax data"]
    B --> C{"Activate contract?"}
    C -->|"No"| D["Recurring invoice: PENDING_ACTIVATION"]
    C -->|"Yes"| E{"Posting mode"}
    E -->|"AUTO – default"| F["Prepare monthly occurrences idempotently"]
    E -->|"MANUAL"| G["Present due occurrence for review"]
    F --> H{"Due, complete and conflict-free?"}
    H -->|"Yes"| I["Post monthly occurrence automatically"]
    H -->|"No"| J["REVIEW_REQUIRED"]
    G --> K["User reviews and posts"]
    I --> L["Lease plan/actual reconciliation and accounting export"]
    K --> L

The recurring invoice describes one recurring billing period, not the total across the whole contract term. In AUTO, the worker posts each due or overdue, complete and conflict-free monthly occurrence exactly once. Future monthly costs are deliberately not yet posted under Costs/Credits; they remain visible in the payment schedule and recurring-invoice occurrences until their due date. Assigning a recurring invoice triggers processing immediately. While the contract file is open, posting counters, occurrences and Costs/Credits refresh automatically, so a due entry appears without reopening the record. An inconsistency stops automation for that period and produces REVIEW_REQUIRED; no partial or substitute posting is made. Bank debit and payment confirmation remain outside FLEET Mira.

When a contract is opened through Edit, an already assigned recurring invoice and its confirmed amount phases are shown again. They are read-only in that dialog because posted and versioned invoice phases must not be changed silently together with general contract fields. Posting mode, monthly occurrences and later assignments are managed through the Recurring invoices tab and its dedicated actions.

If activation is cleared, FLEET Mira stores the contract as a draft and the verified recurring invoice as PENDING_ACTIVATION. Its assignment must be confirmed again when the contract is activated later.

docs.title: Leasing factor and actual rate
docs.text:
The pre-calculation follows the common vehicle-leasing comparison and is not a loan annuity:

Monthly rate = list price × leasing factor / 100

Leasing factor = monthly rate / list price × 100

Factor basis is net or gross. With a target factor, FLEET Mira calculates the planned rate. If the factor is empty, it is calculated from the offer rate, or from the actual rate when no offer exists. The actual contract rate remains separately editable and is authoritative for schedule and contract costs.

The actual factor compares the signed rate with list price. The effective factor spreads special payment, final payment and mandatory factor-relevant one-time costs across the term. The all-in rate adds monthly service components and other one-time costs. Difference from pre-calculation is actual net rate minus planned rate; cent-only rounding is hidden.

Figure: Pre-calculation, actual contract rate, factors and full cost for the anonymised sample contract.

docs.title: Documents, invoices, corrections and mileage
docs.text:
Documents links contract PDFs from the vehicle document archive. Supplier invoices, Recurring invoices and Costs/Credits show actual postings linked at position level; planned payments remain separate in the schedule. A collective invoice can allocate individual positions to multiple vehicles and contracts.

Before posting, an incorrect assignment is edited directly. After posting, a versioned reclassification creates a counter-posting on the incorrect vehicle and a new posting on the correct one. After an accounting export, the correction is delivered in a separate RECLASSIFICATION export. If only the contract or payment-schedule link changes while the vehicle is correct, only lease reconciliation is versioned.

Total mileage is proposed as an editable value using annual mileage × term in months / 12, commercially rounded to whole kilometres. An existing contractual value is retained when opened; after annual mileage or term changes, the proposal can still be overwritten.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
The Leasing group in the Report dashboard provides:

  • active lease contracts at an as-of date by vehicle;
  • active contracts ending in the selected date range;
  • active lease contracts at an as-of date by supplier.

All three reports start with vehicle number, registration and VIN and show contract rate, target, actual and effective factors, all-in rate and total contract cost.

docs.title: Review document intake
docs.text:
Review locally extracted suggestions from synthetic contract documents before applying them. Different values remain visible as conflicts; missing required fields must be supplied explicitly. Source evidence stays accessible in the document area.

Language of some beta dialogs

Some older labels remain German in the English profile. The current Material 3 captures show the actual beta interface without retouching.

docs.title: Driving-licence checks and RFID/NFC
docs.text: The driving-licence check links the recurring policy in a personnel record to an RFID/NFC identifier on the licence. A successful check automatically updates the next due date; the system-managed deadline cannot be completed manually.

docs.title: Requirements and master data
docs.text:
Open Fleet management > Personnel, select the person and choose Edit. Enter at least the personnel number and name and, where available, the licence number and issuing authority. Enable Recurring driving-licence check required and set an interval between 1 and 3,650 days; the usual initial value is 28 days.

The personnel record's Master data tab displays date of birth, licence data, the check policy and interval. Deadlines contains the automatically calculated due date.

docs.title: Assign RFID/NFC
docs.text:
1. Open the personnel record or Personnel > Licence-check evaluation and select the person.
  2. Choose Assign RFID/NFC.
  3. Place the chip on a PC/SC-compatible reader and verify UID, reader and person in the confirmation dialog.
  4. Save the assignment. A UID can be active for only one person; assigning a new UID ends the previous assignment with an audit trail.

The PC/SC UID is displayed and stored in the conventional byte order. For example, the byte-reversed sequence A3 BC 06 02 00 03 04 E0 returned by the reader appears as E0 04 03 00 02 06 BC A3.

Figure: Active and ended UID assignments with their validity period.

docs.title: Perform a PC/SC check
docs.text:
Open the personnel record or evaluation and choose Check via PC/SC. FLEET Mira accepts the check only when the UID read from the chip was actively assigned to the selected person at that time. Confirm the result. The record stores UTC time, method, workstation, result and operator.

A successful check completes the previous system deadline and calculates the next date from check time plus interval. No successful record is created for a missing reader, timeout, unknown UID or another person's UID.

docs.title: Evaluation and exceptions
docs.text:
Under Personnel > Licence-check evaluation, filter by person, state, check requirement, RFID assignment, email address and due-date range. The table shows the latest check, next deadline, remaining days and status. Its context menu opens the personnel record, assigns a UID or starts a check.

RFID CSV rows from a terminal are assigned automatically only when UID and timestamp match one active assignment. Unknown or temporally inconsistent UIDs appear in the RFID exceptions list. An authorised user may associate the row with a person or discard it with a mandatory reason; the source row remains traceable.

docs.title: Notifications, output and audit
docs.text:
Authorised users can preview or send a reminder from the evaluation. Print preview and PDF use the visible filters and columns. Changes to the policy, UID assignment, check, follow-up deadline and exception are recorded in object and global audit logs.

Viewing requires fleet.read; UID assignment, PC/SC checks and exceptions require fsk.check; manual notification requires fsk.notify.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: State Action No PC/SC reader Check the Windows driver and reader, reconnect it and reopen the operation. UID belongs to another person Do not record a check; verify the assignment and selected record. RFID missing Assign an active UID first. Deadline cannot be completed manually Record a successful check or disable the policy in master data. CSV row remains unresolved Check the timestamp and UID validity, then resolve the exception.

docs.title: Material 3 client interface
docs.text: Basic, Pro and Enterprise use the same native FleetMira interface with blue accents, dark navigation and shared Material symbols. Symbols ship with the application and require no internet connection. Permissions and licensing continue to determine which features are available.

docs.title: Compact sign-in
docs.text: The sign-in window has no native title bar. Drag its product-name header to move it; the close control, Cancel and Esc cancel sign-in. Enter submits the credentials. Enabled SSO providers and optional backup restoration remain available. Errors appear inside the window.

docs.title: Enterprise tenants
docs.text: Enterprise signs users in centrally and opens an authorized customer through tenant selection. Customer tenants are distinct from device/location groups and Microsoft Entra tenants. Set up and switch tenants.

docs.title: Shared Material window bars
docs.text:
Client-owned main windows and dialogs use a Material window bar instead of the native Windows title bar. Drag the title area to move a window. Main windows and dialogs designed for it offer Minimize, Maximize or Restore window, and Close. Small dialogs and login only show their applicable actions. Double-click the title area to maximize an eligible window. Alt+Space or a title-area right-click opens its window menu.

Close preserves existing unsaved-change, cancellation and mandatory-input rules. Embedded work tabs do not gain extra title bars. File pickers use Qt presentation; external browsers and identity-provider windows remain separate.

docs.title: Light and dark appearance
docs.text: Open User → My profile and select Light or Dark under Appearance. Save applies the appearance immediately to all open views and saves it for your user account. Cancel discards the selection. The interface uses the dark appearance before sign-in and after sign-out, and whenever no preference has been saved. An explicitly saved Light preference remains available. Another user's selection does not affect your preference. Language and region are managed independently.

docs.title: Navigation and workspaces
docs.text:
The dashboard is a direct primary page occupying the entire content area, without left navigation or an additional work tab. This is the explicitly requested exception to the other areas' navigation pattern.

Other primary areas have grouped navigation on the left and work tabs on the right. Work tabs start empty after a new sign-in. Select a navigation entry to open its overview. Opening an existing workspace activates its current tab. Tabs can be moved and closed; closed overviews remain available through navigation.

Menus, submenus, context menus and important actions display a symbol next to their text. The text remains the authoritative label. Navigation entries that your permissions do not allow are disabled; entries hidden by licensing remain hidden. Additional actions are available in the overflow menu in narrow windows.

In Device management, Open or a double-click on the normal device row opens its record in a separate work tab. Reopening the same record activates its existing tab. Individual URL, system-information and file actions remain available through their respective controls.

docs.title: Analyze a single tachograph file
docs.text:
Analyze single file opens a new work tab for either M or C files in the Tachodata archive area, without a separate analysis window. Captions use the filename with the technical M: or C: prefix. Reopening the same file activates its existing tab and preserves the selected subview. Tabs can be moved and closed; reopening after closing reloads the file. The archive overview remains available.

Single-file analyses started from Fleet Management continue to use its work tabs. The archive.read permission remains required. Sign-out or loss of archive access closes the archive analysis tabs.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The dashboard uses the full content width without left navigation:

The following native views contain synthetic example data only. They show the appearance, not an installation or a production connection.

docs.title: Tachodata evaluation
docs.text: Search and filters are separated from the action area. Expandable vehicle, archive-file and archive-gap hierarchies are retained.

docs.title: Deadline evaluation
docs.text: Filters, record actions and the data table follow a shared structure. A selected row remains blue with white text even when status colours are present.

docs.title: Personnel record and day view
docs.text: The personnel record combines record-specific actions with its related views. The daily timeline and activity table retain their business colours; scrollbars and tab navigation remain available in small windows.

docs.title: Additional dark views
docs.text:
Before authentication, the interface uses English. After sign-in, profile language and region apply; these workspaces show dark appearance.

Existing beta localization gaps

Some older field labels and report descriptions remain German even when the profile language is English. Screenshots deliberately show the actual beta interface. This documentation refresh does not change application localization or functionality.

docs.title: Position maps
docs.text: Position maps display archived coordinates interactively. Viewing a map changes no business data and creates no audit event.

docs.title: Driver card
docs.text: Figure: C positions on OpenStreetMap with source and type filters.

docs.title: Vehicle unit
docs.text: Figure: M positions, border and loading records on OpenStreetMap.

docs.title: Operation and interpretation
docs.text:
• + / − zoom; drag to pan; All points restores the complete extent.
  • Source filters toggle PLACE, GNSS-3H and other records.
  • Type filters distinguish begin, RFU, three-hour GNSS, border and loading records where present.
  • Marker colours follow the legend. Click or hover to see time, source, type, driver/card or vehicle reference and available location text.
  • Filters affect display only; the archive object and position list remain unchanged.

The map uses OpenStreetMap tiles and displays the required attribution. Building the view requires connectivity to the configured tile endpoint; tiles may subsequently come from the local cache. A missing location name is not a missing point: coordinates can exist even when nation or region cannot be resolved unambiguously.

docs.title: Report dashboard
docs.text: The Report dashboard 💎 provides twelve reproducible working-time, mileage, return and deadline reports. Every run stores its filters, time basis, calculation version and result without changing tachograph, telematics or master data. The following screens and Stimulsoft outputs were generated from an anonymised copy of the demo database; activity times and evaluation results were retained.

docs.title: Catalogue and configuration
docs.text:
Figure: Report catalogue with groups, search, favourites, run history and output actions.

Use Configuration to maintain establishment/holiday country, optional subdivision, night-time window and return intervals. A stored report version retains the configuration in effect when it was created; later changes do not rewrite previous results.

Figure: Shared configuration for working-time and return reports.

docs.title: Driver working times by week
docs.text:
Purpose: Condenses daily working time, night work and total working time by ISO week. It supports checks of daily and weekly values and highlights unusual night-work shares.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Working times by driver
docs.text:
Purpose: Combines shifts, activities, countries, distance, day type and data quality for each driver. Use it for operational working-time review and investigation of individual days.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Monthly working times for all drivers
docs.text:
Purpose: Places all drivers in one matrix with daily and monthly totals. It makes workload, missing values and monthly differences easy to compare.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Working-time summary by country
docs.text:
Purpose: Assigns working time to countries or individual days. Rest and availability can be included for cross-border deployment and remuneration checks.

Open the PDF example

docs.title: Mileage reports
docs.text:
The Mileage group contains reports by vehicle, by vehicle and month, by vehicle, month and day, and the Odometer readings per vehicle and day audit report. Filters select vehicles and a date range or from/to month. With no vehicle selected, all active vehicles are included.

Every new mileage and cost run uses the shared OdometerBoundaryResolver exclusively, with the priority M-file midnight → telematics sensor → C-file vehicle use → C-file place → C-file three-hour GNSS → telematics GPS. Only VALID and WARNING readings are eligible. Manual, unverified, unknown and conflicting values are excluded. Opening and closing readings are rounded to whole kilometres first; the displayed difference is then always exactly closing minus opening.

Qualified GPS-server values are stored as daily odometer readings independently of the 28-day position-detail retention. If a closed period is missing a boundary, administrators can use Administration → Cost analysis → Calculation parameters → Odometer determination to mark it incomplete, interpolate linearly or extrapolate. The default extrapolation is limited to seven days and uses the median of plausible daily distances from 14 days. Estimated opening, closing and difference values carry a warning marker. During the current local day, an available qualified actual reading wins. If none exists and extrapolation is configured, the central resolver estimates up to the current calculation instant. Monthly, overall and cost reports use the same closing boundary. If the opening boundary has no sufficiently recent reading, the central resolver applies the same minimum sample count, estimation basis and maximum gap: it derives the median from the first qualified following days and projects backwards from the first actual reading to the opening boundary.

Monthly and daily reports compare mileage with the immediately preceding calendar month or day for the same vehicle. Red and orange arrows indicate increases, blue marks the neutral range from −5 to +5 per cent, and light-green or green arrows indicate decreases.

docs.title: Odometer readings per vehicle and day
docs.text:
This report is the detailed audit trail for the other mileage reports and for cost per kilometre. The on-screen view uses a parent/child presentation: each vehicle is a coloured, expandable and collapsible group header. Internal number, registration, VIN, opening reading, closing reading and difference occupy separate sortable columns. The subordinate daily rows use separate columns for date, odometer reading and source or derivation (M file, C file, telematics sensor, telematics GPS, interpolated, extrapolated or incomplete).

For estimates, the tooltip provides the method, measurement time, supporting readings, estimate distance and algorithm version. The UI, Stimulsoft/PDF and Excel share the same vehicle groups; Excel merges the group header row. Runs above 20,000 daily detail rows are rejected and require a shorter period or fewer vehicles. Existing stored report runs are not modified by the new odometer-boundary-v2 algorithm version.

docs.title: Leasing reports
docs.text: Active lease contracts by vehicle and Active lease contracts by supplier use an as-of date. Lease contracts ending soon uses a freely selected contract-end range. An optional supplier filter narrows all three reports. The result includes vehicle identity, contract, supplier, term and remaining days, contract mileage, actual rate, target, actual and effective factors, all-in rate and total contract cost.

docs.title: Create and output a report
docs.text:
Print layouts are tailored to the report's purpose: driver working-time and planning detail tables omit the Data quality column, while the driver working-time report prints each date completely on one line. The vehicle/day mileage report structures details hierarchically by Vehicle and Month; the daily odometer audit report visually separates Odometer from Source / derivation while retaining a continuous row background. Leasing lists use two-line records for contract/supplier and registration/VIN information, and the supplier report additionally groups by supplier. The violation dashboard prints Duration / deviation as a compact two-line heading.

  1. Open Fleet → Report dashboard 💎.
  2. Select Favourites, Working time, Mileage, Leasing, Planning or Deadlines, then choose a report.
  3. Set the report-specific filters that appear. No object selection means all permitted drivers or vehicles.
  4. Choose Create report.
  5. Open the run in Stimulsoft preview or export PDF or Excel.

The result view explains the calculation and time basis. Every master-data-related grid starts consistently with Vehicle no., Registration and VIN, or Personnel no. and Personnel name (last name, first name). Mixed deadline grids expose all five columns and leave non-applicable values empty. Global search covers every visible column, while headers sort by canonical raw values. Historic runs are normalized for presentation only; a personnel number that was not stored at the time remains empty. The stored source data is unchanged.

The 20 bundled Stimulsoft system reports use the same identity columns. Custom templates are not overwritten and receive the new canonical fields in addition to the existing compatibility fields.

Deadline reports can be filtered by period, object, due type, status and lifecycle. The fleet report additionally filters by basis, trigger, mileage data quality and evaluability. The deadline-specific selectors use a space-saving two-column layout; the compact object list still supports selecting multiple drivers or vehicles. If the period is not enabled, mileage-only deadlines without a date remain included.

Working time includes driving and other work. Availability and rest are included only in reports that expose the respective filter. Night work is calculated against the configured window and the time zone stored with the run. Daylight-saving transitions do not alter elapsed activity durations.

Dashboard access, configuration changes, start, completion, cancellation, failure, opening a stored run and export are audited. Entry requires reporting.dashboard.read; output and configuration may be restricted separately.

docs.title: Personnel and fleet tachodata evaluations
docs.text: The two overview workspaces group archived tachograph files by person or vehicle. They are the entry point to single-file analysis and show known coverage gaps and the next download due date. All times are UTC.

docs.title: Personnel
docs.text:
Figure: Personnel overview with download due date and data coverage.

Each parent row shows driver, personnel number, file count, data and activity ranges, next download and gap status. Data from/to is the complete range declared by the file, while Activities from/to is the range actually covered by parsed activity records. Search covers person, card, filename and archive ID. Date, gap and file-status filters can be combined.

Figure: Expanded driver-card files and archive coverage gaps.

Tachograph files lists linked C files with card number, archive date, period, filename, size, task, status, archive ID and path. Archive coverage gaps lists uncovered intervals between known data ranges. No gap is invented before the first or after the last range unless a business target period exists.

The fleet view works the same way, but assigns M files through the confirmed vehicle link or VIN. Its separate activity range is derived from the actual M-file activity changes. Generation, parser and signature state remain visible per file.

Figure: Expanded M file and calculated vehicle data coverage.

docs.title: Due date and operation
docs.text:
• Green: outside the individual lead time.
  • Orange: within the default ten-day lead time.
  • Red: download due date has passed.
  • A dash means that no effective, unambiguous download due date can be determined yet.

Double-click a file to open the central driver-card or vehicle-unit analysis in one reusable work tab. The context menu offers analysis, archive record, single/selection export and ID/path copy. Export requires archive.export; viewing requires archive.read. Column layout, sorting, filters and expansion state are stored per user.

docs.title: Traffic-offence management
docs.text: This module supports fleet managers with the administrative processing of German traffic offences. It does not replace legal or privacy advice and makes no automatic decision about guilt, liability or the driver.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The following diagram shows the regular workflow and its possible return paths. Driver, guilt, liability and legal decisions are never made automatically; proposals and responses must be reviewed and confirmed by an authorised user.

flowchart TD
    A["1. Intake<br/>Upload, watched import folder or IMAP"] --> B["2. Capture<br/>Archive the original, review OCR and AI proposals<br/>Create a case or assign the document"]
    B --> C["3. Driver assignment<br/>Evaluate tachograph data, telematics, dispatch and default driver"]
    C --> D{"Suitable driver identified?"}
    D -->|"No"| E["Assign driver manually<br/>Record a reason"]
    D -->|"Yes"| F{"Accept the proposal?"}
    F -->|"No"| G["Select a different driver<br/>Explain the deviation"]
    F -->|"Yes"| H["Confirm driver"]
    E --> H
    G --> H
    H --> I["4. Driver enquiry<br/>Send portal link and fillable PDF by email<br/>Review the driver's response"]
    I --> J{"Next processing step?"}
    J -->|"Continue driver identification"| C
    J -->|"Prepare authority response"| K["5. Response to the authority<br/>Create the response from reviewed information"]
    K --> L["Send the response manually"]
    L --> M["Record dispatch"]
    M --> N["6. Closure<br/>Check open items and close the case with an audit trail"]

While the Traffic offences workspace is open, it refreshes the review inbox and case overview from the database every 15 seconds. Selection and scroll position are preserved, and newly added review items are announced in the action row. Refreshing stops completely when the tab is switched away from or closed. The UI never triggers its own IMAP poll; it only displays results already imported by the worker.

Authority documents are accepted by upload, a watched import folder or a dedicated IMAP mailbox. Original files and messages are retained unchanged with a SHA-256 checksum. Text PDFs are read locally; images and scans can be processed with a locally installed Tesseract service. When a document creates a new case, its document type and date, authority, reference, registration, offence time and location, vehicle and response deadline must all be confirmed regardless of document type. When a document is assigned to an existing case, the review shows only the assignment, the required document date and the optional response deadline; the other case fields are hidden and are not requested again.

Once confirmed, the review-inbox item is immutable. View or a double-click opens the already linked case and cannot create a second case or assign the original to another case.

New and unprocessed review-inbox entries are highlighted with red text. Confirmed, rejected or already case-linked entries use the normal text colour. When a row is selected, the shared blue-and-white selection appearance always takes precedence.

docs.title: Case workspace and workflow
docs.text:
Each case opens in its own workspace tab. A localised progress indicator covers Case reviewed, Identify driver, Request driver response, Prepare authority response, Record dispatch and Close case. It consists of six cells inside one surrounding frame: completed steps are green, the active step is red and pending steps are yellow. All six cells are green after the case has been closed. The current task and all available actions are derived centrally from the domain workflow state. Actions that are not yet allowed remain disabled. The workspace reads worker and IMAP results from the database every 15 seconds while preserving selection and scroll position.
