Below Case: [case number] - [authority reference], the following actions are available according to status and permissions: Edit, Refresh driver evidence, Confirm driver, Send driver request, Create fillable driver PDF, Prepare authority response, Record dispatch, Add document, Close case and Cancel case. Case data shows the confirmed master data. Edit opens a modal dialog; authorised users can save changes only after entering a reason. Previous and new values are audited. Changing the vehicle or offence time recalculates driver evidence, while a changed response deadline updates the document-specific due item.

Driver identification shows candidates and evidence with source, priority, validity interval, confidence and conflict state. An active person must be explicitly confirmed. If the evidence chain from tachograph data, telematics, dispatch and the default driver yields no candidate, any active person can be assigned manually with a reason. An automatically identified driver can also be overridden by the person who actually drove; this likewise requires a reason. Manual and overriding decisions remain visible as separate evidence and are audited.

Driver communication contains versioned requests and their related responses. The confirmed driver, email address, SMTP configuration and HTTPS portal are checked before sending. Portal link, return reference and fillable PDF are prepared transactionally and sent asynchronously. The case changes to “Driver response pending” only after SMTP succeeds. Failures remain visible and are included in the daily fleet-manager report. An intentional resend creates a new version and return reference.

Portal, PDF and email responses remain bound to the person and communication that were actually addressed. Raw data and extracted proposals are never overwritten. Review stores a separate confirmed snapshot. Without a preselected default, the reviewer must choose Continue driver identification or Prepare authority response; even an affirmative response never causes an automatic transition.

Authority response creates a PDF only from facts that the reviewer explicitly selects from previously confirmed data. Creating the PDF is not dispatch. Record dispatch captures the answered authority document, channel, time, optional evidence and note. Only the due item for the selected document is completed; any other open document deadline remains open.

The Documents tab contains the unchanged source document and all later additions, such as an objection, legal-protection confirmation or completed witness questionnaire. Internal document types distinguish driver declaration form, authority response and dispatch evidence. Later files are archived with a checksum in the same case file and never replace or modify the source document.

The Emails tab combines inbound messages correlated through IMAP and recorded outbound email in one chronological timeline. Sender, recipient, subject, status and readable message text therefore remain directly traceable from the case.

Audit shows revision-safe changes and workflow decisions. A regular close is allowed only after an authority dispatch has been recorded and no unreviewed driver response or open document deadline remains. Closing with open items requires the dedicated traffic_offences.close_override permission and a reason; open due items are archived rather than incorrectly completed. Cancellation also requires a reason. Closed and cancelled cases are read-only and cannot be reopened in version 1.

Driver identification evaluates only time-overlapping evidence in this order: M data, telematics driver history, dispatch and the historical default driver. A card in the co-driver slot or an unconfirmed card-to-person link is not driver evidence. Every assignment requires confirmation; overriding the highest-ranked proposal requires a reason.

When creating a case, the offence time is entered through a date-time picker. It defaults to the current time, displays date and time according to the signed-in user's region, and stores the instant normalized to UTC together with its local time context.

When assigning a historical default driver, the validity start is selected from a calendar. The date picker defaults to the current date and displays it in the signed-in user's regional format.

Drivers may respond through an internal HTTPS form, a personalised fillable PDF or free-form email. Vehicle use, allegation statement, address, comment and attachments are stored separately and always require review. An address supplied for a case never changes personnel master data automatically.

docs.title: Deadlines and notifications
docs.text:
The dedicated Traffic-offence deadlines view is nested directly below Traffic offences in fleet navigation; the opened workspace tab uses the same title. It refreshes whenever it is opened and after an authority document is confirmed. It displays only time-based domain data such as authority, reference, case, vehicle, confirmed driver, workflow and document status, due date and remaining days. Odometer, odometer source, target or remaining kilometres and distance-based filters are not used in this view. The first visible deadline is selected as the current row on the initial load. Light status highlights use contrasting dark text, while the current row uses the same white-on-blue appearance as the personnel deadline evaluation. Selection and scroll position are retained across asynchronous reloads without taking input focus away from navigation or filters. Double-clicking opens the related case.

Every confirmed document with a deadline receives a separate managed due item. Changing the date updates that item; only the recorded reply for that document completes it. Cancelled documents and documents confirmed as having no deadline archive the item with a reason.

The daily fleet-manager report contains pending driver declarations, replies due today or soon, overdue cases and technical errors. Addresses, free text, offence details, document contents and attachments are never included in the report email. The optional 2x2 widget is added only from the widget catalogue and does not modify existing layouts.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: The driver portal must be published with HTTPS inside the intended LAN/VPN. Access tokens are stored only as hashes, exchanged once for a short-lived session and protected by CSRF validation. Pro uses SQLite and the in-process worker; Enterprise uses PostgreSQL and FleetMiraWorker exclusively.

docs.title: Demo data
docs.text: The distributed demo database contains no traffic-offence cases. If required, the optional idempotent seed python scripts/seed_traffic_offence_demo.py creates 20 penalty notices clearly marked as fictitious and not payable. Each generated case is assigned to an existing vehicle, includes a synthetic enforcement-camera image and is registered with a document reference and test deadline in both traffic-offence management and the document archive.

docs.title: Material 3 navigation and workspaces
docs.text:
The current interface uses shared navigation, movable work tabs and Material window bars. Newly signed-in users start the relevant areas with an empty workspace. A navigation entry opens or focuses its tab; the same static workspace is not opened twice.

Closed static tabs can be reopened. Permissions and licensing determine available actions. After authentication, language and region follow the user profile.

Enterprise provides central sign-in, tenant selection and startup feedback. Normal closing exits the entire client; independent server services continue running.

  • Material 3 interface
  • Enterprise section
  • Set up tenants

docs.title: Vehicle costs and credits
docs.text: Direct costs and credits are entered in the vehicle record. Foreign- and e-invoice lines use the same cost ledger but are edited through the invoice workflow. Only booked entries contribute to cost analysis, the TCO data basis and reports.

docs.title: Prepare categories and suppliers
docs.text: Under Finance > Cost categories, maintain a unique code, label and business classification. Leasing, insurance and tax are usually fixed costs; fuel, repairs and tolls are usually variable. Supplier master data is needed when a foreign document is associated with the entry.

docs.title: Enter a cost or credit
docs.text:
1. Open Fleet > Vehicles, the vehicle record and Costs/Credits.
  2. Choose New.
  3. Verify the vehicle and category and select Cost or Credit.
  4. Enter description, valid from/to, document date, net amount, VAT rate and optional notes.
  5. Select Variable to allocate the full amount to the document date. Clear it to distribute a fixed amount by day across its validity period.
  6. Save the draft.

Net and VAT are stored to the cent; gross is calculated. Zero-percent VAT is supported. Fixed costs require a complete, ordered validity period. Foreign-invoice lines inherit document and validity dates from the header and remain variable.

docs.title: Edit, verify and book
docs.text:
A direct Draft can be edited and given an original document. Verify checks mandatory fields, periods, amounts and document policy. Book then moves it into the immutable actual-cost ledger. Buttons are enabled according to state and permission.

Booked entries are never overwritten or deleted. Cancel creates a linked counter-entry and requires a reason. A commercial credit is entered as its own type and reduces cost. Original entry, correction and operator therefore remain traceable in the audit log.

docs.title: Effect in cost analysis
docs.text:
• Variable costs and credits are allocated completely to the document date.
  • Fixed costs are distributed by day across the validity period.
  • Invoice and credit signs affect totals, comparisons and cost/km.
  • A cancelled booking and its booked counter-entry net to zero while retaining the booking basis.
  • Draft and merely verified entries are excluded.

docs.title: Original documents and permissions
docs.text:
Add document writes the original to the local financial archive, reads it back and verifies its SHA-256. External backup is secondary and never blocks the business workflow. Paper scans additionally require an organisational replacement-scanning procedure.

Reading requires finance.read, editing finance.manage, verification finance.verify, and booking or cancellation finance.book.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text: Problem Correction Fixed cost is flagged Enter a complete, non-reversed validity period. Edit is disabled Only direct drafts are editable; open an invoice line through its invoice. Entry is absent from analysis Check Booked state, reporting period and filters. Wrong period Correct document date for variable cost or validity period for fixed cost.

docs.title: Vehicle-unit analysis
docs.text:
Vehicle-unit analysis uses one selected M file as its base. Drivers, slots and card sessions remain separate; C files supplement comparison only within proven card insertion periods.

This makes the single-file view archive-scoped. Vehicle record > Day/Week/Violations, by contrast, uses all valid M archives assigned to the VIN. Check the heading's record/archive context before comparing periods or totals.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Figure: Generation, signature, vehicle identity, data range and parser warnings.

Warnings identify optional or incomplete download sections. Missing second-by-second speed data, for example, does not change the preserved M file.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Figure: Insertion/withdrawal, slot, card, generation and name.

“No assigned driver card” means no usable active card-insertion interval was found for the slot and period. It does not merely mean that a C file is absent; timeline tooltips explain this distinction.

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
Figure: Vehicle activity intervals with data availability.

Driver changes and team driving are separated by card, generation and slot. Parallel activities from two drivers are never collapsed into one driver row.

docs.title: Day chart
docs.text:
Figure: Driver groups, insertion period and activity tracks for one UTC day.

Navigation depends only on the date. Driver and card appear in group headings. Tooltips on unknown-card groups explain their evidence basis.

Date, arrows and Go to control the UTC day. Each driver group shows card insertion and an activity track; colour and label distinguish driving, work, availability and rest/break. Hover details identify start, end, duration, slot, card and C/M availability. Unknown-card intervals remain a separate visible group.

docs.title: Week chart
docs.text:
Figure: One ISO week with separate driver panels.

Each calendar week appears once. Multiple sessions for the same driver are combined in that weekly panel; driver changes and team drivers stay separate.

Use arrows to move between ISO weeks and review each day's coverage first. Weekly totals apply to the visible range and record/archive context. Missing data is neither rest nor zero activity.

docs.title: Events and faults
docs.text: Figure: Records with code, description, start, end and section.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Figure: Second-by-second speed or a documented empty state.

Only speed records present in the file are shown. An empty state is never replaced by calculated or synthetic data.

docs.title: Technical data
docs.text:
Figure: Readable field tree for manufacturer, device, software and approval.

The tree retains its download-section reference. Unknown optional records remain available through a bounded raw reference.

docs.title: Calibrations
docs.text:
Figure: Calibration time, next calibration, purpose, workshop, VIN and registration.

When a vehicle is created, FLEET Mira uses the chronologically latest suitable record for the separate calibration deadline.

docs.title: Positions, borders and loading
docs.text:
Figure: Time and location records from the selected M file.

The list combines GNSS positions, border crossings and loading/unloading without losing the record type. Coordinate-bearing rows can be opened together on the map.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text: Figure: Verification results for signed download sections.

docs.title: Violations
docs.text:
Figure: Per-driver pre-check and data-coverage notes.

Selected M file checks trips on this vehicle only. Full driver history may supplement other trusted C/M archives. Unknown-card intervals are reported as notes, not personal violations.

Select period and rule modules and recalculate after changes. Every finding identifies ruleset/version, legal basis, assessment period, actual/target value, deviation, calculation basis and severity. Optional BALM guidance is not a fine decision. Review coverage, unknown-card intervals and notices about national exemptions, AETR or Article 12 before assessing a result.

docs.title: Violation dashboard and driver instructions
docs.text: The Violation dashboard 💎 consolidates technical compliance findings into a period-based work list. It does not replace an authority or legal assessment. The screen and report previews come from an anonymised copy of the demo database; driver identities were replaced while activity and finding data were retained.

docs.title: Dashboard screen
docs.text:
Figure: Period and severity filters, weekly trend, driver risk and findings for the selected person.

The screen has four working areas:

  • Filters and actions select the period, visible severities and metric and start the evaluation, dashboard report or driver instruction.
  • Summary shows the development of findings by calendar week.
  • Driver risk assessment shows score, trend, count by severity, possible indicative amount and data quality.
  • Violation details explain timestamp, severity, deviation, legal basis and possible amount for the selected person.

docs.title: Create an evaluation
docs.text:
1. Open Fleet → Violation dashboard 💎.
  2. Select 90 days, 56 days, the current calendar year or a custom period.
  3. Enable the required severities and select Refresh evaluation.
  4. Select a driver to inspect that person's findings in the lower area.

The run stores its period, rulebooks, algorithm version, time basis, filters, sources and checksums. Failed or cancelled runs are audited as well.

Tachograph values are evaluated in UTC by default. When local activity time is enabled under System → Settings, the dashboard uses the selected IANA time zone for day and week boundaries. Daylight-saving transitions change neither source values nor elapsed durations.

docs.title: Stimulsoft dashboard report
docs.text:
Purpose: Provides the period, rulebooks, risk assessment for all affected drivers, violation details and data quality as a printable record. Possible fines are explicitly presented as non-binding indicative values.

Open the violation-dashboard PDF example

Show dashboard report opens this output with the current filters, risk values and trends. It requires compliance export permission and both the Violation dashboard and Stimulsoft Pro features.

docs.title: Stimulsoft driver instruction
docs.text:
Purpose: Brings together the findings to discuss, legal bases, deviations and open personnel deadlines for exactly one driver. Signature fields support a documented instruction record.

Open the driver-instruction PDF example

  1. Select exactly one person with findings.
  2. Choose Create driver instruction.
  3. Review the generated PDF and confirm the print status after printing.

The PDF, checksum, person, findings and creation timestamp are stored as tamper-evident evidence. Findings that have already been delivered are not sent again as new findings in a later instruction. A matching notification rule can deliver each instruction exactly once with its PDF attachment.

Read access, report export and driver-instruction management use separate permissions. Opening, evaluating, exporting, creating and confirming print status produce audit events. Structured details are available as a tree, JSON export and printable output under Administration → Audit.

docs.title: Workshop management
docs.text: The area is available in Pro and Enterprise. The workspace starts empty after login. Open an overview in the left navigation; Open or a double-click opens a record in its own detail tab. Opening it again focuses the existing tab. Search and filters belong to the overview. Record actions, positions, documents and history belong to the detail workspace.

docs.title: Master data and preparation
docs.text:
Reuse existing vehicles, personnel and suppliers. Create commercial customers, units, explicitly classified tax codes, articles, warehouses, storage locations and price groups. Device tenants are not invoice customers. Assign a customer to a vehicle where appropriate. Own vehicles can have a cost category for internal workshop costs.

Maintain supplier purchase prices and price-group sales prices with validity periods. Personnel have separate cost and sales rates. Units distinguish count, time and other quantities. Time factors explicitly refer to hours; labour units require their own approved factor. Quantities and personnel prices are converted only between compatible units. Apply price list uses the rule valid on the service or purchase-order date and displays the calculated result. Disable it for an explicit manual price; text changes retain existing price provenance. A missing sales price requires a decision. Free service requires a reason and explicit confirmation before finalization. Referenced master records are archived.

docs.title: Orders and quotations
docs.text:
A vehicle order proposes the vehicle's current customer. A customer order requires a commercial customer; a vehicle is optional. An alternative invoice customer is selected explicitly and audited. Changing a vehicle's customer does not silently change existing orders. Rebilling displays any difference and requires explicit confirmation of the current mapping.

Master articles, free articles, personnel effort and labour texts are separate position types. Earmarked articles and applied templates are planned demand. They do not change stock. Conversion to actual material checks availability; partial quantities require an explicit choice. Actual material consumption posts a stock issue. Quantity changes post only their difference; price and text changes do not post quantities. An actual return is a separate operation.

Keep planned and performed effort separate. An order can be started, completed and reopened before binding invoicing. Completion posts internal costs for an own vehicle from actual inventory values and cost rates. Repeated completion posts only a changed cost amount.

Quotations support the same four position types and templates. A draft is editable. Issue freezes the version including customer, prices, taxes and document language. New version creates a separate draft referring to the original. Open document displays the PDF. Conversion copies the header and all positions as planned, without stock issues or performed hours. Repetition does not create another order. Conversion opens customer-order details when no vehicle is assigned and vehicle-order details when a vehicle is assigned. Opening or double-clicking a customer order retains its customer overview; the detail tab and navigation agree, and reopening creates no duplicate. Already open order overviews refresh automatically after conversion.

docs.title: Inventory and purchasing
docs.text:
Stock is derived from an immutable movement journal. Negative available stock is prevented. Purchases, issues, returns, count differences, transfers and approved openings retain their source, business date and actual posting timestamp. Purchase drafts are editable; released orders support partial receipts. A reasoned receipt return references the original receipt and issues its current inventory value. Overdelivery and closing an outstanding quantity require an explicit reason.

Create an inventory count document with a UTC cutoff and warehouse. It freezes the cutoff stock for each position. Enter every counted quantity and explicitly approve the document. The counted difference is applied exactly once to current stock; intervening movements remain intact. Approved documents are immutable. The cutoff report uses actual UTC posting timestamps and recorded book values; the business document date does not shift that history.

The default valuation is the moving average per article and warehouse. Global article valuation and fixed prices are configured through a documented valuation change. Historical postings are not revalued. Purchase proposals consider minimum stock, planned demand, stock and confirmed outstanding supply; minimum purchase quantities and package sizes apply. Indicators disclose their period and missing history.

docs.title: Outgoing invoices and corrections
docs.text:
Invoicing supports manual invoices and completed orders for one invoice customer. Previously consumed order material is not issued again. Direct sales are issued exactly once on finalization. Administration provides separate annual number ranges for invoices and corrections; reserved numbers are never reused. Drafts have no final invoice number.

Finalization freezes reviewed data, reserves a number, generates and validates XML or hybrid PDF and seals the originals in the archive. Errors prevent issuance. Interrupted finalization resumes with the same finalization ID. A reasoned abort retains the number evidence; already sealed originals are completed.

Issued invoices cannot be edited or deleted. Full cancellation and supported partial corrections create new documents referring to the original. Invoice correction is not a material return. Old-part and disbursement rules require versioned examples approved by a tax specialist. Unapproved special treatments are blocked.

DATEV, CSV/ZIP and REST use the same frozen handover data. Retries preserve export ID and package. An uncertain transmission status requires clarification; without confirmed receiver idempotency the system does not resend blindly. The complete auditor export additionally includes originals, field descriptions, relationships, rule versions and audit evidence. Create auditor export in the transfer overview works without a selected or existing outgoing invoice. DATEV includes debtor master data alongside the booking batch; Finalization belongs to the approved export configuration.

Archive status and external backup status are separate. Successful offline finalization does not confirm external backup. Follow the operating procedures and architecture and release gates.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Open Retention under Invoicing. The overview filters document classes and due reviews. Open a record to extend its deadline, apply or release a legal hold, or review an individual case. Each change requires a reason and the current record version. Linked documents share the longest deadline. Releasing a hold does not change the minimum deadline. Review reports remain traceable and perform no physical deletion; that operational action is locked.

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: The CSV/ZIP export is a transport-neutral hand-off for booked foreign invoices. One ZIP contains the invoice header, supplier snapshot, all vehicle positions, a manifest and every verified original document.

docs.title: 2. Foreign-invoice workflow in FLEET Mira
docs.text:
1. Create the supplier and cost categories.
  2. Create an invoice draft with number/date, totals and payment details.
  3. Add one or more vehicle-linked cost/credit positions.
  4. Add received originals; the document vault uploads and verifies each hash.
  5. Resolve the gross/split difference to exactly zero cents.
  6. Verify and book the invoice.
  7. Export once or transfer through REST. Corrections use cancellation/credit, never edits to booked rows.
flowchart LR
    H[Invoice header] --> P[Vehicle positions]
    P --> D[Original documents]
    D --> V[Cloud verification]
    V --> C[Cent-accurate validation]
    C --> B[Booking]
    B --> Z[CSV/ZIP export]

docs.title: 3. Archive layout
docs.text:
Filename: Accounting_<document-number>_<invoice-id>.zip (filesystem-invalid characters are replaced).

manifest.json
invoice.csv
supplier.csv
positions.csv
documents/
  <document-id>_<original-file-name>

CSV is UTF-8 with BOM and semicolon delimiter. The first row contains stable field names. Line endings are CRLF. Values containing delimiter, quotes or line breaks are RFC-4180 quoted.

docs.title: 4. manifest.json
docs.text: Field Meaning format DLTNG-ACCOUNTING-EXPORT legacy contract token version export format version idempotency_key stable duplicate-prevention key invoice_id FLEET Mira invoice UUID documents[] ordered archive names of original documents

docs.title: 5. invoice.csv
docs.text:
Exactly one data row.

Field Meaning/function id immutable invoice UUID document_type INVOICE or CREDIT_NOTE correction_of_invoice_id linked corrected invoice, optional document_number supplier invoice/credit number document_date ISO document date delivery_date ISO performance/delivery date, optional delivery_note_number supplier delivery note, optional cost_center accounting cost centre, optional payable_until due date payment_term_days net payment term discount_term_days cash-discount term discount_rate_bp discount basis points net_cents declared invoice net amount tax_cents declared tax amount gross_cents calculated net + tax currency currently EUR status must be BOOKED booked_at_utc, booked_by booking evidence created_at_utc, updated_at_utc technical history description, note optional business text

docs.title: 6. supplier.csv
docs.text:
Exactly one snapshot row.

Field Meaning/function id supplier UUID supplier_number internal supplier number name supplier name creditor_number accounting creditor number street, postal_code, city, country postal address tax_id tax/VAT identifier phone, email validated contact data payment_term_days supplier default

The row is the current master snapshot at export time; the invoice ID and originals remain the audit anchor.

docs.title: 7. positions.csv
docs.text:
One row per active invoice position.

Field Meaning/function id position UUID invoice_id owning invoice UUID vehicle_id vehicle UUID vehicle_internal_number operational fleet number vehicle_registration registration snapshot vehicle_vin VIN snapshot cost_category_id, cost_category_code, cost_category_name cost classification entry_type COST or CREDIT description booking text valid_from, valid_to, document_date invoice date for invoice-bound positions net_cents, tax_cents, gross_cents cent amounts tax_rate_bp VAT basis points variable always true for invoice-bound positions note optional text

Signed comparison amount is cost positive and credit negative. For a credit-note header the comparison normalises the invoice sign so the displayed difference remains meaningful.

docs.title: 8. Original documents
docs.text: Only locally verified originals are included. Bytes must match the stored SHA-256; generated previews never replace XML or hybrid invoice originals. The ZIP itself is a delivery package, not the retention master. The local financial archive remains the evidence store; external backup is optional.

docs.title: 9. Validation rules
docs.text:
• gross_cents = net_cents + tax_cents;
  • signed sum of active position gross equals the invoice gross under document-type sign rules;
  • every position references exactly one vehicle;
  • every manifest document exists in documents/;
  • duplicate supplier/document number/date or identical document hash requires administrative override before booking;
  • only one successful export per idempotency key.

docs.title: 10. Audit and import guidance
docs.text: FLEET Mira audits export start/result, invoice, document IDs and correlation ID but not document content. Importers should validate manifest version, reject path traversal, process to a transaction/staging area, persist the idempotency key and return a reconciliation report containing invoice ID and target accounting ID.

docs.title: 11. Compatibility
docs.text: Consumers must ignore unknown additive columns. Required column removal, rename, type or sign change creates a new format version. The DLTNG-... format string remains a legacy technical identifier.

docs.title: 1. Scope
docs.text: FLEET Mira parses driver-card C files and vehicle-unit M files through one TachographImportService. The original compressed archive object remains the evidence source; parsed tables are replaceable derived data.

docs.title: 2. Import pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Archive ID] --> B[Read and verify GZIP/hash]
    B --> C[Classify binary content]
    C --> D[Parse C or M structure]
    D --> E[Verify certificates and signed sections]
    E --> F{Result}
    F -->|Valid| G[Atomically replace derived rows]
    F -->|Invalid/unverifiable| H[Persist quarantine results]
    F -->|Technical failure| I[Keep previous valid details]
    G --> J[Links, deadlines, UI cache invalidation]
    H --> J

Public integration points:

TachographImportService(db_path, logger).import_archive_id(archive_id)
DriverCardFullParser.parse_bytes(data)
VehicleUnitParser.parse(path)
DriverCardSignatureVerificationService.verify(parsed, trust_store, reference_time)
SignatureVerificationService.verify_sections(parsed, trust_store)

docs.title: 3. Classification
docs.text: Classification uses protocol/file identifiers in the binary content, never the filename alone. Result values are DRIVER_CARD, VEHICLE_UNIT and UNKNOWN. C/M filename prefixes are validated only for readout-date and plausibility functions.

docs.title: 4. Driver-card data
docs.text:
The C parser preserves block kind, application/file ID, generation, order, raw data bytes and following signature bytes. It maps identity, card validity, authorities, driving-licence number, activities, events, faults, vehicles and positions.

Important identity mapping:

Parser value Business use holder surname/first names person conflict check and display birth date optional person value card number/generation card link and C/M matching card issue/valid-from/expiry card record and expiry deadline driving-licence number/authority person licence data preferred language/country card metadata

No guessed values are generated from unrelated byte ranges. Text fields strip encoding indicators/control bytes and normalise whitespace without changing meaningful characters.

docs.title: 5. Vehicle-unit data
docs.text:
Supported download groups are G1 TREP 01–05, G2 v1 21–25 and G2 v2 31–35. Derived tables include overview/identity, card sessions, slot activities, events, faults, overspeed, second-by-second speed, technical/calibration records and position/border/loading data.

Unknown bounded optional records are retained as warnings. Invalid length/protocol sequences produce parse failure. Driver/workshop names use the same normalisation rules as C text.

docs.title: C files
docs.text:
• G1: EF.Card_Certificate, EF.CA_Certificate, RSA PKCS#1 and SHA-1 over exact data-block bytes.
  • G2/G2V2: Card_Sign, MSCA_Card, optional link certificate and ECDSA over exact signed EFs.

docs.title: M files
docs.text:
Every available signed VU download section is verified separately against the applicable ERCA/MSCA/VU chain. Trust and certificate validity use the best plausible signed file time, otherwise archive/download time with warning.

Overall priority: INVALID, then UNVERIFIABLE, then VALID. cryptography missing, signature/certificate missing or trust anchor missing produces UNVERIFIABLE, not VALID.

docs.title: 7. Parser and quarantine status
docs.text:
Status Meaning PARSED_VERIFIED parse and all required verification valid PARSED_VERIFIED_WITH_WARNINGS valid evidence with non-fatal parser warnings QUARANTINED_INVALID_SIGNATURE cryptographic invalidity QUARANTINED_UNVERIFIABLE required proof cannot be completed PARSE_ERROR structural/technical parse failure

Quarantine files remain visible/exportable but cannot create trusted person/vehicle links, contribute to combined C/M analysis or compliance snapshots.

docs.title: 8. C/M comparison
docs.text: The selected archive remains the base. Opposite-source intervals match by normalised card number, card generation and UTC overlap. A sweep-line comparison cuts only on interval boundaries. Valid overlapping data is shown as C and M available; one-sided coverage remains C-only or M-only. C data has priority only in the complete person-history view, never by modifying raw source rows.

docs.title: 9. Reprocessing and idempotency
docs.text: Archive hash prevents duplicate originals. Reprocessing writes new derived rows only after a successful parse/verification transaction. A failed reparse preserves the last valid details. Import, deletion, restore or reparse invalidates affected UI comparison caches.

docs.title: 10. Extending the parser
docs.text:
When adding a record type:

  1. document normative file/record identifiers and generation;
  2. validate lengths before reading;
  3. preserve source section/index and raw reference;
  4. keep UTC values unchanged;
  5. add fixture and malformed-length tests;
  6. add signature impact tests;
  7. update both language versions of this document and API schemas;
  8. never infer a business identity from an ambiguous value.

The older technical module and table names containing ddd or DLTNG remain compatibility identifiers.

docs.title: GPS-server.net integration
docs.text: The GPS-server.net integration is available in Pro and Enterprise. It exclusively uses the read-only User API 1.20. Basic has no telematics functionality.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
FLEET Mira synchronises GPS-server objects, current positions, location messages, routes, events and human-readable addresses. The IMEI is the external object identifier. Its link to a FLEET Mira vehicle is time-bound, so tracker replacements retain the correct historical assignment.

Vehicles are suggested first by a unique normalised VIN and then by a unique registration. An administrator confirms the assignment. Provider fields never update local vehicle master data automatically.

The vehicle record's Master data tab shows the latest reliable odometer reading with source and quality, plus the last known human-readable position using the signed-in user's regional format. Edit vehicle opens the same modal master-data form as the vehicle list. For an active assignment, Open telematics opens a dedicated workspace that is reused per vehicle.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Open Administration → Telematics → GPS-server.net. Additional telematics providers are added at the same level as separate subtabs.
  2. Enter a name, the actual HTTPS base URL, the GPS-server time zone and, optionally, the expected GPS-server username.
  3. Pro: enter the User API key. It is protected per user with Windows DPAPI outside the database.
  4. Enterprise: provision the User API key on the FleetMiraWorker server. PostgreSQL stores only the credential_ref.
  5. Test the connection and start the first synchronisation.
  6. Review the reconciliation list and assign every GPS-server object to a vehicle.
  7. Select sensor, GPS or unknown as the odometer type for each object when the API does not identify it unambiguously.

The base URL is never inferred from the key or hard-coded to a particular GPS-server host. FLEET Mira appends the User API path /api/api.php?api=user.

docs.title: Deleting a connection
docs.text: Select an existing connection and choose Delete. After explicit confirmation, FLEET Mira removes the connection together with synchronized objects, time-bound vehicle links, positions, events, coverage intervals and the GPS-server odometer readings projected from that evidence. Vehicle master records and the audit trail are retained. In Pro, the cleanup runs serially in the in-process worker and removes the user-protected API key. Enterprise enqueues an idempotent job; only FleetMiraWorker removes the PostgreSQL data and machine-protected key.

docs.title: Creating a vehicle from a GPS-server object
docs.text:
1. Run at least one object and position synchronisation.
  2. Select exactly one object under Administration → Telematics → GPS-server.net → Vehicle assignment.
  3. Choose Create vehicle from GPS-server object. The command is available both as a button and from the table row's context menu.
  4. Review and complete the internal number, registration, VIN, vehicle type, manufacturer and model.
  5. Save the record. FLEET Mira creates the vehicle, links the object for the configured initial backfill period (30 days by default), and reassigns stored positions, events and odometer observations within that period. A different earlier vehicle assignment is never overwritten.

Comma-separated message parameters are evaluated individually. If the latest position message contains a formally valid 17-character VIN in io256, it is prefilled as a provider observation. This never changes existing local vehicle master data. Differences between the object master and io256 are explicitly flagged for review. If a vehicle with the same VIN or registration already exists, use Assign selected object; FLEET Mira will not create a duplicate.

Look up manufacturer and model online is an optional one-off request. Only after confirmation is the VIN sent to the official US NHTSA vPIC service. The service focuses on vehicles intended for the US market, so European vehicles may return only manufacturer data or no reliable model. The result therefore remains an editable suggestion and requires administrative review before saving.

docs.title: Vehicle record and telematics workspace
docs.text:
The Telematics: [vehicle no.] – [registration] workspace contains:

  • Current location, with human-readable address, measurement time, live request and a native OpenStreetMap map,
  • Route history, with From/To selection and the last seven days as its default,
  • Positions, a combined evidence list for tachograph and telematics data,
  • Events from the synchronised telematics history.

Route history initially uses local data. Refresh displays that data immediately and only loads uncovered intervals in the background. After confirmation, Reload from provider bypasses the cache and is restricted to users with telematics.reconcile. Pro runs the request in its in-process worker; Enterprise only enqueues PostgreSQL jobs for FleetMiraWorker. Waypoints are stored immediately after the message request; optional route aggregation and larger geocoding batches do not block their display. The latest position is reverse-geocoded specifically. Telematics points are joined chronologically by straight segments. Gaps longer than 30 minutes are dashed; FLEET Mira neither road-snaps nor invents waypoints. Tachograph positions can be displayed as differently coloured reference markers but never form the route line. With more than 20,000 telematics points, the warning to narrow the period remains visible while the map still renders a chronological, database-side overview of at most 5,000 representative points, including the start and end. Sensor parameters are not loaded for this query. Technical zero coordinates and invalid values do not affect the map extent or route.

The vehicle record's Positions tab globally sorts tachograph and telematics evidence and provides a source filter. With Tachograph selected, Refresh only reloads the local database. With All or Telematics, it starts a targeted position catch-up for the assigned vehicle and selected period; Enterprise hands the same request to FleetMiraWorker. Retrieval and storage progress is visible in the global status bar. Evidence from different sources remains separate even when time and coordinates match. Without the licence feature or telematics.read, the list contains tachograph data only.

The GPS-server.net web interface is not embedded. GPS-server.net excludes embedding its map in its FAQ. FLEET Mira therefore uses locally synchronised data and the native map, preserving permissions, retention and Enterprise worker boundaries.

On the Enterprise worker server, the key is requested securely without a command-line argument or log output:

FLEET-Mira.exe --telematics-secret-action set --telematics-credential-ref "<connection-id>"

Use status to check provisioning and remove to delete the key. The Windows service does not need to be reinstalled afterwards.

docs.title: Synchronisation and odometers
docs.text:
Objects are synchronised daily. Current positions and position/event catch-up run every five minutes by default. Successful historical intervals, including empty responses, are registered as cache coverage. Repeated requests for completed periods therefore use only the database; mixed periods are reduced to their missing sections. The open end receives a two-minute overlap. Provider windows are at most 24 hours. Failed or partial responses are not marked as completely covered. The connector normalises both object responses and the seven-field position arrays returned by User API 1.20. History and date selection are limited to the local start of day 28 days ago through the current time.

In Pro, the Qt timer triggers one serialised in-process worker thread and immediately returns control to the UI. HTTPS requests, retries and larger history imports therefore run in neither the sign-in thread nor the UI thread. Periodic and manually requested telematics operations in the same Pro installation share one execution lock. Position messages are stored in backend-neutral transactions of 500 records rather than opening and committing a database connection for every waypoint. Normal application shutdown waits for the active pass in a controlled manner.

Pro uses exactly one telematics writer because additional SQLite worker processes would increase write locking and API load. Enterprise executes this work exclusively in the separate FleetMiraWorker. Its PostgreSQL queue supports leases and multiple worker instances, but one instance remains the recommended GPS-server.net setup. Horizontal scaling only becomes useful when jobs are partitioned by connection and provider limits are observed.

The last real odometer value before local midnight is projected as the daily value when it is no more than 24 hours old. FLEET Mira does not interpolate values. Raw observations within one day are compacted into a candidate containing the latest value and measurement time, count, minimum and maximum. A newly received real sensor observation is already shown with warning status in the vehicle record until regular daily projection and validation have run. For Teltonika data, the connector recognises the GPS-server odometer including the corresponding io389 (kilometres) and io16 (metres) parameters. Priority is:

  1. signed M midnight reading,
  2. approved manual reading,
  3. GPS-server sensor reading,
  4. C-file reading,
  5. GPS-server GPS reading,
  6. unknown telematics source.

GPS-server readings are not signed M events. Decreasing values and implausible daily distances are marked as conflicts.

docs.title: Enterprise webhook
docs.text:
Enterprise can receive events through this TLS-protected reverse-proxy path:

/api/telematics/webhooks/{connection_id}/gps-server/{secret-token}

The endpoint accepts GET and application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST. A secret URL token, the expected GPS-server username and an optional IP allowlist protect it because GPS-server does not document a webhook signature. Conflicting GET and POST values are rejected.

The webhook only acknowledges receipt and queues an API catch-up job. Positions and odometer values are subsequently confirmed through the User API. Raw webhook payloads are deleted after 30 days.

docs.title: Security and operations
docs.text:
• Use only a User API key, never a user password or Server API key.
  • API keys, complete URLs and query strings must never be logged.
  • Outbound HTTPS connections use the native Windows certificate store. Certificate and hostname verification remain enabled; the Windows Chain Engine can securely complete an incomplete server chain.
  • Restrict production keys to the worker IP where possible.
  • Detailed positions are retained for a fixed 28 days from the local start of day. Each object's latest known state, daily odometer readings, events and audit data are retained. Sensor parameters remain losslessly available as compressed zlib-json-v1 during the detail period.
  • ACTION_REQUIRED indicates key, permission, certificate or response-format problems. DEGRADED indicates temporary network or server failures.
  • If Address is being resolved remains visible, inspect the latest telematics_geocode_position run. Depending on the GPS-server installation, GET_ADDRESS can return JSON or plain text; both formats are supported.
  • Remote commands, Location API, Server API, media and the device protocol are outside this integration.

docs.title: FleetMiraApi: operations and administration
docs.text: Source implementation dated 2026-11-05, version 1.1.0-beta9. This page describes the new implementation. Passing source tests does not replace installed service/upgrade acceptance or sign-in on an Android device.

docs.title: Components and prerequisites
docs.text:
FleetMiraApi is an independent Windows service using NT SERVICE\FleetMiraApi. It requires a regular Enterprise installation and PostgreSQL. SQLite fallback is prohibited. The API process runs no WorkerRuntime. FleetMiraWorker continues to process central uploads, imports, fleet reads and other background jobs; it no longer opens API listeners in Enterprise. Basic/Pro retain their existing SQLite/desktop composition.

API, worker and PostgreSQL can initially share a server. Distributing them across hosts additionally requires shared, appropriately protected mobile intake storage and the necessary portal/certificate files. Co-location creates no special runtime mode. The API reads the central licence entitlement; the worker retains the licence key and activation/verification loop.

For unattended installations, exit code 10 means a required configuration, permissions or service-start step failed after copying the files. The installation is not operational. Inspect protected setup/service logs and Windows service status, correct the cause and rerun setup. Setup protects intake and log directories for administrators, SYSTEM and the service account. Existing files and subdirectories retain working inheritance rules. Permission errors are not ignored as successful steps.

docs.title: Setup and migration
docs.text:
1. Back up the database and configuration using the existing operational procedure before updating. Include the Enterprise installer's api component. The Worker setup type includes the API service, which remains separately selectable.
  2. Run regular versioned schema migration with the maintenance account. New tables use api_service_ and api_oauth_ prefixes. Runtime accounts receive no additional DDL privileges.
  3. Provision the certificate chain and private key on the API host. Only administrators and the service account need private-key access. Devices must trust the issuing CA. Certificate verification is not disabled.
  4. In the Enterprise client, under Administration → Communication and integrations, open API service, API configuration, API credentials and Logs. Current users.manage and settings.manage permissions are required.
  5. Enter the HTTPS public URL, bind address, port and server certificate/key paths. The public hostname must be trusted. Review log limits and permitted Android scopes, save, then Reload the relevant service instance.
  6. Configure DNS and firewall for the explicitly selected HTTPS port. No public firewall rule is created automatically. Forwarded headers cannot replace an actual TLS connection.

Without central configuration, the service adopts existing enabled config/mobile-api.json and config/telematics-api.json once. A certificate, key and explicit hostname are required. Additional existing listeners retain their ports as legacy_listeners. Existing mobile DNS-SD configuration is adopted. Original files and tokens are neither deleted nor overwritten. Central configuration takes precedence after adoption. Without valid configuration the service remains UNCONFIGURED and opens no listener.

During upgrades, setup also stops an API service already bound to its own application directory. Foreign service image paths are rejected. Changes and restarts remain subject to normal operational maintenance. Stop the new API service before rolling back to an older worker, which could otherwise create duplicate listeners. Check database/version compatibility separately before rollback.

docs.title: Endpoints and credentials
docs.text:
The service composes existing controllers at their existing paths: /api/mobile/v1/, /api/devices, /api/dashboard/devices, /api/telematics/, /api/drivercard/ and, when configured, /traffic-offences/. Accounting export remains an outgoing worker request. The archive service stays independent.

The desktop's local driver API retains its loopback and session-token restrictions. Central driver access instead uses the separate drivercard audience with drivercard.read and drivercard.parse. It requires explicit global access and never claims to enforce unsupported customer restrictions. Mobile, device, telematics and driver tokens are not interchangeable.

In API credentials, choose a user, label, audience, scopes and a validity of 1–365 days. Device credentials require explicit customer assignments or global customer access. Telematics and central driver access require global access. Mobile credentials have no customer restriction. Current user permissions are checked during issuance and each request. The plaintext token appears once and is not stored in the database. Transfer it securely to a technical integration; requests use Authorization: Bearer <token> over HTTPS.

Revocation requires confirmation and remains available after licence expiry. The database stores credential metadata and hashes, never bearer secrets. The list and audit events identify the owner, grants and validity.

docs.title: DTCO Android browser sign-in
docs.text:
The public client is dtco-android, with the exactly registered redirect de.eh.dtco:/oauth/callback. Save a Fleet Mira server target in Android, then select Sign in to Fleet Mira. An Android Custom Tab displays the server's HTTPS sign-in page. This implementation authenticates existing local Fleet Mira accounts. Existing desktop SSO providers do not thereby become web SSO providers; that requires separate web registrations and a verified server-side broker.

Endpoints are GET/POST /oauth/authorize, POST /oauth/token, POST /oauth/revoke and GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server. Only Authorization Code with S256 PKCE and Refresh Token are supported; no password grant or embedded client secret. The browser form is bound to a short-lived secure HttpOnly/SameSite cookie. PKCE requests/forms expire after five minutes; single-use codes expire after 60 seconds.

Access tokens last 15 minutes; the overall app session lasts at most 30 days. Refresh tokens rotate on use; proven reuse of an old refresh token revokes the entire session. The mobile credential ID remains stable across refresh so upload receipts and pending jobs retain ownership. Android Keystore protects tokens and the temporary PKCE proof. Refresh preserves offline account binding; new sign-in explicitly renews it. The app verifies redirect, state and stored target before accepting tokens.

Scopes are limited by client grants and current user permissions. Password changes, account locks, disabled local login, session expiry and revocation block the app session. Individual phones appear as separate mobile credentials and can be revoked independently. Manually provisioned integration tokens remain supported. Additional iOS clients require explicit separate client/redirect registrations; no iOS app is implemented here.

docs.title: Logs and diagnostics
docs.text:
logs/api/api.jsonl contains structured UTF-8/UTC diagnostics with request ID, endpoint family, HTTP status and processing duration. URL secrets, query strings, payloads, passwords and tokens are never logged. The central host suppresses legacy parser diagnostics containing card/file details. Technical failures contain exception types and stack locations without exception content or local variables.

Defaults: rotate daily and at 50 MiB, retain at most 30 days, total budget 1024 MiB. The budget must accommodate at least two maximum-size files. Debug mode expires automatically after 15 minutes. Log write failures are visible in service diagnostics. Audit events remain separate in the database; log rotation does not delete them.

The logs workspace provides search, severity filtering, optional automatic refresh and export of visible sanitized JSONL rows. A read request returns at most 64 KiB/200 lines. Temporary database log responses expire after five minutes; completed other control requests after seven days. Requests interrupted during process termination become UNKNOWN and are not replayed automatically.

API service displays node heartbeat, listener state, licence/maintenance availability, log availability. Diagnose, pause, resume, debug and reload use short-lived PostgreSQL control requests that recheck current administrator rights. PostgreSQL/restore maintenance blocks business access. Pause leaves token revocation available. GET /health/live publicly confirms process response only. Browser requests to /health open Fleet Mira Health without sign-in, in English and dark Material 3 by default. The overview shows API, worker and database state, worker jobs and resource measurements with source and time. Sanitized logs remain restricted to active local Mira administrators with users.manage and settings.manage. See the illustrated setup guide.

docs.title: Local recovery
docs.text:
The FLEET Mira API shortcut launches DLTNGDownloadTool.exe --api-console. It can inspect Windows service state and protected local logs without a database/API connection. Start/stop are subject to Windows SCM permissions; run as administrator when needed. Before application authentication, the console uses English.

The installed executable also supports --api-service install|remove|start|stop|query|run|console. run is the SCM entry point; console is the interactive diagnostic host. Do not run both for the same host. Service installation/removal and start/stop require Windows administrator rights. remove deletes the service, not business data, logs or tokens. A database advisory lock prevents competing API hosts on the same machine. Shutdown stops acceptance and waits a bounded time for HTTP work; if the deadline is exceeded the SCM host exits with an error for recovery.

Fleet Mira Health at /health is public, English and dark by default. Worker job summaries and resource measurements are public; logs remain administrator-only. Setup and measurement limits: FleetMiraApi service.

docs.title: 1. Scope and responsibility
docs.text:
FLEET Mira archives tachograph data and financial documents locally before performing any backup. The local primary archive is authoritative; an external backup is optional and does not enable business functions.

  • archive_dir contains immutable compressed tachograph originals.
  • financial_archive_dir contains originals and manifests for supplier invoices and e-invoices.
  • document_archive beside the database contains originals and manifests for personnel and vehicle records.
  • SQLite stores metadata, relationships, statuses and audit data.
  • A backup target contains only downstream verified replicas and database snapshots.

Import, display, analysis, verification, booking and export remain fully available without a backup target. Remote changes are never synchronised automatically into the local primary archive.

docs.title: 2. Primary archive and backup layout
docs.text:
The local primary archives use separate configurable paths:

archive_dir/
  YYYY/MM/<archive-id>.ddd.gz

financial_archive_dir/
  YYYY/<invoice-id>/<document-id>/
    original.<ext>
    manifest.json

An optional backup target continues to use the compatible prefix:

DLTNG/<installation-id>/
  archives/YYYY/MM/<archive-id>.ddd.gz[.enc]
  financial-documents/YYYY/<invoice-id>/<document-id>_<sha256>.<ext>[.enc]
  documents/YYYY/<person|vehicle>/<record-id>/<document-id>_<sha256>.<ext>[.enc]
  manifests/...
  database/YYYY/MM/archive_YYYY-MM-DD_HHmmssZ.db.gz[.enc]

DLTNG is not renamed so existing objects remain reachable. The primary archive and backup target must not resolve to the same path.

docs.title: 3. Status model
docs.text:
Archive status and backup status are independent.

Archive status Meaning STAGING local storage has not yet been confirmed LOCAL_VERIFIED the local original was fully read back and SHA-256 verified LOCAL_MISSING the expected local original is missing LOCAL_CORRUPT local size or checksum does not match REMOVED_AFTER_RETENTION an administrator removed the original after retention review Backup status Meaning NOT_CONFIGURED no active target; not a business error PENDING a durable backup job exists UPLOADING transfer is active VERIFIED the backup object was fully read back and verified FAILED a retryable failure was recorded REMOTE_MISSING a previously verified backup object is missing

LOCAL_VERIFIED is the prerequisite for business functions. backup_status describes only the additional copy.

docs.title: 4. Archiving and backup flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Import: DDD, supplier document or e-invoice"] --> B{"Document type"}

    B -->|"Tachograph data"| C["Compress DDD locally and calculate original/stored hashes"]
    B -->|"Supplier invoice"| D["Store original in the local financial archive"]
    B -->|"XRechnung"| E["Prepare original, structured XML and validation report"]

    C --> F["Read back and verify local file and manifest"]
    D --> F
    E --> F

    F --> G{"Local verification successful?"}
    G -->|"No"| H["Abort import, clean temporary objects and audit the error"]
    G -->|"Yes"| I["Commit metadata, relationships and audit to SQLite"]

    I --> J["Status LOCAL_VERIFIED"]
    J --> K["Display, analysis, verification, booking and export available"]
    J --> L{"External backup configured?"}

    L -->|"No"| M["Complete local operation"]
    L -->|"Yes"| N["Persist backup job"]
    N --> O["Optionally encrypt and transfer to target"]
    O --> P["Read back complete backup and verify hash"]
    P --> Q{"Backup verification successful?"}
    Q -->|"Yes"| R["Backup status VERIFIED and audit"]
    Q -->|"No"| S["Backup status FAILED and automatic retry"]

    S --> K
    R --> K
  1. Every import is archived locally first.
  2. DDD files retain their GZIP layout; financial and e-invoice documents receive an original and manifest in the financial archive.
  3. Only successful local read-back and hash verification produces LOCAL_VERIFIED.
  4. LOCAL_VERIFIED enables every business function.
  5. Without a backup target, the workflow completes successfully in local mode.
  6. With a target, an additional copy is created asynchronously.
  7. Backup failures change only backup status and do not block locally verified documents.
  8. Local originals are not deleted after successful backup.
  9. A verified backup can restore the local primary archive after loss or corruption.

docs.title: Tachograph data
docs.text: DDD files are compressed locally under archive_dir. Original and stored hashes, archive ID, source and audit are stored in SQLite. Search, analysis, export and logical deletion work without a backup target. The existing layout is not migrated.

docs.title: Supplier invoices
docs.text: Original documents are stored atomically with a manifest under financial_archive_dir and read back. Verification, booking, preview and accounting export require a locally verified original rather than a cloud object. Retention and legal hold apply to the local original and manifest.

docs.title: XML XRechnung and hybrid PDF
docs.text: Import prepares the received original, embedded XML for a hybrid PDF, and validation report as one unit. Invoice, lines, allocations and document relationships are committed only after every required object is locally verified. Failure removes temporary objects and leaves no partial invoice.

docs.title: Target-independent Quick Backup
docs.text:
Basic and Pro open a wizard under Administration → Backups → Quick Backup. Database only retains the local diagnostic ZIP containing archive.db and its SHA-256 manifest. Complete manual backup also includes every active DDD, financial and record-document object referenced by that snapshot, including their manifests. Output can be a portable ZIP64 file or a versioned backup directory.

The manual wizard writes only to a local or UNC path and creates no configured target, durable queue or retention job. Optional AES-256-GCM encryption requires the recovery key to be exported separately before backup starts. Both formats are fully read back and can be opened through Restore …; incomplete sets and checksum failures are rejected. See the Backup and restore how-to for the complete procedure.

Exactly one active target can be configured under Administration → Backups:

  • LOCAL_FILESYSTEM: a second local drive or UNC/NAS share;
  • HTTPS WebDAV;
  • Google Drive.

The wizard tests availability, write access, upload, complete read-back and SHA-256. A LOCAL_FILESYSTEM target must be physically or administratively separate from the primary archive. HTTP WebDAV is rejected. Google Drive uses drive.file; OAuth tokens are DPAPI-protected.

Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption is a backup-target property. The local primary archive is protected through Windows, volume and filesystem controls. An exported recovery key must be stored separately and offline.

docs.title: 7. Optional backup and retry
docs.text:
After LOCAL_VERIFIED, an active target receives a durable job. The object is optionally encrypted, transferred, fully read back and checked. Only then is backup status VERIFIED.

Retries occur after 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes and then no more often than every six hours. A restart resumes pending jobs. Different content under the same object ID is a conflict and is not overwritten.

The task option Wait for external backup before deleting at source defers tachograph mark_processed and terminal deletion until VERIFIED. It is disabled without an active target. In standard mode, local archiving completes the download and backup follows asynchronously.

docs.title: 8. Database snapshots
docs.text:
Snapshots run daily at 02:00 UTC by default:

  1. create a consistent file through the SQLite Backup API;
  2. run PRAGMA integrity_check;
  3. calculate SHA-256 and GZIP compress;
  4. optionally encrypt;
  5. transfer to the active filesystem, WebDAV or Google Drive target and read it back.

Retention keeps 30 daily snapshots and one monthly snapshot for 12 months. Only expired database snapshots are deleted automatically, never DDD or financial archive objects.

docs.title: 9. Migrate existing cloud documents
docs.text:
Existing documents without a local original are migrated automatically and resumably:

  1. adopt existing spool files after checking stored SHA-256;
  2. download and, where necessary, decrypt remote-only originals;
  3. verify size and original hash;
  4. atomically store original and manifest under financial_archive_dir;
  5. set LOCAL_VERIFIED and audit the migration.

Failures become visible as LOCAL_MISSING or LOCAL_CORRUPT. Legacy documents remain remotely readable until migration; business processing requires successful local adoption. Administration shows total, migrated, pending and failed counts.

docs.title: 10. Restore one object
docs.text:
1. Select the object and a verified backup.
  2. Confirm administrative permission and required reason.
  3. Read the backup into a temporary file.
  4. Verify backup hash, decrypt where necessary and verify the original hash.
  5. Atomically move it into the expected local primary archive.
  6. Fully read and verify the restored local object.
  7. Only then reconcile archive and backup statuses and audit the restore.

Failure leaves existing local objects unchanged and removes partial files. A logically deleted business row is not reactivated automatically.

docs.title: 11. Database restore
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Select snapshot"] --> B["Read temporarily from backup target"]
    B --> C["Verify hash, decrypt and decompress"]
    C --> D["SQLite integrity_check"]
    D --> E["Stop schedulers and writers"]
    E --> F["Create safety copy of current DB"]
    F --> G["Atomically replace database"]
    G --> H["Restart application and run migrations"]
    H --> I["Reconcile primary archives and backup status"]

Database replacement is staged for restart if the live connection cannot be closed safely. Before writing the startup marker, Mira also checks every DDD, record, financial, and manifest reference. Missing or damaged archive objects are displayed together. With backup.restore, collective confirmation, and a mandatory reason, the consistent database can still be restored; references are normalised to safe portable target paths and remain visible as requiring repair. Readable damaged files are copied unchanged to quarantine. A failed database check never creates a replacement request.

During an Enterprise restore, mira_restore terminates only normal application and worker sessions for the controlled PostgreSQL cutover. Active DBA or superuser sessions are never terminated automatically. The administrator must close them before final approval; otherwise the cutover stops without data loss.

docs.title: 12. Full disaster recovery
docs.text:
1. Install a compatible FLEET Mira version in isolation.
  2. Configure the backup target without starting normal imports.
  3. Supply the recovery key where necessary.
  4. Restore and verify the database snapshot.
  5. Reconstruct the DDD and financial primary archives from manifests.
  6. Verify all compressed/decompressed DDD hashes and document SHA-256 values.
  7. Reconcile database relationships, local archive status, backup status, retention and audit.
  8. Test representative C/M analysis, sign-in, supplier invoice and XRechnung workflows.
  9. Document approval before production cutover.

docs.title: 13. Target change, permissions and audit
docs.text:
A target cannot be deleted while retained objects reference it. Target change copies, reads back and verifies objects; references change only after success. Keep the old target until the reconciliation report is approved.

  • backup.read: read status;
  • backup.run: retry and verify jobs;
  • backup.manage: manage targets and encryption;
  • backup.restore: restore objects.

Target changes, connection tests, key-export confirmations, failures, snapshots, retention deletion, migration and restore are audited without secrets, tokens or keys.

docs.title: 14. Operational checklist
docs.text:
• daily: primary archive availability and free space, local integrity errors, backup backlog and latest database snapshot;
  • weekly: target availability, quota, authentication and random hash verification;
  • monthly: database retention, financial archive completeness and migration progress;
  • quarterly: isolated restore of database, DDD archive and financial archive;
  • after path, credential, target or version changes: connection test and immediate snapshot;
  • incident: preserve logs and audit and do not overwrite the last known-good database.

These mechanisms support integrity, traceability and retention. Formal GoBD compliance additionally depends on operations, permissions and procedural documentation.

docs.title: Two different backup responsibilities
docs.text:
Scope Contents Purpose Tenant backup PostgreSQL customer database, manifest and bound DDD, finance and record archives Controlled restore of one specific customer Platform protection Control database, all customer backups, role/configuration mapping, protected keys, certificates and service configuration Rebuild the entire platform after server loss

A tenant backup does not replace control-database backup. A SQL dump alone does not contain all original files or machine-bound secrets. Conversely, a file copy does not replace a consistent PostgreSQL backup.

Enterprise uses PostgreSQL exclusively. The client configures backups and enqueues requests; FleetMiraWorker performs backup, upload, verification, retention and restore. No local SQLite snapshot service is started.

docs.title: Configure tenant backup
docs.text:
1. Open the correct customer and verify its identity.
  2. Open Administration → Backups. With appropriate backup privileges, select a filesystem/UNC, HTTPS WebDAV or Google Drive destination according to approved configuration.
  3. Use a dedicated destination/object directory for the encryption key. Do not overwrite existing directories with a new key.
  4. Export the recovery key during setup and store it separately offline. Losing the key can prevent recovery.
  5. Run upload/read-back tests, request a manual backup and verify its completion.
  6. Set schedule and retention for your recovery objectives. Defaults are daily at 02:00 server time and 14 daily, 8 weekly and 12 monthly copies.

A backup set includes a PostgreSQL custom dump, versioned manifest, commit marker and SHA-256 referenced archives. VERIFIED means complete upload, read-back, decryption and verification. A started job or an existing filename is not a verified backup. Google Drive is one-way backup, not synchronization.

docs.title: Restore a tenant safely
docs.text:
1. Verify target customer and a verified backup. Plan a maintenance window, owner and rollback; separately back up the currently reachable state.
  2. Enter the required reason and select Prepare restore. The worker checks the dump/files and builds a staging database.
  3. Schema, tables and archive references are verified. READY_FOR_APPROVAL is not a switch. READY_FOR_APPROVAL_WITH_WARNINGS requires deliberate review of missing or damaged archive components; a corrupt dump remains a hard failure.
  4. A user with backup.restore selects Approve production switch. Archive warnings require additional explicit confirmation and a mandatory reason.
  5. The worker switches under maintenance control. Previous database leases are revoked; the preceding database remains available for rollback. Other tenants must not be rebound to this data.
  6. Sign in again and verify customer identity, data, documents, a worker job and licensing. Create and verify a new backup.

Archives are verified and replaced atomically below the bound data root. Old absolute file paths from a backup are not trusted restore targets. On failure, inspect rollback and integrity status; do not simply mark the job successful. The preceding database is retained for seven days by default.

docs.title: Protect the entire platform
docs.text:
Keep administrative backups and separately protected operating records for:

  • a consistent control database and versioned tenant, user and membership mappings;
  • customer databases and their corresponding verified file archives;
  • PostgreSQL roles and required privilege mappings;
  • protected worker licensing/backup keys, recovery keys and integration secrets;
  • server configuration, trusted provisioning policy, certificates and private TLS keys;
  • service identities, local/UNC permissions and required external configuration.

DPAPI-protected files are machine-bound. Copying them to another computer does not replace supported key export/import or secret re-provisioning. A verified database backup does not prove full recovery on another host. PITR/WAL archiving is outside the described beta workflow.

docs.title: Recovery and regular rehearsal
docs.text:
After server loss, rebuild trusted infrastructure, identities and keys first; then restore the control database and map its matching customer backups consistently. Stop the old worker before replacement-server transfer and explicitly perform license transfer. Do not automatically merge other customers or identically named users.

Rehearse only in an explicitly authorized isolated environment. Verify restored data, archives, memberships, customer isolation and actually executed jobs. Avoid accidental production effects from external integrations. Customer-specific WebDAV/Drive, UNC/gMSA and network failures require operational acceptance.

docs.title: Install and configure Enterprise
docs.text: This guide applies to beta9 R3. Enterprise uses PostgreSQL and central identity management. Use only the Enterprise package on Windows Server, RDP and Citrix systems.

docs.title: 1. Plan topology and requirements
docs.text:
All-in-one server: PostgreSQL, API, worker, archive service and provisioning service run on the same Windows server. A client can run in a user session there. There is no special combined runtime mode.

Distributed installation: Clients run on separate computers; server services remain independent components. Plan reachable database endpoints and server-bound file archives. The provisioning service belongs to the trusted server context; clients receive no administrative passwords.

Decide before starting:

  • 64-bit Windows and local administrative installation rights; size resources for customer count, archive volume and concurrency.
  • A stable HTTPS address such as https://fleet.example.internal:8443, with a matching certificate SAN. Private keys stay on the server.
  • PostgreSQL data on a local fixed NTFS volume, not a network drive or user profile.
  • Separate protected customer data/archive roots and backup destinations outside the running system.
  • Firewall access: HTTPS from clients to the API host; PostgreSQL only for authorized hosts. Do not publicly expose the database, service control or provisioning named pipe.
  • For remote PostgreSQL connections, configure TLS according to operational policy with verified certificate chain and host identity.

docs.title: 2. Verify files and existing installations
docs.text:
Download installers and checksums, compare SHA-256 and observe beta status. Before updating, stop client access and create verified database, archive, configuration and key backups. An existing customer database must never automatically become the control database.

Existing-installation conversion is maintenance

The server setup below creates a new platform. Existing single-customer installations require explicitly planned conversion with verified backup and rollback. A copy or matching username does not authorize identity merging.

docs.title: 3. Install PostgreSQL
docs.text:
1. Run the PostgreSQL server installer elevated.
  2. Configure local storage, port and the required database passwords. Keep passwords separately protected.
  3. The default local Windows service account is mira_postgres. A custom permitted account name must be unused for a fresh installation; existing accounts are not adopted or reset.
  4. Complete installation and check postgresql-x64-mira.

The database and Enterprise installers are separate packages. An existing PostgreSQL service name alone does not establish a suitable empty target platform.

docs.title: 4. Configure a new platform
docs.text:
Unattended setup reads a protected INI through /MIRACONFIG. This example shows structure only, not usable credentials:

[tenant_server]
Host=127.0.0.1
Port=5432
SetupUser=postgres
SetupPassword=<enter-locally>
AdministratorPassword=<strong-personal-password>
PublicUrl=https://fleet.example.internal:8443
Bind=0.0.0.0
Certificate=C:\FleetMiraSetup\server.pem
PrivateKey=C:\FleetMiraSetup\server-key.pem

Do not put the INI or TLS key in Git, email or shared download folders. The setup INI must be owned by SYSTEM or the built-in Administrators group and grant access only to those identities. An additional individual administrator ACE is rejected too.

The standalone permission routine audits without changes by default. Run elevated:

.\protect_enterprise_setup_inputs.ps1 -LiteralPath C:\FleetMiraSetup\enterprise.ini -Mode Audit
.\protect_enterprise_setup_inputs.ps1 -LiteralPath C:\FleetMiraSetup\enterprise.ini -Mode Protect -BackupManifest C:\FleetMiraSetup\acl-before.json -RequireCompliant

BackupManifest must be new. The routine changes permissions, not file contents; -Mode Restore with the same manifest restores saved permissions for exactly the same files. Protect the manifest itself. Protect TLS files and other setup inputs according to their actual secrets.

docs.title: 5. Install Enterprise components
docs.text:
1. Run the Enterprise installer elevated. On the server select the client if required, Fleet Mira Worker Windows service and Fleet Mira API Windows service.
  2. Supply the complete protected file for a new platform. Example:
.\FLEET-Mira-Enterprise-1.1.0-beta9-Setup-x64.exe /TYPE=custom /COMPONENTS=client,worker,api /MIRACONFIG="C:\FleetMiraSetup\enterprise.ini"
  1. Wait for successful completion. Setup creates a separate control database and the first central administrator. Customers are provisioned explicitly afterwards.
  2. Check FleetMiraApi, FleetMiraWorker, FleetMiraArchive, FleetMiraProvisioner and PostgreSQL. API, worker and archive use their own restricted service identities. The local provisioning service runs as SYSTEM for explicitly authorized maintenance.
